```jsonc
                "steps":7,"last_tool":{"id":"toolu_…","name":"Bash","summary":"running the tests"},   // tool calls made, the latest one (what it does now; summary in the request's language, like a workflow agent's latest_tool); updated_at is its last message's time, not the file's mtime
                "model":"claude-haiku-4-5-…","tokens":23456}],   // the model it ran on, its latest reply's in its own transcript (never <synthetic>), not the one its Agent call asked for; tokens is its latest reply's context + output tokens, as a workflow agent's. Each absent until it has replied; old nodes don't have them. sessions.changed goes out when its running, steps, last_tool or updated_at change; these ride along
 "loop":{"kind":"wakeup|cron","prompt":"/loop …","reason":"…","interval_seconds":1800,"next_at":"...","cron":"*/5 * * * *","ticks":12},
 "goal":{"objective":"…","status":"active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete","reason":"…",   // the goal it's working on
        "tokens_used":12345,"token_budget":500000,"seconds":600,"updated_at":"..."},                              // absent when there is no goal
 "plan":{"done":3,"total":5,"current":"Reproducing the crash in landscape","at":"..."},   // the agent's own task list (Claude Code's TodoWrite / TaskCreate / TaskUpdate): done of total items completed, current = the item in progress (its activeForm, else its subject; one line, at most 120 characters; absent when none is), at = when these last changed. Absent when it keeps no list, and for Codex and runtimes. Old nodes don't have this field
 // TCP ports the Agent's processes listen on that answer HTTP: one entry per port; title is its home page's <title> (absent if none). Old nodes don't have this field
 "ports":[{"port":5173,"addr":"127.0.0.1","pid":4242,"process":"node","title":"Vite + React"}],
 // Linked unfinished to-do: only present while currently linked (not released) and the to-do is unfinished; filled in by the hub
 "todo":{"id":"todo_…","title":"Ship version 1.3 of the weather App"},
 "quiet":true,   // an Agent working (or that worked) on a quiet task: kept out of task notifications and the global badge, and stays set after the task is done
 "background":[{"id":"b85polnoj","kind":"shell|agent|monitor|workflow","description":"…","command":"…",   // background commands / subagents / Monitors / workflows that haven't reported back yet
                "output_file":"/private/tmp/…/b85polnoj.output","started_at":"...",
                "expires_at":"...",          // Monitor: stops by itself at this time (the "expires in 30m" in the result); absent if not stated
                "run_id":"wf_c1d9daf8-cd2"}], // workflow: which run in workflows it is; only running workflows are here (old clients still treat it as a background task)
 "background_ended":[{"id":"b85polnoj","kind":"shell|agent|monitor|workflow","description":"…","command":"…", // recent ended outcomes, oldest first, at most 8 and from the last day
                      "output_file":"/private/tmp/…/b85polnoj.output","started_at":"...","ended_at":"...",
                      "status":"completed|failed|stopped|killed|ended","exit_code":0}], // exit_code only when the transcript states it; stopped work need not have one
 // Full session info only; bounded / summary list rows omit background_ended. Older nodes and hubs omit it: clients must not infer an outcome when a task only leaves background.
 // Claude Code subagents and workflows use their own history fields. Ended entries never count as running background work.
 // Claude Code workflows (multi-agent scripts the Workflow tool runs in the background, docs/protocol/agent-states.md "Background workflows"): the last day's, newest first.
 // Running ones (running=true) count as background work: the hub computes state as working, doesn't push "done", doesn't judge the to-do complete or auto-close this Agent. Old nodes don't have this field
 // phase_stats follows phases order, including phases with no agents yet, then appends undeclared phases; title="" means unknown. done counts journal results only; failed counts the journal's failed lines (omitted when 0); agents stopped when the run ended are in none of done / failed / running.
 // A retried agent (Claude Code's workflow view starts the same call again: the journal's same key, a new agentId) counts once, as its latest attempt: the attempts it replaced are in no count, phase_stats or agents, only in tokens / calls.
 // Each agent's tokens is the latest assistant usage's input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens, not a cumulative total. Claude Code's own error replies (model <synthetic> / isApiErrorMessage, usage all zeros), usage whose input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens is 0 (a gateway's on a turn's other replies, whatever its output_tokens) and a gateway's whole-turn sum (over transcript.PlausibleContext) are skipped: the last real one stands.
 // calls counts tool_use / server_tool_use, deduplicated by nonempty tool_use_id; latest_tool keeps the last tool even after the final reply. latest_tool.summary is a short line on what the call does, in the request's language (the node writes it in Chinese and the hub rewrites it, like activity). Clients retain their existing display when these fields are absent.
 // Pushes: sessions.changed goes out when a workflow's status, phase, any of its agent counts, or a listed agent's latest_tool name / calls change, at most as often as node rereads workflows (1.5 s); tokens, last_text and the rest ride along with those pushes.
 "workflows":[{"task_id":"wdp5zxh37","run_id":"wf_c1d9daf8-cd2","name":"parity-audit","summary":"…",
               "status":"running|completed|failed|killed|stalled","running":true,   // stalled: no end notification, but no activity for 30 minutes (its claude is gone); not counted as running
               "phases":["Audit","Verify"],"phase":"Verify","phase_index":2,"phase_count":2,   // phases from the script's meta; phase is the phase of the most recently started agent still running, phase_index counts from 1, 0 = unknown
               "phase_stats":[{"title":"Audit","started":180,"done":167,"failed":2,"running":11},{"title":"Verify","started":5,"done":0,"running":5}], // per-phase counts across all agents, unaffected by the 60-agent response limit
               "tool_use_id":"toolu_…",                                            // the Workflow call that started it
               "agents_started":185,"agents_done":167,"agents_failed":2,"agents_running":16, // the total is known only once finished (the script dispatches as it runs): show "done / started"; agents_failed only when > 0
               "tokens":123400,"calls":420,                                    // sums across all agents, before truncation; tokens is not cumulative consumption
               "started_at":"...","ended_at":"...","updated_at":"...",           // ended_at only once finished; duration = (ended_at or now) - started_at
               "error":"Error: Workflow aborted",                                 // first line for failed / killed
               "agents":[{"id":"a55ab0b9…","session_id":"<id>@a55ab0b9…","label":"audit:chat-rich","phase":"Audit",   // in start order, at most 60 (newest kept)
                          "running":false,"status":"running|done|failed|stopped",   // failed: the journal says it failed (an API error ended it); stopped: it hadn't come back when the run ended
                          "started_at":"...","ended_at":"...","updated_at":"...","last_text":"…", // ended_at is absent while running; done and failed agents use the last exchange time (file mtime as fallback), stopped agents prefer the run's end time; omitted if unknown
                          "model":"claude-example","latest_tool":{"id":"toolu_…","name":"Read","summary":"Reading example.go"}, // summary in the request's language
                          "tokens":1234,"calls":8}]}],                   // each agent is read as a subagent: GET the content of session session_id
 "asks":"Push it to beta?",   // what the last reply asks the user, read by the node off the whole reply (last_text is only its start); absent when it asks nothing (docs/protocol/agent-states.md "Awaiting your reply")
 "asks_read":true,            // the node read asks off the reply (empty asks then means it asks nothing, was answered, or its closeout says done and needs nobody); without it the hub reads last_text when it is whole
 "awaits_reply":true,         // stopped (unread / idle) on a question nobody answered, with no card, error or background work. Computed by the hub; clients list an idle one as "Awaiting your reply", not folded with the idle ones
 // Session hierarchy (see "Session hierarchy" below), each omitted when empty:
 "completed_todo":{"id":"todo_…","title":"…"},  // display-only completed ownership, never active `todo` or supervision
 "started_at":"...",                    // when the session began (a Codex rollout's first line, a runtime's created time); set by the node where it knows it
 "creation_id":"<id>",                  // start-call identity, used to bind a pre-created task to a session that appears later; omitted when unknown
 "asking_parent_session_id":"<sid>",    // a runtime child that waits for the user (status blocked, its parent fields cleared): the parent it asks for. Set by the node
 "parent_agent_id":"<sid>",             // a Claude desktop app's side session: the session it was started from. Set by the node
 "aliases":["<sid>"],                   // the other ids its computer knows the row's conversation by, none of them listed beside it. A runtime's session listed under an id of its own whose chat is a Claude transcript on its computer: its transcript first, then the sessions that one was forked from, newest first. An Antigravity CLI conversation: on a pane's row its own agy-<conversation id>, which the manager keeps the row's archive under, then the agy pane rows that showed it before, newest first. A Claude desktop app session: the transcripts it went on from. The manager shows no archive record under one beside the row, and the newest record among them and the row's own says whether the row is archived ("Agent session archives"), and an A2A tool given one acts on this row. Set by the node
 "folded_under":"<sid>",                // a child session: its topmost listed ancestor on the same machine, whose chat shows it; a tab's worker: its lead; a side session: its parent's topmost listed row. Set by the manager
 "folded_as":"worker",                  // beside folded_under on a row that is no child: "worker" for a tab's worker, "side" for a side session. Set by the manager
 "folded_side":"<sid>",                 // beside folded_under on a row folded through a side session that is not that side (a side's own Codex child): the side whose chat its cards belong to. Set by the manager
 "children":{"total":3,"working":1,"needs_you":1,"workers":2,"sides":1,"sides_working":1,"sides_needs_you":1,"sides_unread":1},   // on that ancestor: every session folded under it, by their own states (working / needs_you omitted when 0); workers: how many of them are its tab's workers (folded_as "worker"); sides: how many are side sessions (folded_as "side"), and sides_working / sides_needs_you / sides_unread those sides by their own states (each omitted when 0). Set by the manager
 "background_waiting":true,   // background_working, and all that background work only waits: its background commands sleep, loop on a check or watch something, using next to no CPU, and no subagent or workflow runs. Clients write "Waiting in the background", lighter than Working and not in its count; state stays working, so a client without the field shows Working. Omitted when false
 "background_working":true,   // state is working only because of background work (this turn is over, workflows / background commands / Monitors / subagents are running): clients write "Working (Background)". Computed by the hub; omitted when false, so its absence means an old hub only when no run carries tool_use_id and no agent status: there, look for state=working with a running workflow
 // The user's latest manual compaction (assistant chats only, present only after POST …/compact): running → done | failed (error is a human-readable reason); the node keeps it until the next one
 "compaction":{"state":"running|done|failed","error":"…","started_at":"...","finished_at":"..."}}

// Todo: a to-do item
{"id":"todo_…","title":"Ship version 1.3 of the weather App","notes":"Notes","done_at":null,
 "created_at":"...","updated_at":"...",
 "origin":"<assistant chat id>","plan_id":"plan_…",   // only on tasks opened from an assistant chat
 "part_of":"todo_…","after":["todo_…"],   // a piece of the request part_of names, waiting for the pieces in after; omitted for a to-do that is no piece
 "start_error":"rpc: connection closed",         // the task's Agent failed to start: the hub also sets done_at, and the task ends there; cleared on reopen.
                                                 // A coded refusal (a launcher the new terminal tab can't run) is the hub's sentence in the user's language; its code is on the plan's task
 "quiet":true,   // dispatched by the main chat while "notify about main-chat tasks only in the main chat" was on: fixed at creation, never changes
 "done_by":"auto|review|cancelled",   // empty = user / launch failure; auto = legacy judge closure; review = accepted; cancelled = cancelled, reason in done_reason
 "cancelled_at":"...","cancelled_reason":"…",   // additive cancellation projection; cancelled_at mirrors done_at. Older cancellations may still say done_by=review with supervision.state=cancelled
 // Supervision record: only on tasks dispatched by the main chat; clients that don't know it show the to-do as usual
 "supervision":{"supervisor":"<main chat id>",
                "done_when":["PR merged into master","Light / dark screenshots posted in the PR"],   // acceptance criteria, may be an empty array
                "expect_minutes":30,                                    // estimated minutes, 0 / absent = not given
                "state":"",       // "" in progress | pending_review awaiting review | user_check awaiting the owner's verification (task stays open) | rework being reworked | needs_user waiting for the user to decide | parked waiting on purpose until a time | accepted accepted | cancelled cancelled
                                  // (for accepted / cancelled the to-do is done; after the user reopens it, it counts as in progress)
                                  // a plan's task that takes the to-do over with a new Agent (continues / todo_id) starts a new round:
                                  // state goes back to "" and round to 0, the earlier review stays in reviews
                // only while state is parked (additive): what the task waits for in one sentence, until when (RFC 3339),
                // what kind of thing it waits on (owner_priority | someone_else | external_event | date) and how many times in a row it was parked with no agent turn in between;
                // a parked task is open and is not waiting on the user. Clients that do not know the state show the task as in progress
                "parked":{"reason":"The design team has to pick the icon set first","until":"...","waiting_on":"someone_else","count":1},
                "round":1,        // how many rework rounds, at most 2
                "reviews":[{"at":"...","verdict":"accepted|rework|needs_user|parked|cancelled","round":1,   // round only on rework; "by":"reviewer" on a rework the independent review started
                            "checks":[{"criterion":"Light / dark screenshots posted in the PR","met":false,"evidence":"Only the light one"}],"note":"Add the dark screenshot"}],
                // its agent's latest report to the supervisor (report_to_supervisor); absent until it reports, and after a hub restart until it reports again
                "progress":{"kind":"progress|question|blocked|done","step":3,"steps":5,"text":"one line of what it said",   // step / steps absent = not said
                            "line":"the report paraphrased in the user's language",   // one sentence of at most 30 characters (60 outside Chinese and Japanese), written by the triage's model shortly after the report; absent until then, and for good with no model or when it failed
                            "detail":"the report as the agent wrote it (Markdown)",   // at most 2000 characters, ending in … when cut; absent when it equals text
                            "at":"..."},
                // clients show progress.line ?? text in the Progress row and progress.detail ?? text (Markdown) in the task's details;
                // line and detail are for clients only: no prompt, supervision message, briefing, card or push reads them
                // the latest independent review of its change; absent when none ran
                "auto_review":{"id":"rv_…","state":"running|clean|blocking|failed|cancelled","round":0,"count":2,"blocking":1,
                               "findings":"the reviewer's report","error":"why it failed","session_id":"<reviewer>","worktree":"<its copy>",
                               "started_at":"...","ended_at":"..."},
                // the done judge found the latest stretch of work stopped on a decision only the owner can make; absent when that does not hold. While it is there the task is not accepted.
                "waits":{"work":"... (when the stretch began)","at":"...","reason":"the judge's reason"},
                // only while state is pending_review (additive): when the task entered it (RFC 3339). Set on the way in, kept by every later write
                // while the review waits (a criterion's report, a new supervisor), absent in every other state. Clients list a review younger than
                // one hour with the tasks in progress, as its supervisor's to do, and an older one under Needs you; with the field absent (an older hub, or a
                // review that began before the hub kept the time) they keep the task under Needs you. updated_at is not a stand-in: other writes move it
                "pending_since":"...",
                "updated_at":"..."},
 // The task's brief: what was asked when the work was handed out, never rewritten; absent on a to-do with none.
 // Clients that don't know it show the to-do as usual.
 "brief":{"id":"brief_…","created_at":"...",
          "request":{"text":"the owner's words, verbatim","part":true,"at":"...","conversation":"<chat id>","message_id":"<source item id>"},   // absent when the owner did not ask for it
          // request.part is true for a selected passage and omitted for a whole message. message_id and at always identify the original message.
          // request.truncated is true when text was clipped at 2000 characters. request.via lists the relaying conversations, oldest first.
          "started_by":"owner|assistant|leader|routine|hub|unknown",
          "trigger":"supervision|followup|routine|conversation|notice|meeting|wake","trigger_title":"…","reason":"why it was started",   // when not the owner
          "conversation":"<chat id>","goal":"one sentence","done_when":["…"],"expect_minutes":37,"estimate_source":"learned","out_of_bounds":["…"],   // as handed out
          "estimate_evidence":{"minutes":37,"sample_count":7,"cohort":"repo_machine"},   // automatic choice, optional
          "reconstructed":true,"handover":"the prompt at hand-over, not the owner's words",   // a task from before briefs
          "log":[{"at":"...","kind":"dispatch","source":"task_plan","plan_id":"plan_…","round_id":"plan_…/todo_…@...","todo_id":"todo_…","expect_minutes":37,"estimate_source":"learned","estimate_evidence":{"minutes":37,"sample_count":7,"cohort":"repo_machine"}},
                 {"at":"...","kind":"scope","todo_id":"todo_…","by":"<chat id>","change":"…","why":"…","done_when":["…"],"expect_minutes":90,"estimate_source":"override",
                  "added":["…"],"dropped":["…"],"approval":{"text":"…","at":"...","conversation":"…","message_id":"…"}},   // approval: the owner's message that allowed a risky step
                 {"at":"...","kind":"completion","source":"report_to_supervisor|task_review|judge","todo_id":"todo_…","round_id":"plan_…/todo_…@...","actual_minutes":45},
                 {"at":"...","kind":"estimate_due","todo_id":"todo_…"},   // accepted delivery of the current estimate_due review cue
                 {"at":"...","kind":"overdue","todo_id":"todo_…"}],
          "criteria":["…"],"expect_minutes_now":90,     // done_when and expect_minutes as the scope changes left them
          "estimate_source_now":"override","estimate_clock_at":"...","estimate_due_at":"...","estimate_due_told_at":"...",
          // estimate_evidence_now is present when the current estimate has automatic evidence; an override clears it.
          // Evidence cohort is repo_machine, machine, comparable, default (too few samples), or history_unavailable.
          "actual_minutes":45,"completion_reported_at":"...",   // latest completion; every round remains in log
          "clock_at":"...","due_at":"...","overdue_at":"...",   // the overdue clock: from the hand-out or latest scope change to max(expect × 3, 24 h); overdue_at once its supervisor was told
          "result":{"at":"...","todo_id":"todo_…","by":"judge","verdict":"accepted|cancelled",   // by absent: the supervisor's review; by=judge only on legacy history
                    "criteria":[{"criterion":"…","state":"met|not_met|unchecked|dropped","evidence":"…","change":"the scope change that dropped it","changed_at":"..."}],
                    "also_done":["…"]}},
 // The to-dos that carried the brief's work, oldest first; why: why it stopped (the reason the one that took over gave, else its own end)
 "lineage":[{"todo_id":"todo_…","title":"…","agent":"claude","machine":"<machine id>","session_id":"…","started":"...","ended":"...","why":"…",
             "continues":"todo_…","superseded_by":"todo_…","current":true}],
 "spaces":[{"machine_id":"…","space":"group/alpha","linked_at":"..."}],
 "agents":[{"machine_id":"…","session_id":"…","linked_at":"...","released_at":null,
           "title":"…","cwd":"…","agent":"claude","start_error":"","source":"manual|space|spawned|leader|worker|review","via":""}]}   // review: an independent reviewer, released from the start
 // agents[].agent is the link's Agent-kind snapshot from the session or start answer's session.agent. Planned, spawned and quiet agent_start links
 // fall back to the explicitly resolved launcher kind, including when agent_start adopts a session after a lost answer.
 // A launcher-repair link uses only the repair Agent's start answer. Empty means unknown. An empty relink preserves the stored kind.

// Item: one normalized transcript entry (one per content block)
{"id":"<entry uuid>#<block idx>","seq":123,            // seq = transcript line number, monotonically increasing, used for increments and paging
 "ts":"...","role":"user|assistant|system",
 "kind":"text|thinking|tool_use|tool_result|notice|image|fold|turn_duration|visualization",
 "text":"…",                                           // text of text / thinking / notice / tool_result
 "model":"claude-opus-5-5",                           // assistant items only, optional: the model that wrote the item as the transcript records it (Claude Code's message.model, never its "<synthetic>";
                                                      // a Codex turn's turn_context model). Absent when the transcript does not say and from older nodes; clients draw a divider where the replies' model changes
 "usage":[{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","in":3,"out":412,"cache_read":40210,"cache_write":1180}], // optional: the tokens of the model requests this item stands for, one entry per model and speed; see "Token usage on items"
 "codex_heartbeat_quiet":true, // optional, assistant text: the node decoded a Codex DONT_NOTIFY envelope; the hub localizes its generated text. Matching prose has no marker and is left as written.
 "model_refusal":{"subtype":"model_refusal_fallback","original_model":"primary-model","fallback_model":"fallback-model","category":"synthetic-policy","scope":"session","explanation":"Upstream refused the request","text":"<the refusal's own words>"}, // optional, kind=notice: the record's values as recorded (unknown model_refusal_* subtypes, categories and scopes too) and `text`, its string `content`. Never the record's line (`raw`) or its other fields: they stay in the transcript and the node; clients must not show or keep a `raw`. The notice's `text` is the refusal's words, which the hub writes again in the reader's language
 "tool_use_id":"toolu_…",                             // shared by tool_use and tool_result; clients merge them into one card by it
 "tool_name":"Bash", "tool_input":{...},              // tool_use only
 "is_error":false,                                    // tool_result only
 "outcome":{"status":"failed","exit_code":2,"tail":"…"}, // tool_result only, optional: what the call came to (status, exit code, duration, the output's end, patch, files, git, read range, answers), see "Tool outcomes"
 "full_size":4874,                                    // text was truncated (in pages and pushes, tool output is at most 4 KB, other text 24 KB): the byte size of the full text;
                                                      // truncated text ends in a note line: for tool output "…（已截断，点开看全文，共 N 字节）" ("truncated, open to see the full text, N bytes"; the web app has a "view full text" button),
                                                      // for other text "…（已截断，共 N 字节）" ("truncated, N bytes")
 "queued":true,                                       // user text only: a message typed while working, absorbed mid-turn
 "client_msg_id":"…",                                 // this item comes from a message the web app sent with this client_msg_id (text, image, or the notice /compact turns into),
                                                      // recognized by the node, see "Matching pending messages"; old hubs / nodes omit it
 "wake":true,                                         // a notice or agent tool result started a new turn after Claude was idle
 "narration":true,                                    // optional Codex commentary, still a text item but not a final reply
 "injected":{"kind":"task_notice","state":"done",…},   // user text only: this is a message Persona sent to the model (task notification, scheduled task, wake-up…), not written by the user; added by the hub when sending, see "Messages injected by Persona"
 "source":{"kind":"conversation|patrol|followup|supervision|meeting","conversation_id":"…","title":"…"}, // optional input provenance, independent of role; id/title optional, see "Message source"
 "from":"peer name",                                  // optional native peer sender (another Claude session, a teammate, a Paseo Agent); a display name, not necessarily a conversation id
 "compact":{"trigger":"manual|auto","pre_tokens":151467}, // notice only: the context was compacted here (Claude Code's compact_boundary); the web app draws a divider and folds the following "已从压缩的上下文继续" ("continued from compacted context") and the idle-compaction note into it
 "task":{"kind":"shell|monitor|agent|workflow|task",     // task notices; also agent tool results associated with their launching call
         "status":"running|completed|failed|killed|stopped|event|ended|waiting","title":"description or the command's first line",
         "task_id":"…","tool_use_id":"toolu_…","exit_code":0,"output_file":"…", // tool_use_id: the call that started the task, also when the notification names only the task (an earlier one of the task named it); a Paseo child's notice has neither
         "detail":"the Monitor event / the subagent's result / the whole command (entities decoded)"},
 "fold":{"items":1294,"tools":647,"thoughts":110,     // kind=fold only (only when the request carries fold_work): a folded stretch of work, see "Folded work"; may carry tasks, images, usage
         "errors":3,"tool_names":["Bash","Read","Edit"],  // failed tool results and the tools called (at most 10); absent from older nodes
         "until":"...","through_seq":6890,"through_id":"…#0",
         "changes":[{"path":"/…/a.go","add":12,"del":3,"exact":true}],   // the files its successful edits changed; [] when none
         "sources":[{"url":"https://example.com/page","title":"…"}]},   // the web pages its successful web calls used; absent when none
 "image":{"mime":"image/png","data":"base64"},       // image only (images in tool_result are also split into image items, with tool_use_id)
 "visualization":{"path":"…/visualizations/2026/11/18/<codex session id>/chart.html", "mode":"wide", "title":"Quarterly sales"} // kind=visualization only (Codex "visualize"):
                                                      // a self-contained HTML fragment on the node, never its bytes; mode is "wide" or absent, title optional. Clients fetch the
                                                      // fragment with …/items/{id}/visualization and run it offline in their HTML sandbox
}

 "review_count":2,                                              // that review's finding count, parsed from its marker; omitted when unknown
 "reviewer_session_id":"uuid",                                 // that review's hidden reviewer, for correlation, not a list entry
 "plan_then":"acceptEdits",                                     // plan: the supported mode recorded at start, authoritative on every approving surface; absent, plan or unknown keeps legacy choices
 "tool_input":{...}, "summary":"rm -rf build",                   // permission

 "screen":"visible terminal text",                                // screen (TUI dialogs hooks can't cover)
 "always_keys":["tool:Bash"],  // node → hub: what "Always Allow" on an assistant chat's permission card lets through; the hub records it and answers the same card itself; not used by clients
 "always_honored":false,       // manager → clients: whether answering Always is kept; see "Always allow" below
 "can_clarify":true,           // manager → clients: this prepared assistant approval accepts owner questions; additive, absent on older managers
 "owner_proposal":true,         // manager → clients: server-owned exact connector proposal; never infer this from tool_name
 "approval_batch_id":"oab_…", "approval_item_id":"oai_…", // durable batch and optional item target; batch cards omit item
 "owner_approval_phrases":["发","同意"], // complete exact replies accepted for this proposal; empty/absent means no reply button
 "no_expiry":true,              // with resumable+owner_proposal: remain pending across the former deadline and restart
 "detachable":true,            // node → manager, assistant command gates only: release the initial hook after 75s and continue with a one-time exact-call grant; ignored elsewhere
 "execution_cwd":"/absolute/work/dir", // node → manager, required beside detachable: where this command actually runs; included in the exact-call grant, unlike display-only cwd
 "tool_title":"Computer control", // manager → clients: its own tool's name for people, in the user's language; see "Always allow" below
 "tool_name_title":"Report to supervisor", // manager → clients: the tool alone, beside a tool_title that also says what the call does; see "Always allow" below
 "agent":"codex", "reason":"…", "always_label":"本会话不再问这个命令"} // a card the node read from the Codex / compatible forks TUI ("Codex questions and approvals"); always_label is emitted in Chinese: "don't ask about this command again this session"

// Resolution (by kind)
{"answers":{"<original question text>":"the chosen label; multiple joined with \", \"; or custom text"}}   // question
{"approve":true,"mode":"bypassPermissions|acceptEdits|default|auto"}          // plan approved; plan_then on the card, when present, replaces an older client's mode
{"approve":false,"feedback":"Change it to…"}                                  // plan sent back
{"allow":true,"always":false} / {"allow":false,"message":"…"}                // permission
{"allow":true,"edited_text":"replacement text"}                             // permission, only on the card's editable_text and with no other resolution field
{"keys":["down","enter"],"text":""}                                         // screen: keys / text sent to the pane
{"dismiss":true}                                                            // any: give up, hand back to the computer's TUI
{"dismiss":true,"pending":true,"approval_id":"ix_…","message":"End this turn…"} // detachable initial hook only: no decision and no execution; the card stays pending
{"allow":true,"approval_id":"ix_…","edited_text":"optional replacement"}   // manager → node only: one consumed exact-call continuation grant for the named earlier card
{"dismiss":true,"reason":"replied_in_chat"}                                  // the assistant's ask_user taken back because the user wrote in the chat
{"cancel":true}                                                             // question with can_cancel:true: discard without an answer
{"answers":{"…":"…"},"answered_by":"assistant"}                               // answered by the assistant: question only; web app replies don't carry answered_by
```

### Reviewing a session's work

A `question` interaction with `tool_name: "persona_session_review"` is a completed independent review, not an Agent asking
for input. Its `summary` is the localized finding count (or "Review complete"), `review_report` is the full Markdown report,
`review_count` is the count parsed from the reviewer, and `reviewer_session_id` correlates the hidden reviewer. These
fields are absent on other cards. The
card has one question with two options, **Send to agent** and **Dismiss** (the latter carries `action: "defer"`). Answer
with the ordinary `{"answers":{"<original question text>":"<option label>"}}`; the manager, never the browser, forwards
the persisted report. Send uses a normal source-session message (resuming a stopped source at the owner's explicit
request), while Dismiss sends nothing. Review cards have no notification quick answer and expire after seven days.

### Editable Lark approval text

Only the Claude Code Bash `PreToolUse` gate declares `editable_text`, and only for one static, proxy-authenticated Lark message send/reply whose JSON object has a non-empty top-level `text`. Codex, agent runtimes, lark-cli, file-backed or dynamic bodies, multi-call commands and non-message routes keep the ordinary permission card. The field carries the current text alone: no route, method, query, recipient, mention or tool argument is editable.

`edited_text` is valid only as `{"allow":true,"edited_text":"…"}` on that card. The manager rejects it with Always, Deny, dismiss, cancel, answers, fields, action, reason, remembered or any other resolution field; After a plain edited Allow, the node retires the original card's one-use grant by interaction id, splices only that body word, classifies and checks the new command through the same gate, and grants only the edited call once. Method, path, query, gate and every other body field must remain identical, including JSON numbers too large for float64. Claude receives `updatedInput` with every original tool-input field and only `command` replaced. A denial note remains `{"allow":false,"message":"…"}` and becomes the denied call's tool result.

### Always allow

A permission card offers **Always allow** only where the answer is kept. The manager says so in
`always_honored`, a tri-state:

- `true`: it is kept. The manager sets it on a node's card in an assistant chat whose `always_keys` it remembers
  (a store, at most 32 keys, no `fields`), and on a card of its own that says in `always_label` what it keeps (the apps
  a computer may use, LCU's own scopes).
- `false`: nothing would keep it. The manager sets it on every other card it asks itself: the extensions' tools
  (`computer_*`, `browser_run`, connector writes, `extension.ui`), `persona_settings`, its to-do, agent
  and confirmations in a track; and on a node's card in an assistant chat it will not remember (keys but no store, more
  than 32 keys, `fields`, no keys at all, as a gated command confirmed whole names none, or a track
  conversation's card, confirmed each time). Clients show only Allow and Deny, and
  no scope line. An `always` answered on such a card anyway is dropped: the card is allowed once.
- absent: clients keep their own rule: on the web and in Lark a card
  from Claude (no `agent`, or `claude`) or one with an `always_label`. Agents sessions' cards never carry the field: their
  agent keeps Always itself (Claude Code's session rule).

The field is a tri-state rather than a plain "kept" flag because absence cannot mean "not kept": an Agents session's
Claude card and a manager card look the same otherwise (a session, no `agent`, no `always_keys`). A client therefore hides the choice only on an explicit `false`. The value is the manager's: whatever a node sends in
the field (or in `tool_title`) is dropped.

`tool_title` is the tool's name for people in the user's language (`assistant-tool_titles` in the hub's catalog), set by the manager on its own tools' cards and on a node's card for one of
Persona's own MCP tools (`mcp__persona__…` under either namespace: "Report to supervisor · Done", any other "Persona · agent read"). Clients title the card with it, and otherwise
with `tool_name`; Agents sessions' cards for any other tool never carry it. Where the title also says what
this call does (a report's kind), `tool_name_title` names the tool alone ("Report to supervisor"): a line about what
Always covers, every call of the tool, uses it, else `tool_title`, else the tool's name in words. Both are in the
hub's language (the manager's `lang`, from the hub's locale) like the rest of the text it writes, whatever language
the client is in. A node's value for either is dropped.

### Approval clarification

`can_clarify` marks an assistant-owned permission card with a process-local prepared operation. A question is an action, not a Resolution. `POST /api/v1/interactions/{id}/clarify` accepts only `{text, client_msg_id}` and returns `{"ok":true,"pending":true}` after the exact original conversation accepts the owner's verbatim question; the card remains pending. Blank questions and trimmed questions over 1,000 Unicode code points are rejected. Extension principals receive 403.

The original tool returns the non-final outcome `{clarifying:true,text}` rather than an Allow or Deny. Its text says the question is not an approval decision and arrives as a separate owner message. A short-lived, one-time proof binds the authenticated question to its card, exact text, destination and `client_msg_id`: the hub issues it for a full-device Web request, and the extension manager issues it only after a fresh Feishu owner action. The assistant returns the opaque token through `session.send_once`; the hub consumes it before sending and the devices manager alone writes `owner_input`. Proof never grants Apply. A later fresh owner Allow rechecks the current proposal and executes at most once; Deny executes nothing.

Clarified cards preserve their remaining decision time while answers run, with a cumulative 24-hour pause budget. Pending snapshots publish the current effective `expires_at`: the actual pause-budget deadline while paused, then the resumed decision deadline. Same-ID updates carry it without another arrival or push. Every terminal path sends one result containing the literal interaction ID to the original conversation.

### Exact owner replies for connector batches

A permission interaction with `owner_proposal:true` is a durable server-owned connector proposal, not an instruction to approve from a prose summary. `approval_batch_id` identifies its batch; item cards also carry `approval_item_id`. The client may offer an exact-reply action only when the card advertises a nonempty `owner_approval_phrases` entry and has its complete origin metadata. Direct Allow and Deny remain available and resolve the same durable target; Always is never created by an exact reply.

The web client sends `{text,client_msg_id,approval_reply_to}` to the existing session-message endpoint, with no `via`, model, quote, image or other composer metadata. `approval_reply_to` is the exact interaction ID. A successful approval replies `200 {"ok":true,"approval_reply":true,"interaction_id":"<same id>"}` and does not deliver the phrase to the node/model. The client verifies this receipt; it is not a normal `{ok:true}` send and must not fall back to ordinary delivery or `/interactions/{id}/resolve`. A repeated logical operation retains its `client_msg_id` and operation ID. Feishu instead requires an authenticated owner DM reply to the exact stored parent card plus a fresh one-use proof. All other locations, attribution and non-exact claims fail closed.

Persistent proposals carry `resumable:true,no_expiry:true`. Only that complete owner-proposal combination restores an unanswered card with no deadline; an arbitrary ordinary interaction cannot acquire indefinite life by setting `no_expiry`. Both feature switches and the phrase list are assistant settings below.

### Subagent deliveries as tool results

Claude Code subagent launch receipts, peer reports (including `SendMessage` to the parent), handbacks and task
notifications use the existing `tool_result` kind when the parser knows their launching `Agent` or `Task` call.
Both the item and its `task` carry that call's `tool_use_id`; `task.kind` is `agent`. The association comes from the
runtime's agent ID and launch record, or a notification's explicit call ID, never the sender's display name.
Unrelated cross-session messages retain their existing `user` text and `from` provenance. Unknown associations are
not invented.

- `task.status: running` marks a launch receipt or an interim report. `waiting` also remains nonterminal. These
  results do not end the running subagent or count as a user question. Completed, failed, killed and stopped results
  are terminal. Unknown statuses must not be inferred as completed.
- Each delivery retains its original item ID and sequence. There can be several results for one call: clients keep
  an ordered result list rather than replacing earlier reports with the latest item. Render them only under the
  original call, collapsed by default and manually expandable, not as independent messages in the parent chat.
  Running subagents keep their existing work/progress presentation.
- `text` is the report body, capped for pages with the normal `full_size` marker. `task.detail` is a bounded 4 KB
  compatibility preview. Use `text` first and the existing item full-text endpoint for manual full inspection.
  Launch receipts are not reports. A status-only notification, including the pointer after an already delivered
  handback, has no `text` or `task.detail`; its status still participates in the call's lifecycle.
- `wake` marks a task notification or associated peer report delivered as a user line while the parent was idle,
  including hidden `isMeta` peer lines. Queued-command attachments absorbed mid-turn do not carry it. It starts a
  new parent turn without becoming a user-authored message: clients begin a new exchange at it, so the last words
  of the turn before it stay that turn's answer and are never folded into the woken turn's work. Cold windows reconstruct earlier launch associations
  and delivery status before parsing their tail; incremental reads append results, never rewrite the old receipt.
  Antigravity also emits a generic system `notice` with `wake: true` when its background work resumes after a
  delivered answer. Live ACP and native transcript readers use the same exchange boundary before the resumed
  content, including when a viewer has already advanced past the native scheduling notification.

The Claude transcript history token includes an opaque parser-version component; the existing history-change reset discards cached standalone peer cards when an updated node is first read. Clients must not parse this token or require a new feature flag.

### Answering a question from its notification

A question notification may carry an optional top-level `ask` alongside `interaction_id`, `machine_id`, `session_id` and `hub_id`.

```json
{
  "interaction_id": "ix_example",
  "machine_id": "computer_example",
  "session_id": "session_example",
  "hub_id": "hub_example",
  "ask": {
    "question": "Which library?",
    "options": ["pgx", "sqlc"],
    "multi_select": false,
    "rev": "<opaque rev from the hub>"
  }
}
```

`ask` is present only for a `question` card with exactly one question, at least one option, no fields to fill in, not from a Just me turn, whose asker did not say going ahead cannot be undone (an `ask_user` card's `reversible: false`, which a to-do's view marks `open_only`), and a conversation of a track. The question and ordered option labels are complete; the shortened alert text is never an answer source. `rev` is an opaque 12-character hexadecimal SHA-256 prefix covering the question, option labels and their order, and `multi_select`. Clients echo the received value; they do not calculate it.

Send the selected zero-based index back to the hub identified by the notification, using the same authentication as resolve:

```http
POST /api/v1/interactions/ix_example/choose
Authorization: Bearer <device token>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: en

{"option":1,"rev":"<rev from ask>","client_id":"<unique id for this tap>"}
```

For a card with `multi_select:true`, send `{"options":[1,0],"rev":"<rev from ask>","client_id":"<unique id for this submission>"}`. Send exactly one of `option` or `options`; `options` must be non-empty and have no repeated indexes. A single-select card accepts only one index. The hub validates the current card and revision, maps indexes to the complete labels in the card's order, and forwards a normal Resolution to the card's owning manager. For the example, index 1 becomes `{"answers":{"Which library?":"sqlc"}}`; multi-select indexes `[1,0]` become `{"answers":{"Which library?":"pgx, sqlc"}}`. Supplying a manager header does not override the card's owner.

On success the response is `200 {"ok":true}`. Keep the same `client_id`, target, revision and indexes when retrying a submission after a lost response. The body ID uses the existing `withClientOp` receipt mechanism; without `client_id`, an explicit `X-Persona-Op-Id` UUID is also supported. When both are present, `client_id` determines the receipt ID. A stored successful receipt replays success even after the card has disappeared. Reusing an ID with different parameters or another device returns `409 op_id_reused`. Without an operation ID there is no durable receipt. Full device credentials may choose. Extension credentials require `agents.control` and remain limited to their own manager's cards.

Errors have `{code,error}`, with human-readable `error` localized in English, Simplified Chinese or Japanese. Branch on `code`:

| HTTP | Code | Meaning and client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed JSON, a missing revision or missing / conflicting selection fields. Open the card. |
| 400 | `invalid_choice` | An index is negative, beyond the options, or repeated, or an `options` entry is null. Open the card. |
| 400 | `single_select` | More than one option was supplied for a single-select card. Ask for one selection. |
| 400 | `not_choosable` | The current card cannot be answered by notification choices (multiple questions, no options, fields, a Just me turn, an asker who said it cannot be undone, a track's conversation or another card kind). Open the card. |
| 409 | `ask_changed` | The revision no longer matches. Open and refresh the card; never apply the old index to new options. |
| 409 | `not_pending` | The card is absent from the hub's pending cards, or the manager reports it already ended. This includes unknown, answered, withdrawn and expired cards; do not submit another choice. Open the card to inspect the current state. |
| 409 | `op_id_reused` | The submission ID already names a different operation. Keep the original request when checking its result. |
| 413 | `too_large` | The request body exceeds 4 KiB. |
| 502 | `assistant_in_doubt` | The connection dropped or timed out after sending; the choice may already have been applied. Open the card to check it. The receipt stays unknown and the same ID will not execute again. |
| 503 | `assistant_offline` | The owning manager did not receive the choice. Retry the unchanged submission when it reconnects. |

The shared authentication, scope, size-limit and operation-receipt errors still apply. A `202` receipt state of `pending` or `unknown` is not successful delivery: repeat the unchanged request to inspect its receipt, or open the card, retaining the original submission ID. An uncertain upstream outcome must not be resubmitted under a new ID. An `assistant_offline` refusal keeps no receipt when the store can release it, so the same ID can be tried again; an uncertain result stays recorded.

When `ask` is absent or cannot be rendered completely by the client, open the card. Do not reconstruct answers from clipped alert text. A question explicitly marked `reversible: false` opens the card.

### Closing a question without an answer

A question advertises `can_cancel:true` only when its runtime can discard that request and release its waiter without interrupting the task. Clients hide the close action when the field is absent or false. Send only `{"cancel":true}` to the existing resolve endpoint; mixing cancellation with answers, dismissal, approvals, keys, or other actions returns 400 and leaves the card pending. Approvals cannot be cancelled through this action. Folding a card remains local UI state.

The manager records `cancelled` with the cancellation resolution, removes the pending card, and releases its waiter once. Repeated HTTP cancellation returns the recorded result, and a reconnecting resumable hook receives the same cancellation instead of a new question. Claude `AskUserQuestion` hooks deny only that tool call without `updatedInput.answers`; Codex owned and joined app-server `item/tool/requestUserInput` requests receive `{"answers":{}}` on the original request, with no user message or `turn/interrupt`. The assistant's `ask_user` tool also releases its wait with an explicit no-answer result. Existing `dismiss` still hands control back to the computer.

Manager-owned `persona_triage` cards also advertise cancellation. Their cancellation defers only that turn, removes its wakeup, and sends no Agent message. Triage option objects may carry `action:"defer"`; clients still submit the selected label in `answers`, and the owner interprets the action on that exact offered single-choice option. Terminal outcomes are replayed to the owner without showing the same ID again.

Terminal-only Codex questions (including asynchronous rollout questions) do not advertise cancellation: sending Escape may fold a pane, clear notes, or stop a turn.

### Decision fields

The assistant's `ask_user` card keeps what the assistant said of the decision, on the card itself and so in `GET /api/v1/interactions/history` (`assistant/decision_deadline.go`, `keepAskDecision`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `deadline` (card) | RFC 3339: when, unanswered, its recommended options are taken by default (reversible) or the user is reminded again (not). Absent without a deadline |
| `reversible` (card) | Whether going ahead can be undone, as the assistant said it. Absent when it did not say (it must with a deadline): never guessed |
| `questions[].recommend` | The label of the option the assistant recommends, always one of the question's options. Absent when it recommended none |

Every other card (Agents' questions, permissions, plans, screens) has none of them. They are optional keys on the `interaction` object. A card the assistant passed on to the user keeps its single recommendation in `delegate.recommend`.

### Who answered a card

`resolution.answered_by` says who answered, and where when it was not a direct answer on a card: absent for the user (in the web app, a channel, or the to-do the question became), `assistant` for the assistant on the user's behalf (`reason` says why), `terminal` for a decision the terminal made on the computer (the card stays `dismissed`, with no fabricated approval), `default` when nobody answered and the recommended options were taken at a reversible deadline (`reason` says so).

An `ask_user` card that expires unanswered becomes a to-do. Its history stays `expired`; what was answered after that is recorded on it with `resolution.late: true` (`assistant/late_answer.go`, `db.LateAnswer`): the user's own answers on the to-do (`answered_by` absent; one per question as each is given) or the default taken at the deadline (`answered_by: "default"`, with the deadline's `reason`), and `resolved_at` becomes when that happened. A question that cannot be undone is never taken by default, so its history keeps no answer until the user gives one. Only the manager writes `late` and `answered_by`: a client's answer has them dropped.

### MCP elicitation

`hello.features` adds `elicitation`. Clients must declare it explicitly in `client_hello.features`; the web client declares it by default (the web client's `X-Persona-Client` gives platform web, version 1, matching the `platform` / `version` in its `client_hello`). The `interaction` object in the existing `interaction` event gains the following optional fields; no keys are added at the envelope's top level:

```json
{
  "kind": "elicitation",
  "mcp_server_name": "example-mcp",
  "agent_id": "agent_example",
  "agent_type": "worker",
  "elicitation": {
    "mode": "form",
    "message": "Please choose",
    "requested_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"choice": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

In URL mode `elicitation` is `{"mode":"url","message":"Open the link to confirm","url":"https://example.com/confirm","elicitation_id":"request_example"}`. `mcp_config_source`, `tool_name` and `tool_use_id` are all optional and present only when the source provides them; Claude Code's Elicitation input provides no tool association or config source, and nothing is inferred when they're missing.

Resolution gains optional `action` and `content`. `{"action":"accept","content":{"choice":"yes"}}` submits a form; accepting a URL sends only `{"action":"accept"}`; decline and cancel are `{"action":"decline"}` and `{"action":"cancel"}`. `{"dismiss":true}` still means giving up the takeover and handing it to the terminal. A reply without a valid action returns 400 and the request stays pending.

Delivery and fallback rules:

- Both broadcasts and connection initialization filter out connections that didn't declare the capability. After a connection first declares it, still-pending elicitations are resent; repeated hellos don't resend.
- The REST pending and history lists are filtered too. That kind is returned only if an active connection with the same credential and the same `X-Persona-Client` platform / version has declared the capability; an HTTP header can't declare a capability by itself.
- If there is no compatible connection at creation, it is handed back to the terminal immediately, leaving no request waiting for an answer. The existing timeout, revocation and restart-recovery rules for interactions still apply.
- WebSocket notifications for these cards go only to connections that declared both `ws_notify` and `elicitation`. The shared Fleet keeps using the existing terminal prompt and is not given the new kind.

The new fields are stored in the existing interaction JSON payload.

## Saved Agent searches

The default manager owns reusable runtime-Agent query definitions in its Postgres setting `agents.saved_searches`.
The hub forwards these routes unchanged; explicit `X-Persona-Manager` pins a captured owner, otherwise the default
manager is used. The web deliberately uses the default rather than the sidebar's current Assistant. These routes
do not execute or interpret a search, start sessions, run commands or send messages. Applying a query remains a
client action through the existing palette.

| Method and path | Body | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/saved-agent-searches` | none | `SavedAgentSearches` |
| `POST /api/v1/saved-agent-searches` | `{revision: decimal string, action, ...fields}` | full confirmed `SavedAgentSearches` |

```text
SavedAgentSearches { revision: decimal string, searches: SavedAgentSearch[], can_write: bool }
SavedAgentSearch { id, name, query, created_at: RFC3339, updated_at: RFC3339 }
```

The revision is a canonical nonnegative int64 decimal string on the wire (no leading zeros except `"0"`), preserving
identity in JavaScript. It is stored as int64 in Settings. An absent key starts at revision `"0"` with `searches: []`;
a failed read is never an empty success. GET and POST require a real store with both `Setting` and `CompareSetting`.
Full-role connections may write; extension tokens with `agents.read` may only read.
No extension write scope is granted. `can_write` reflects the request role, not a promise that the next write succeeds.

| Action | Fields beyond revision/action |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | `name`, `query`; server creates `search_` + 24 lowercase hex ID and UTC timestamps |
| `update` | `id`, `name`, `query`; preserves identity, creation time and position |
| `delete` | `id`; removes that entry without resetting collection revision |
| `move` | `id`, optional `before_id`; absent/empty appends, an existing different anchor inserts before it |
| `restore` | full captured `item`, optional `before_id`; restores a deleted identity only when ID/name are absent |

Every action has an exact field set; unknown, duplicate, differently cased or mixed-action members are rejected.
The body limit is 16 KiB. Names are trimmed, control-free, 1–64 Unicode code points, unique by Unicode case-fold.
Queries are trimmed, valid UTF-8, control-free and 1–1,024 bytes; a leading `>` is rejected because the palette treats
it as command mode. Relative-time expressions stay relative. At most 50 records are retained. Restored timestamps
must be valid, nonzero and ordered; restore preserves the captured metadata. IDs and anchors must use the generated
ID syntax. A missing anchor or self-move is invalid.

A mutation checks the supplied revision against the read document, then atomically replaces it using
`CompareSetting`. A successful mutation increments revision exactly once, including a valid no-op; int64 overflow
is refused. Only after success does the manager broadcast `saved_agent_searches` with `{revision: decimal string}`;
its normal manager stamp identifies the owner. No query text or names are included in the event. The client reloads
that owner while its view is open, and never retries a conflicting write automatically.

Errors: 400 `invalid_request` / `limit_reached`, 403 `forbidden`, 404 `search_not_found` for a missing entry,
409 `conflict` for stale/CAS revisions, 409 `duplicate_name` for conflicting names/restore IDs, 503 `not_supported`
when durable CAS is unavailable, and 503 `storage_unavailable` for read/write failure or corrupt stored data.
Clients distinguish missing entries from an unsupported endpoint and
name validation from revision conflict. Failed actions emit no event and change no persisted collection.

Undo is a `restore` using the revision acknowledged by the delete, never a blind overwrite of the whole collection.
Another write invalidates that Undo. The visible entry order is the stored array order. Newer reads must not replace
a dirty editor's draft or retarget an in-flight request after credential/default-manager changes.

## Workspaces

`GET /api/v1/workspaces` belongs to the manager (the hub forwards it unchanged over the bus `http.request`; 503 `assistant_offline` while the manager is away). It lists the code directories the user's computers know, for the web app's pickers (the composer's `@` mentions, a task's existing workspace):

```text
Workspace { id, machine_id, source, source_id, title, cwd, branch?,
            online: bool, available: bool, last_seen?: RFC3339 }
```

The list merges host spaces, desktop project catalogs and current session directories. Codex saved projects, including empty ones, have source `codex_app`; Claude Desktop local saved environments and directory fallbacks have source `claude_desktop`. Saved Claude identities are scoped to desktop profile and account, preserve native names and can share one project ID across several local roots. These sources do not require a terminal engine. A source's unknown directory may be empty, and clients can't bind based on it. When a machine is offline or enumeration fails, the last snapshot (Postgres `workspace_snapshots`) is used with availability marked, and discovery errors go into `errors`. One source failing must not clear other sources' results. Alias snapshots are grouped by the current effective machine, with the latest complete snapshot winning. A workspace survives a machine going offline and a hub restart through its snapshot. Storage unavailable returns 503 (`not_supported` when the manager's store keeps no snapshots).

Session gains optional `workspace_cwd`: the physical directory verified by the node with symlinks resolved, used only for workspace association; the original `cwd` stays unchanged. The field may be omitted for directories that don't exist, can't be resolved or can't be read. Clients prefer it and fall back to `cwd` when it's missing. The value is cached briefly and is no guarantee of permission or existence for later file operations.

## Main chat readiness (`assistant_readiness`)

Whether the main chat works right now and which step is missing is computed by the hub for the web app. The assistant service answers, for `full` devices only. When the assistant isn't connected it returns 503 `assistant_offline` like the other assistant APIs.

```
GET  /api/v1/assistant/readiness            → Readiness
GET  /api/v1/assistant/readiness?probe=1    → Readiness, plus an actual one-word check of the main chat's next turn (costs money; calls for the same computer, launcher and model within 30 seconds return the last result, and only one runs at a time; it runs to the end even if the client stops waiting: up to 20 s to work out the next turn, up to 170 s for the check (the node's own bound is 150 s), then the 12 s self-check, 202 s in all, so clients wait longer than that)
POST /api/v1/assistant/readiness/dismiss    {"dismissed": true}  →  {"ok": true} (an empty body equals true; false undoes it)
POST /api/v1/assistant/warm                 → {"ok": true, "readiness"?: Readiness} (same structure, no probe; if it can't finish within 2.5 seconds it returns the last recorded one, omitted if none was ever recorded)
```

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "mode": "setup",                 // full / setup; chat_only is reserved and not produced
  "ready": false,                  // mode == "full"
  "next": "model",                 // the first step that isn't ok / skipped; null when all are fine
  "machine": {"id": "mbp", "name": "Lin's MacBook"},   // the main chat's computer; null if none
  "launcher": "claude",            // the effective launcher (Model configuration › Main chat takes precedence); the claude and model steps name theirs
  "steps": [
    {"id": "computer", "state": "ok", "machine": "mbp"},
    {"id": "claude", "state": "ok", "version": "2.1.308"},
    {"id": "model", "state": "problem", "code": "not_logged_in", "machine": "mbp", "launcher": "claude",
     "title": "Claude Code isn't signed in", "detail": "Sign in once on Lin's MacBook, or use an API key instead.",
     "action": {"id": "connect_model"}, "alt_actions": [{"id": "login_claude"}]},
    {"id": "first_message", "state": "todo", "code": "never_tried", "title": "Say hello", "detail": "…", "action": {"id": "test_assistant"}}
  ],
  "suggestions": [{"id": "what_can_you_do", "title": "What can you do for me?", "local": true}],
  "probe": {"ok": false, "agent": "claude", "millis": 2140, "error": "…"},   // only with ?probe=1 and the computer ok
  "dismissed": false,
  "checked_at": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z"
}
```

- `steps` always has four entries in a fixed order: `computer`, `claude`, `model`, `first_message`. `state`: `ok` / `todo` / `problem` / `checking` / `unknown` / `skipped`. `todo` / `problem` always carry `code`, `title`, `detail` (per `Accept-Language`) and usually `action`; `model` in `unknown` carries them too (`model_unverified`).
- `computer`: no computer is `todo` + `no_machine` (`add_computer`); computer not online is `problem` + `node_unreachable` (`wake_computer`); node too old (doesn't know model configuration) is `problem` + `node_outdated` (no button). With no confirmed computer selected, a pending computer owned by the manager is `todo` + `machine_pending` (`confirm_computer`); the top-level `machine` has its ID and display name, and the computer step's `machine` has its ID. With several pending computers, choose the smallest ID. This is a confirmation target, not permission to run there: main-chat creation returns 409 `machine_pending`, `action: "confirm_computer"`, `delivered: "none"`, and `machine_name`. A selected confirmed computer keeps priority even when offline. When the computer isn't `ok`, the next three steps are all `unknown`.
- `claude`: the node self-check (`node.doctor`'s `claude-version`, cached per computer: 10 minutes when a version was read, 1 minute when not) reading a version is `ok` + `version`. The default launcher `claude` not found by the login shell is `problem` + `claude_missing` (`install_claude`, alternative `connect_model`); a check whose `claude --version` did not answer this time while the shell found claude (state `unanswered`: its 10 seconds ran out on a busy machine, or it printed no version) is `unknown`, never `claude_missing`. The last chat start being refused gives `claude_missing` / `launcher_missing` (no longer counted once a later self-check reads a version, or the launcher is back on this computer), and the same when the launcher health check's record says the command wasn't found. Your own launcher no longer existing on this computer is `launcher_missing` (`connect_model`; launchers added in Persona and direct API providers speaking Messages count as present on every computer in their device scope). A launcher running Codex or a runtime is `skipped`. An old node without the self-check, or your own launcher whose version can't be read, is `unknown`. A self-check that didn't finish answering this time is `checking` (GET waits at most 12 seconds, warm 2 seconds; the result is cached either way). Once the model has answered, it is always `ok`.
- `model`: of the launcher the main chat's next turn runs, named in the step's `launcher`: Main chat's, or the main chat's kept pick's when that is on another launcher (the `claude` step follows it too, an external adapter's pick aside), where the main chat's failed turn on Main chat's launcher stands until a newer pass of the picked model. It takes the newest piece of evidence: the latest probe (same computer and launcher, and the model the main chat's next turn asks for there; a pass counts against the main chat's own failed turn only when the node ran the check as that turn, `assistant_turn: true`, or could not have: a launcher of Codex or another agent, or a runtime's launcher, which only get the plain check), the main chat's latest turn (the session's `turn_error` / `turn_error_code`, or a normal answer), the launcher health check record (within 6 hours). If the newest is an answer, `ok`; if it's a failure with a recognized cause, `problem` + `not_logged_in` (`connect_model`, alternative `login_claude`) / `auth_failed` (`edit_provider`) / `model_route` / `rate_limited` (`connect_model`) / `model_fallback_unavailable` (no action) / `tool_search_unsupported` (`test_assistant`) / `upstream_unavailable` (`test_assistant`); with no evidence, or a failure of unrecognized cause, `unknown` + `model_unverified` (`test_assistant`), which doesn't count as a problem. For `rate_limited`, the optional `occurrence` identifies this failure occurrence: a main turn uses its `updated_at`; health-only evidence with a subscription `resets_at` uses that reset window; other evidence uses its timestamp. When newer health evidence has the same reset as the main turn, the turn's identity wins, so settlement and repeated checks do not revive a dismissed warning while another turn in the same reset window is still new. The response's `checked_at` is only the read time. Clients can use `occurrence` without treating another launcher's successful reply as recovery. For `auth_failed` and `model_route`, `alt_actions` includes `test_assistant` so the user can verify a repair even after `first_message` is `ok`, without replacing the current chat. On `not_logged_in`, when the machine has any launcher besides the step's own that can run the main chat (the ones the Main chat purpose lists for it; the machine's list, no probing of the others' sign-in state), `alt_actions` also includes `main_chat_model` — open the model configuration's Main chat purpose and switch to one of them — and the step's `detail` says so instead of only pointing at an API key. The `detail` says the main chat runs the Claude Code CLI, whose sign-in the Claude desktop app's does not give, and names `claude auth login` in a terminal on that computer; when the machine's list has the desktop app's launcher (`claude-desktop`, source `claude_desktop`), it also says an Agent started with it runs in the app on the app's own sign-in. That launcher, like the Codex App's, runs no main chat, so it is never the switch. It never spends tokens on its own. The evidence also includes the node's `claude.auth_status` (free; cached per computer per launcher: 10 minutes when signed in, 1 minute when not signed in or no answer (the call failed, `timeout`, `unreadable`), 10 minutes for an old node's `unknown method`): `not_logged_in` counts as a failure (`not_logged_in`). A `claude.ai` sign-in counts as an answer only when there's no other evidence or the newest is `not_logged_in`; it can't override a recognized `auth_failed` / `model_route` / `rate_limited`. Keys, gateway tokens and cloud providers (`api_key`, `api_key_helper`, `oauth_token`, `third_party`) don't count as evidence; with no other evidence, the `unknown` `detail` says "uses an account or key it was set up with, not tried yet". `unknown` doesn't count as evidence.
- `first_message`: `ok` once the main chat has answered (recorded, then always `ok`; a changed main chat counts too); if it never answered and the latest turn failed, `problem` + that turn's code; otherwise `todo` + `never_tried` (`test_assistant`). While `first_message` offers `test_assistant`, an unverified `model` step has no action: the try is one button, on `first_message`, where clients show its spinner and answer; the probe it runs verifies the model. It doesn't affect `mode`.
- `mode`: `setup` when any of `computer`, `claude`, `model` is `todo` or `problem`, except `rate_limited`, `model_fallback_unavailable`, `tool_search_unsupported`, and `upstream_unavailable` (none is a setup step on the machine, so `mode` stays `full`); `unknown` / `checking` don't block.
- `suggestions`: in `setup` only the two `local: true` ones (`what_can_you_do`, `how_to_connect_model`; the client opens local help, nothing goes to the model); in `full` also `largest_folders`, `connect_mail`, with `prompt` (the exact text sent when tapped).
- `probe` is `POST /api/v1/launchers/{name}/check`'s `{ok, agent, model, answer, millis, error, assistant_turn?}` on the main chat's computer. If the computer step is not `ok` (including `machine_pending`), `?probe=1` sends no probe and the response omits `probe`. When the computer didn't answer (offline, timeout) only `error` is present; such results are not recorded and not used as model evidence. When the launcher's health record on that computer is failing, an answered probe also updates it: a pass clears it, a failure other than a single timeout updates the check time of a record still in force; without a failing record nothing is kept.
- What the probe checks: the main chat's next turn as a message would run it (the chat's kept pick, else Model configuration › Main chat, a launcher that can't run it given way, as the send path resolves it; nothing is kept, started or switched), through the node's `launchers.check` with `assistant_turn: true`, `model`, `effort`, `conversation` (the main chat) and `config_dir` (the profile Main chat starts new chats in). A pick the message would be refused on is the probe's `error`, with nothing run or recorded; so is a pick on an external adapter's launcher, which no `launchers.check` can try (the node refuses it, `adapter_probe_unsupported`), and the first message is not counted as answered. The record keeps the launcher, `model` and `effort` it checked; one checked for another model is never reused for a probe and its pass never clears the step's failure.
- Scheduled tasks: a run that comes due first computes readiness with the same rules (no probe). If a step this run needs is blocking, it isn't sent; the run record has `status: "skipped"`, `not_ready: true`, and `error` "Your computer or model isn’t set up yet, so this one was skipped", with no push. These skips, including temporary sleep / offline cases, neither count toward nor reset a failure streak. **Run Now** and one-off tasks don't check (a one-off closes when due, so a skip would lose it).
- Storage: the latest result, `dismissed`, the latest probe, chat start refusals, the main chat having answered once, and scheduled tasks waiting for readiness (`routines_waiting`) are stored in Postgres `settings` under `assistant.readiness`; nothing is written when the result is unchanged (ignoring `checked_at`, but retaining `occurrence` changes). No events are pushed; clients re-fetch when entering the Persona tab, after pairing succeeds, after adding / confirming a computer, after saving a provider, and on `machines` changes.

## Origin of assistant conversations (`origin`)

Assistant conversations (sessions with `assistant: true`) carry `origin`: who opened the chat. The hub records it when the chat is opened (the assistant's settings `assistant.origins`: session id → origin, `origin_ref`, start time),
and fills it into the session lists sent to clients through the snapshot (`SessionView.origin` / `origin_ref`) (`sessions` / `sessions_delta` pushes, `GET /api/v1/sessions`, `conversations` in `GET /api/v1/assistant`).
Once recorded, the origin never changes; Agent sessions (`assistant: false`) don't carry it. The hub includes `conversation_origin` in features.

| `origin` | Opened by | `origin_ref` | Sidebar |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` (or absent) | The user creating one in the web app (including the main chat, and ones opened with **Hand to AI** in the Inbox or a Lark chat) | — | Recent, no mark (All Chats: Mine) |
| `channel` | The user sending `/new` in a channel such as the Lark bot or WeChat | Channel id (`feishu`, `wechat`…) | Recent, its channel's mark (All Chats: Mine) |
| `inbox` | The handling chat for an Inbox item (AI twin) | Inbox item id | Recent, marked Inbox |
| `task` | Scheduled tasks and follow-ups (`schedule_followup`, including `new_conversation` ones and the own chats of `notify_user`-only `push: "asked"` tasks); also the built-in background supervisor's chat, which has no `origin_ref` | Task id | Recent, marked Scheduled Tasks (not the background supervisor) |
| `spawned` | Opened by another chat with `conversation_new` | Session id of the chat that opened it | Recent, marked Spawned from Chats |
| `lark_agent` | Sending `/agent …` in Lark (the extension via `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations`, `purpose: "lark.agent"`) | Extension id | Recent, Lark's mark |
| `extension` | Opened by another extension via `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` | Extension id | Recent, marked Extensions |

- **`opened_by`** (`SessionView.opened_by`, the session's `opened_by`): the extension whose token opened the chat (`POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` with an extension's token, whatever its `purpose`), by id.
  The assistant notes it when the chat opens, from the extension the hub's auth found for the request (a client's own `X-Persona-*` headers are dropped on the way) and nothing else: not from `origin` or `origin_ref`, and never over the bus (`assistant.start` cannot set it).
  It is absent for every other chat, for the main chat even when an extension opened it, and for chats whose origin the backfill judged: the backfill never sets it.
  A chat made main later (`PUT /api/v1/assistant {"main": …}`) loses it for good, and making another chat main does not bring it back. Only that extension's token may change the chat's permission mode (`agents.permission_mode`); a chat without it is refused.
- Sending into an existing chat doesn't open a new one and isn't an origin: a task continuing in its own chat, quiet-task notifications (`task_notice`) going into the main chat, channel messages to the main chat, `conversation_send`.
- **How clients use it**: absent, empty, `user` and `channel` count as the user's own; everything else counts as an auto chat, including values added later that the client doesn't know (shown as **Other**).
- **Titles**: an auto chat's title is set from the start (no waiting for the first turn, no model call), following "MMDD | kind | topic": Inbox `MMDD | 收件箱 | <the item's title>`, scheduled tasks `MMDD | 定时 | <task name>` (the kind words are emitted in Chinese: 收件箱 = Inbox, 定时 = scheduled).
  `收件箱` is not among the kinds the model may pick (only the hub uses it). Other origins still get a title after the first turn.
  A title an extension gives the chat it opened (`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/rename` with its token) is a hint the model reads, not the title.
- **Only a scoped token makes an extension the opener**: the hub tells the extension apart by its own token (`permissions.hub`).
  An extension that calls with the hub's full token (`hub_api`) is the user as far as the hub can tell: its chats are `user` and carry no source mark, and its renames are the user's.
- **Backfilling chats without an origin**: when the hub sees the session list of the assistant's machine, it fills in assistant chats that have no origin yet (`by: "backfill"`): AI twin sessions recorded on Inbox items → `inbox` (filling the title too);
  chats recorded on tasks (`run_session_id`, sessions in run records) and titles started with `定时` (scheduled) → `task`; a first message starting with the Inbox AI twin / chat-forward / scheduled-task prompt → the matching origin;
  the rest → `user`. It can run repeatedly: already recorded ones are untouched.

### Sidebar

- **Recent** under **Persona Chats** lists every chat by last activity whoever opened it, except the main chat, the archived ones, the built-in background supervisor (in All Chats only) and the scheduled tasks' own chats (`origin == "task"`: they keep their Scheduled Tasks entry and All Chats).
