The heading folds the rows, with the folded / open state kept on the device (default open). The web lists its setting (5 by default) with Show more, and an explicitly chosen count is never reset.
- **A chat Persona opened carries its source's mark** beside the title in the channel mark's place: the icon and name of its All Chats filter where that filter exists (Inbox · Scheduled Tasks · Lark /agent with Lark's mark · Spawned from Chats · Extensions · Other), named in the tooltip. One source mapping decides the mark everywhere, and agrees with the All Chats filter; the same chat has the same mark in Recent, the search results and All Chats.
- **All Chats** has an origin filter at the top (All · Mine · Inbox · Scheduled Tasks · …) and opens on **All** every time: the last pick is not kept (on the web the pick is in the address, `/history/<origin>`, so Back returns to it). Search covers all chats whatever their origin.
- **Conversations an extension opened** (`lark_agent`, `extension`) say so: their rows carry the source's mark as every chat Persona opened does (Lark's for Lark /agent, the extensions symbol otherwise, named "From Lark /agent" / "From an extension"; one mark per row, the origin's over the channel's; the web draws the opening extension's own icon, `opened_by` else `origin_ref`, when that extension is installed with an icon, and name it "From <its name>" while that icon is drawn; the Lark extension's own /agent keeps Lark's mark and words), and the message that opened the chat gets the "From Lark /agent" / "From an extension" line a channel's message has, once the loaded history reaches that first message. A message from a channel keeps its own channel line. `channel` and `user` chats get no origin mark (a channel's chat keeps its channel's).

## Remote images

`GET /api/v1/remote-image?url=<absolute http(s) address>&size=<long side in px>` (the manager's, `remoteimage` behind `assistant/remote_image.go`; feature `remote_images`). The web app loads the pictures an Agent's or the assistant's reply names by address (Markdown `![alt](https://…)`) here instead of from their host: the host sees the manager's address, never a device's, and the web app gets the size it draws. Full devices only (403 otherwise); no extension scope opens it. `url` is read as written in the query, its percent escapes undone and a `+` kept as a plus; escape `&`, `=`, `#` and spaces in it.

- **Sizes**: `size` is rounded up to 256, 512, 768, 1024, 1536 or 2048 (none or 0: 1024). JPEG, PNG, GIF (its first frame) and WebP are decoded, turned upright by their EXIF orientation, scaled to fit `size` × `size` (never enlarged) and encoded again (JPEG, PNG when transparent), which drops their metadata. HEIC and AVIF pass as they are (up to 8 MiB). The type is read from the bytes, never from `Content-Type`; SVG (it can carry scripts) and everything else are refused.
- **Where it fetches**: an `http` / `https` address with a host and no user info, at most 4 KiB. The host is resolved once and every answer must be an ordinary public address (public IPv4, global IPv6; never loopback, private, shared, link-local, ULA, multicast, documentation, transition, NAT64, reserved or a cloud metadata service): one answer that is not refuses the name, and only the checked numbers are dialled (`pinneddial`), so a second DNS answer cannot move the fetch (rebinding). Redirects (at most 3) are checked the same way at every hop. An operator proxy from the environment gets a CONNECT to the checked number, never the name.
- **Behind a fake-IP proxy**: when the machine's resolver answers a name only with a TUN proxy's own addresses (198.18/15, sing-box's fc00::/18; Clash, mihomo and sing-box hand these out in fake-IP mode), the real addresses are asked of a DNS-over-HTTPS service's JSON API (`?name=&type=1|28`, 5 s, kept a minute per host) and go through the same check; they are dialled by number, through the proxy's tunnel. A failed or empty lookup refuses the picture (`address_not_allowed`): a fake address is never let through. The service is the manager's `manager.json` `remote_images.doh` (default `https://dns.alidns.com/resolve`; `""` turns the lookup off), and it learns the host names of the pictures looked up this way.
- **What it sends**: no cookies, no credentials, a generic User-Agent, and no Referer, except one retry naming the picture's own origin (`https://<host>/`) when the host answers 401 or 403 without one (hotlink protection; it tells the host nothing it does not know).
- **Limits**: 20 MiB per source (`Content-Length` checked first), 40 megapixels, 15 s per fetch, 6 fetches and 2 decodes at once, the same picture fetched once however many ask, 60 fetches a minute per device (what is cached costs nothing; over it: 429 with `Retry-After`), a failed address answered from memory for 2 minutes.
- **Cache**: the sources and every size drawn, in the manager's `cache/remote-images/` (a cache: it may be deleted at any time), at most 512 MiB, the least recently used dropped first.
- **Answer**: the picture with its own `Content-Type`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`; or a JSON error with `code`: `bad_url` (400), `address_not_allowed` (403), `too_large` (413), `unsupported_type` (415), `bad_image` (422), `rate_limited` (429), `fetch_failed` (502), `timeout` (504).

## Avatars

One protocol for every picture of a person or a conversation the web app shows; the web app never reaches a third party for one.

- **The value a source gives**: one string, `avatar`, wherever a source names a picture (a connector's Inbox thing, `InboxThing.avatar`). `https://…` is an address on the open internet that the manager fetches; anything else is one of the source's own media refs, whose bytes its extension gives (a connector's `Media(ref)`, the same refs its conversation page carries). An `http://` address, or a value over 2 KiB, is none. A value names fixed bytes: a changed picture gets a new value (a new ref, a new address, or a version in it), which is what makes caching for good safe.
- **What the web app gets**: the manager lists the hub path in `avatar_url`, `/api/v1/avatars/{source}/{value as unpadded base64url}` (`extwire.AvatarURL`). Inbox items list `connector.avatar_url`; the stored item keeps the source value. Connector thread pages list optional `avatar_url` on `chat`, `chat.author` and each message's `sender`. Their existing `avatar` fields still carry the original values. A thread page's legacy ref loads through `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/media?ref=`. A missing or unavailable picture shows the initial.
- **Messaging extensions**: a checked account, conversation, person or profile retains its original `avatar`. The manager also supplies `avatar_url` for a public HTTPS address or a registered source's `media/<key>`. Messaging paths include `messaging=1`; local media also names the effective opaque `account` for multi-account sources. Two accounts can share a media key and return different originals. When one ID names both a messaging source and a connector, the marker selects the messaging source. Each manager caches the original under the source and account and draws the requested sizes from that original. An uninstalled source's avatar cache is removed.
- **Feishu**: a listed Feishu Inbox item, gateway chat, member, user profile or account carries `avatar_url` beside its original picture. A chat message carries `sender_avatar_url`. Keys, legacy `/agent/v1/media/` and `/api/media/` paths, and recognised Feishu CDN static-resource links all resolve through the registered Lark gateway. The path includes the numbered gateway slot as `lark_account`; the signed-in user's identity in `account_id` is a different value. A page with the default slot pins the gateway read to the slot it resolved. The manager rounds the four output buckets up to Lark's nearest multiples of 24 (72, 144, 264, 528 pixels), keeps inputs for each slot and size separately, and draws them again before serving.
- **`GET /api/v1/avatars/{source}/{value}?size=<px>`** (the extension manager's, `extmgr/avatars.go`): full devices only (403 otherwise); no extension scope opens it. `{source}` is an installed connector, enabled messaging source or registered Feishu gateway (404 otherwise; a connector ref also needs its `threads`). Stateless: the value is in the path. `size` is rounded up to 64, 128, 256 or 512 (none: 128). The picture is decoded, turned upright, scaled to fit (never enlarged) and encoded again (JPEG, PNG when transparent), which drops its metadata and anything that is not the picture: an extension's bytes are never served as they came. A ref whose bytes the connector's conversation page kept (`cache/connector-media/`) is drawn from them, signed out too.
- **Fetching an address**: `remoteimage`'s Avatars profile, the checks of "Remote images" with these limits: `https` only, at the start and at every redirect (at most 3); every answer for the host public, the checked numbers dialled (no rebinding), a fake-IP proxy's names through the same DoH (`manager.json` `remote_images.doh`); no cookies, credentials or Referer; PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF (its first frame) only, read from the bytes (HEIC, AVIF, SVG and everything else refused); 4 MiB per source, 16 megapixels, 10 s per fetch. An extension's bytes are held to the same types and sizes.
- **Limits**: a device may start 300 fetches a minute; only fetches count (a picture from the cache, or another size drawn from a kept source, costs nothing), so a screen of new rows loads whole. The same picture is fetched once however many ask; a value that failed is answered from memory for 2 minutes.
- **Cache**: the manager keeps connector pictures in `cache/avatars/<source>/` and messaging pictures in `cache/avatars/_messaging-<source>/`. Gateway pictures live in `cache/avatars/_lark-<plugin>/` and are dropped when that plugin is removed. The sources can be removed independently, even when they have the same ID. The shared limit is 256 MiB, with the least recently used dropped first. A new picture gets a new value. A source's directory goes with its data (Delete Saved Data).
- **Answer**: the picture with its own `Content-Type`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`; or a JSON error with `code`: `bad_url` (404 for a path that is not an avatar, 400), `address_not_allowed` (403), `too_large` (413), `unsupported_type` (415), `bad_image` (422), `rate_limited` (429, `Retry-After`), `fetch_failed` (502, the connector signed out or failing included), `timeout` (504). The web app draws the initial on any error.
- **The web app**: `Monogram` draws connector Inbox rows and thread senders and authors. It requests the pixels needed for the displayed size from the item's manager and reuses its image cache. The initial stands in for a missing or failed picture.

## Extension entry-list settings

An extension detail whose configuration declares entry lists has an **opted-in projection**. A client that implements the editor adds `entry_lists=1` to `GET /api/v1/extensions/{id}/-/` and to every configuration, secret, enablement, contribution, auto-upgrade, handoff-rule or clear-secret request whose response it uses as a detail. The old `/api/v1/plugins/…` aliases accept the same query. This is a request capability, not a hello feature flag.

- With the query, `form.fields` retains the list's recursive `items` and flat `fields`, its logical `secret`, and `clears_secret: true` on an address whose configured-network target change deletes the entry secret on save. Saved configuration entries carry the host-owned reserved `_id`. A capable configuration write accepts existing IDs unchanged and entries without IDs as new; the response contains their minted IDs. Unknown, duplicated or cross-list IDs are rejected.
- Dynamic secret views use the live entry `_id` as `name` and add `list` and `entry_title`; they carry only the ordinary set state, last-four hint or provider reference. Set, replace, reference and clear use the established `/secrets/{name}` routes after the entry has been saved. Secret plaintext is never returned. Removal or a normalized configured-target change deletes the dynamic secret atomically with configuration.
- Without the query, the response filters entry-list fields from `form.fields` and dynamic rows from `secrets`, but **does not remove their raw `config` arrays**. This prevents a client that has not opted in from presenting an unknown editor or mistaking host metadata for a declared text field. A configuration PUT without `entry_lists=1` calls the preserving write path: current entry arrays replace any omitted or stale arrays in the submitted draft while ordinary scalar edits still save. It cannot add, remove, reorder or rebind entries and cannot delete their secrets.
- An opted-in client making an immediate fixed-field save (for example a machine switch) adds `preserve_entries=1` to the configuration PUT alongside `entry_lists=1`. It selects that same preserving write while keeping the response's entry-capable form and dynamic secret rows. Only a full editor's configuration PUT without this flag may authoritatively change the arrays.

The manifest's `config:<list>[].<field>` permission and logical list-secret declaration cover current and future entries; entry values are not included in the permissions digest. The fixed-slot `x-from` migration and its lossless-or-refused inverse on rollback are part of preview/install, not a client-side transform.

## Extension install, upgrade and uninstall

The synchronous preview, install and upgrade responses include an `operation_id`. Preview requests to
`POST /api/v1/extensions/-/catalog/preview` and `POST /api/v1/extensions/-/preview` accept `"async": true`.
Install and upgrade accept the same flag, and uninstall accepts `?async=1`. These requests return HTTP 202
and the initial `operation` snapshot.

An install or upgrade takes over its preview's operation. A concurrent request for a preview already
being installed receives 409 `installing_already`. The download cache lets a later preview join an
ongoing download if the original request timed out.

## Error reports (feature `error_reports`)

Clients report their errors and crashes only while `features` has `error_reports` (an extension takes them). Without it they send nothing, and drop what they kept.

`POST /api/v1/error-reports` (full device credentials; not pairing tokens or extension tokens)

```json
{"reports": [{"id": "4f0c…", "source": "web", "kind": "exception", "level": "error", "time": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z",
  "release": "1.4.0", "build": "512", "os": "macos", "os_version": "15",
  "message": "TypeError: x is undefined",
  "exceptions": [{"type": "TypeError", "value": "…",
    "frames": [{"function": "load", "module": "inbox", "file": "/assets/inbox.js", "line": 88, "in_app": true}]}],
  "breadcrumbs": [{"time": "…", "category": "navigation", "message": "inbox", "level": "info"}],
  "tags": {"mechanism": "onerror"}, "previous_launch": true}]}
```

- `ErrorReport` in `schema/extension/protocol.schema.json` is the format; `source` is the client's own (`web`); `hub` and `manager` are refused. `fingerprint`, `count` and `received_at` are the manager's: what a client sends there is ignored.
- At most 20 reports and 256 KB a request (400 beyond). `202 {"enabled": true, "accepted": n, "dropped": m}`: dropped are invalid, repeated (same `id`), folded (the same problem within 10 minutes) or over the rate limit; none of them should be sent again. `200 {"enabled": false, "accepted": 0}`: the feature is off; nothing was kept.
- **What clients put in**: no user content (message text, mail, documents, prompts, notification bodies, file names the user chose), no device ids, account, hub address or machine names; breadcrumbs carry short code-chosen text (a route's name, a route pattern). The manager scrubs again whatever slips through.
- **Keeping and retrying**: a client keeps reports locally until it gets a 2xx (a crash is written before the page dies and sent at the next load with `previous_launch`), at most 50 for at most 7 days, and makes each report's `id` once so a retry is recognized.

## REST (client → hub)

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines` | `{"machines":[Machine]}`. A Machine from a current manager has `clipboard: {supported, enabled, reason?, reason_code?}` (clipboard sharing; `reason` in the reader's language when it can't share) |
| GET | `/api/v1/navigation` | `{"start"?, "pages"?, "overview"?}`: the page the web app opens on, the sidebar's arrangement and Overview's extension cards with its own sections, one per hub, so the owner's for all their devices; each is left out until something is stored, see "Navigation" |
| PUT | `/api/v1/navigation` | `{start?, pages?, overview?}` → the record; `full` only; none of them, or one of another shape, returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/workspaces` | `{workspaces:[Workspace],errors?:[{machine_id,error}]}`; workspace discovery independent of Agents, keeps the last known info on failure |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/reconnect` | Reconnect that machine's node |
| GET · POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/codex/{sid}/takeover` | Signed-in full-device route; generic device-call APIs are denied. GET → `{token,cwd,transcript_path,continuation_prompt}` with a single-use two-minute token. POST requires `{token,confirm_stop:true}` only while the original writer is running; `false` is accepted once it has exited. The manager verifies process identity and terminal instance, then sends one Ctrl+D only with empty composer and no modal or queued input. It waits for process exit, a complete stable transcript ending, and a fresh writer scan; any failed check or timeout refuses. No signals or forced termination. Takeover resumes the same thread/session ID in a new terminal tab. The separate continue option alone starts an independent session with context and attached to-do preserved. `encrypted_context` is continuation-only. |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{id}/confirm` · `…/reject` | Confirm / reject a computer waiting for confirmation (feature `machine_trust`, "Computer trust" below); only accepts a signed-in full device or the main token (a temporary identity from a pairing code gets 403) → `{"ok":true}`. confirm: confirming an already-confirmed one is also 200, unknown machine 404; reject only works on pending ones (already confirmed 409 `not_pending`, unknown 404) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes` | The terminal browser tree (feature `terminal_panes`, `full` only): `{hosts:[{kind, stream, control, new_tab, workspaces:[{id,label,number?,cwd?,branch?}], tabs:[{id,workspace_id,label,number?}], panes:[{pane, terminal, tab_id, workspace_id, agent?, status?, title?, cwd?, session_id?}]}]}`; includes shell panes with no Agent. `terminal` is the terminal-stream address `pane:<pane>`, `session_id` is the Agent session running in that pane (use it to open the terminal when present) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes` | `{workspace_id, kind?}`: open a new shell tab in this space (doesn't steal focus on the computer; the directory is the space's own, the request cannot set it) → `{pane, terminal, tab_id}`; `full` only, called only when the user taps |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes/close` · `…/panes/split` · `…/panes/agent` · `…/panes/git` · `…/tabs/close` · `…/tabs/rename` | Terminal node menu actions, `full` only: `{pane}` closes a pane; `{pane, direction: right\|down}` splits → `{pane, terminal}`; `{pane, launcher}` starts an Agent in a shell pane → `{session_id}`; `{op: pull\|push\|fetch, pane \| workspace_id+kind?}` → `{op, outcome, message, output?}` (`outcome`: `fetched`, `up_to_date`, `pulled`, `nothing_to_push`, `pushed`, which clients say in their language; refusals are 409s with `code` `no_directory`, `not_a_repository`, `detached_head`, `no_upstream`, `uncommitted_changes`, `not_fast_forward`, `push_rejected`, `pull_failed`, `push_failed` or `fetch_failed`, the hub's sentence in the request's language and the node's words, git's included, as `detail`; `git/pull` refuses with the same codes); `{tab_id, kind?}` closes a tab; `{tab_id, label, kind?}` renames a tab. Only these fields are accepted; a directory or command cannot be specified |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes/close_finished` | **Close finished terminals**: closes the terminals stopped Agents left (panes Persona opened for a session, no Agent in them now, only shells in front, checked again on the node); `{"panes"?: "<pane id>,…"}` limits it to the ones the user confirmed, `{"preview": true}` lists them and closes nothing → `{"closed":[{pane,session_id,tab_id,workspace_id}],"kept":[{…,why}],"preview"}`. Full devices only; nothing calls it on a timer |
| GET · POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/doctor` · `…/doctor/fix` | The machine page's **What This Computer Can Do**, `full` only: GET is read-only and returns the `personad node doctor --json` report `{ok, dir, checks:[{name, status: ok\|warn\|fail, state, detail, hint, items}], fixed}`; POST rewrites the files Persona generated itself (same path as `--fix`), checks again, and returns the new report. An explicit `Accept-Language` is forwarded as the node RPC's optional `locale`, so a new node's human `detail` / `hint` / human `items` use the page's language; without the header the hub keeps the legacy request and report. An old node ignores `locale` and its report passes through unchanged. An old node without the RPC returns 502 `unknown method node.doctor` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/diagnosis?sections=processes,disk,tools` | What is using this computer, `full` only (an extension's token 403 `read_only`): `Diagnosis` `{machine_id, at, processes?:{mem_total, count, groups:[{name, kind: agent\|engine\|persona\|other, count, rss, cpu?}]}, disk?:{volumes:[{mount, used, total}], folders:[{path, bytes}], partial, caches:[{id, path, bytes, in_use}]}, tools?:[{id, version}]}`. `sections` left out or empty asks for all; a section is present when it was asked for and the computer can answer it (Windows answers tools only). Paths are `~`-relative, process groups are names only (never arguments or environment). Errors `{error, code}`: unknown machine 404 `not_found`; unknown section 400 `bad_request`; offline 503 `machine_offline`; a node without capability `machine_diagnose` 409 `node_outdated`; no answer within 30 s 504 `deadline`; any other node failure 502 `diagnosis_failed`. |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/cleanup` | Empties rebuildable caches: body `{"ids":["go-build", …]}` (ids of the fixed catalog only, never a path) → `CleanupResult` `{freed_bytes, available_before, available_after, items:[{id, bytes, status: cleaned\|in_use\|missing\|failed, error?}]}`; `freed_bytes` is the home volume's available space after minus before, never below 0. Same role and errors as `…/diagnosis` (empty or unknown ids 400 `bad_request`), waiting up to 120 s |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/prepare` · `…/worktree/create` | **New Worktree…**, `full` only: `{workspace_id, kind?}` → `{root, repoName, branch, path}` (repo top level, repo name, the workspace's current branch, the directory the host puts checkouts of this repo in: herdr's configured one, Orca's default workspace directory, Paseo's worktrees folder for the repository); `{workspace_id, branch, path, kind?}` → `{workspace_id, tab_id?, pane?, terminal?, path, branch}`: checks out the branch if it exists, otherwise creates it from the workspace's HEAD, and opens it as a herdr workspace or an Orca worktree under the source one (Orca picks the folder from its own setting and names it after the path's last element; the answer's `path` is where it is), or has Paseo make it as a Paseo workspace (the path must be in the folder prepare returned, and its last element is taken as Paseo names a folder, see `worktree.create` below); the path must be absolute and either not exist or be an empty directory; never forces, never deletes. Each host in `panes` gains a `worktree` boolean. The hub sends the request's language as `locale` (the body's, else its `Accept-Language`, else the user's) to every worktree action that takes one (`prepare`, `create`, `source`, `preset`, `delete`, `add`, `rename`): the node words its refusals in it |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/add` · `…/worktree/status` · `…/worktree/remove` | A new agent's own worktree, `full` only: `{cwd, branch?, name_hint?, kind?, locale?}` → `{path, branch, root, workspace_id?}` (`git worktree add` from the folder's repository on `persona/<slug of name_hint>`, made unique, under the checkouts directory; opens no workspace); `{cwd, kind?}` → `{worktree, ours, path?, branch?, root?, main_branch?, checkouts?, dirty, unmerged}` (`checkouts`: where a new agent's worktree of this repository goes); `{path, kind?, delete_branch?:bool, force?:bool}` → `{removed, branch_deleted}`. `kind` is the engine that makes the worktree and says whether it is Persona's: the one the agent opens in (New Agent's `status` and `add`) or ran in (`status` and `remove` when it is closed: the session's `host`); omitted, the computer's default engine. On Paseo Paseo makes it as a workspace of its own, in its own folder (`workspace_id` is that workspace); `status` calls it Persona's (`ours`) only when it is the folder of a worktree workspace Paseo made (`owned`), and `remove` then has Paseo archive that workspace, which removes the folder, never while a session in the workspace is running (`worktree_in_use`, as for an Agent in the folder; the client tries again a few times while the closed Agent leaves Paseo's list), with `force` for changes and an unmerged branch as for herdr, the branch deleted after the folder. Removing the bare checkout would leave Paseo a workspace in a folder that is gone. 409 `not_a_repository`, `not_our_worktree` (not one of Persona's, or a folder inside one), `worktree_in_use` (a live agent's folder is in it), `worktree_dirty` (`dirty`), `worktree_unmerged` (`unmerged`, `main_branch`), `worktree_failed` (git's reason); `force` removes uncommitted work and an unmerged branch, and a client sends it only after the user confirmed |
| PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/engine` | `{"engine":"herdr"\|"herdr-core"\|"herdr-both"\|"orca"\|"tern"\|"rex"\|"paseo"\|"cindy"\|"t3code"}` → 200 with the updated Machine; unknown engine 400 `{"error"}`, unknown machine 404. Works while offline too (stored, takes effect on connect); `machines` is pushed as usual afterwards ("Engine" below) |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/botmux` | PUT `{"on":bool}` → 200 `{"on"}`; GET also returns `{"on"}`. **Also Show botmux Sessions**: stored per machine; if never set, uses `machines[].botmux` from hub.json, otherwise on; works while offline, and a PUT sends `node.configure {"botmux", "claude_dirs"}` right away (the hub adds `claude_dirs` to every `node.configure` that names neither it nor `keep_sessions`, so the node keeps its directories). Missing `on` 400 |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/herdr` | "Start herdr automatically when needed" under **Settings › Machines › Engine**: GET → `{autostart, running, known, installing?, install_error?}` (`known` says whether the node can tell if herdr is running); if the machine is online and the last check is more than 3 seconds old, it first asks the node's `herdr.server.status`; PUT `{"autostart": bool}` changes the switch, sends `node.configure {"herdr_autostart", "claude_dirs"}` when online (`claude_dirs` so the node keeps its directories), and returns the same as GET: missing `autostart` 400, engine not `herdr` / `herdr-both` 404, can't save 500 |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/herdr/start` | The "Start" button next to "herdr isn't running" in the Agents list: the node's `herdr.server.start` (waits up to 40 seconds) → `{autostart, running, known: true}`; node too old or the call fails 502 ("Engine" below) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/computer` | Whether this Mac has Cua Driver right now and can be controlled by the assistant (the hub asks the node's `computer.status` on the spot) → 200 `Computer` (`{enabled, installed, version?, daemon, accessibility?, screen_recording?, desktop?, screen_sharing, displays?, ready, note?, job?}`; `displays`: the Mac's display arrangement while Screen Sharing answers); plugin `cua` not enabled, or not a Mac → 404 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/computer` | `{"enabled"?: bool, "no_auto_lock"?: bool, "screen_x264"?: bool}`: the machine page's **Let the Assistant Control This Computer** switch, written to `machines` in the `cua` plugin config, and its per-Mac switches, written to the config's lists of the same names (`no_auto_lock`: keep this Mac from locking on idle while the extension is on; `screen_x264`: "x264 on a direct LAN") → 200 `Computer`; plugin not enabled or not a Mac → 404. `machines` is pushed as usual afterwards |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/computer/{install\|grant\|cancel}` | The machine page's **Install Cua Driver**, **Grant Access**, **Cancel**: the node runs it in the background (`computer.install` / `computer.grant` / `computer.cancel`), → 200 `Computer`, progress is in its `job` (`{kind, state: running\|done\|failed\|cancelled, step?, error?, started}`), and the page keeps polling with GET. Plugin not enabled for this machine 404; offline, a job already running, or node too old 409 |
| GET / DELETE | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/computer/apps`, `…/computer/apps/{bundle}`, `…/computer/apps/revoke/{bundle}` | The machine page's **Apps Allowed for the Assistant**: GET → `{"apps":[{bundle_id, name, at}],"manager"}`; DELETE removes the saved approval by its identifier and returns the remaining list (future prompts follow `app_approval`); can't save 500. Optional `?expected_manager=<manager id>`: the hub checks it against the manager it relays to (409 `machine_owner_changed`) and acknowledges a successful answer with `X-Persona-Computer-Apps-Owner`. The guarded `…/apps/revoke/{bundle}` requires it (428 `expected_manager_required`); the hub relays it to the manager as the plain DELETE |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/browser` | This Mac's ego lite (plugin `ego`): GET asks the node's `browser.status` on the spot → `Browser` (`{enabled, installed, version?, set_up, imported, analytics?, ready, note?, screen_sharing, displays?, job?}`); PUT `{"enabled": bool}` is the machine page's switch (the plugin's `machines`). Plugin not enabled or not a Mac → 404 |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/browser/{install\|open\|cancel}` | The machine page's **Install ego lite**, **Open ego lite**, **Cancel**: the node runs it in the background, progress is in `job`. Plugin not enabled for this machine 404; offline, a job already running, or node too old 409 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/launchers?purpose=` | `{"launchers":[Launcher], "default":{provider, model, effort}}`: a Persona-managed provider's entry carries its `display_name` (absent when it has none, and on rc-file, built-in and PATH launchers; feature `launcher_auto_name`), which clients show over `name`. `default` is the effective value for this purpose in **Model Settings** (`purpose` defaults to `agent.new`; the main chat's picker passes `assistant`), `provider` is the launcher name (clients look its title up in `launchers`, as for `tiers[].launcher`), and the client shows "Default: …". For purposes that are not launcher-based, `default` is null. For `agent.new` only, `tiers` `[{name, launcher, model?, effort?, description?}]` and `tiers_profile` `{id, name}`: the Agent presets, the tiers of the model profile in use whose launcher this computer has (its `launchers`), by name; absent with no profile in use or none to offer; for `assistant` / `task`, `unavailable` `[{name, display_name?, kind, agent?, api?, code, reason}]` (feature `assistant_model_pick`): what the main chat can't run on this computer, with `reason` in the request's language: the computer's launchers whose agent or engine can't run assistant chats (`code` `not_main_chat`), then Settings › Model providers' providers that can't here: a direct API speaking Responses or Chat Completions (`api_protocol`, `api` names it), an agent that can't (`not_main_chat`), out of this computer's device scope (`launcher_out_of_scope`) or skipping a computer with its own sign-in (`launcher_own_service`); `kind` is `launcher` or `api`. Hidden launchers are never in it; `[]` when nothing is. For `agent.new` (and no `purpose`), `unavailable` in the same shape lists only the Persona-managed providers in this computer's scope that their own-service rule leaves out here (`launcher_own_service`), so New Agent's picker can say why one is missing; absent when there are none. `?purpose=task` uses the same assistant-compatible list with computer-scoped scheduled-task defaults; ordinary `purpose=assistant` retains its own effective default. |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/launchers/{name}/models?refresh=1` | The models this launcher's CLI lists in `/model` (choosing a model for a new Agent): `{"agent","models":[{"id","name","description"?,"resolved"?,"default"?,"efforts"?,"default_effort"?,"service_tiers"?,"custom"?,"price"?,"aliases"?}],"locked"?}`. `id` is the value to put in `model` when starting a session; `default` is the one that runs when no model is given (picking it is the same as not picking); `resolved` is what an alias (opus…) maps to under this launcher's settings; `efforts` are the reasoning efforts it supports, weakest to strongest; `service_tiers` is the model's native Codex `serviceTiers` metadata as `[{id, name, description?}]`, absent when the model or the node does not supply it (clients never infer speed support from a model name); `price` is an exact built-in catalog entry's global standard USD reference price per one million tokens (`input`, `output`, optional `cache_read`, `cache_write` for a 5-minute cache write and `cache_write_1h` for a 1-hour one, which takes `cache_write`'s price when absent), omitted for unknown, inherited or input-size-tiered prices and never treated as the gateway's own quote; `aliases` are the other spellings the manager folded into this row because they run the same model with the same context window on this launcher (Claude Code's tier aliases on a gateway provider whose tiers name one model; never across routes or windows, never the `default` row): each still counts as this launcher's model wherever a model is checked, a saved pick naming one keeps working, and clients match a saved model and the search against them; `locked` is the reason the launcher hard-codes its own `--model`, so picking has no effect. Agents with no list to ask (compatible Codex forks, runtime ones) return `models: []`. `agy` on herdr is discovered through the local `agy models` launcher, with the usual cache and refresh behavior. The node starts the CLI once to ask (a few seconds) and caches for 10 minutes; `refresh=1` asks again. An optional `host` selects the catalog for an Agent start in that engine. Use `host=agy` for the catalog of an existing Antigravity companion session. Omitting the host uses the machine's default, and `purpose=assistant` uses the Assistant catalog. If it can't list them, 502 `{"error"}`; if this computer's node doesn't have the feature yet, 404 `{"error","code":"node_outdated"}` (the web app hides the model row). After the CLI's own entries come the model IDs the user typed for this launcher on this computer before and that ran (`custom: true`, most recent first, at most 8, without the ones the list already has; no `efforts`: they aren't known; none for a `locked` launcher or an agent other than Claude Code / Codex) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/launchers/{name}/models/custom?model=<id>` | Forget one typed model ID of this launcher on this computer (the list row's "Forget") → `{"ok":true}`; forgetting one that isn't remembered is also 200; a `model` that isn't a model ID (`proto.ValidModelID`) 400; full-access devices only (403 for a read-only role, extensions can't call it) |
| GET | `/api/v1/model-config/providers/{id}/models?refresh=1&machine=` | The `/model` list of a launcher-type provider (`launcher.<name>`) in model settings: the same response as the row above (with the IDs typed on that computer, `custom: true`), plus `machine` (which one was asked). It picks one of the online computers that have this launcher: the one named by `machine`, the assistant's, the hub's own, then the rest. Unknown provider, or a plugin / API-type provider 404; all computers that have it offline 503; node too old 404 `node_outdated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/launchers/presets` | Provider presets supplied by plugins `{"presets":[{id, plugin, name, description?, kind, api?, base_url, model?, small_model?, models?…}]}` (`id` is `<extension>/<provider>`), picked under "Add from plugin" when adding a provider; an empty list when plugins can't be reached |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/test` | Test connection, without going through a node: `{name?, base_url?, auth?, api_key?, headers?, model}` → always 200 `{ok, ms, model, error?, code?, auth?}`. `code` identifies a recognized failure: `region_blocked` (Anthropic's region refusal, 403 `{"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"Request not allowed"}}`; another key will not help), `auth`, `not_found` (the endpoint is absent), `model_not_found` (a 400 / 404 body says the selected model is absent or unavailable to this key although the gateway is reachable, including an Anthropic 404 `not_found_error` whose message starts `model:`), `quota_exhausted` (HTTP 402), `wrong_protocol`, `timeout` or `unsupported_effort`. A client that does not recognize a code displays `error`; codes are additive. With `name`, unset fields come from that stored provider; if `base_url` differs from the stored one, the stored key and headers are not sent. The key goes in one header: `auth` `api_key` → `x-api-key`, `bearer` → `Authorization: Bearer`, left out → the stored provider's (or preset's) method, or both headers when neither is named; a stored Codex / Antigravity launcher always gets both; `auto` tries Bearer, then `x-api-key` on 401 / 403, and a success answers `auth` with the one that worked (feature `launcher_auth_auto`). Responses and Chat Completions always send Bearer |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/discover` | Fetch models: same request as above (without `model`; with an optional `agent`, the agent a provider not saved yet runs) → always 200 `{models:[{id, name?, context_window?, max_output_tokens?, efforts?, all_efforts?, default_effort?, no_effort?, image_input?, tool_calls?, inherited_from?, price?}], error?, code?}`; `auth` as for the test, but the answer never names the method found (a model list may not check the key). `inherited_from` is the catalog id an unlisted newer generation took a missing window or thinking level from; `price` is present only on exact catalog entries and is never inherited; `code` as above. The rest is what the gateway's list or its `/v1/model-capabilities` report said, each omitted when it said nothing: `max_output_tokens` the reply limit; `efforts` stays within low…max (the levels as Claude Code takes them) and `all_efforts` adds the gateway's own words (`none`, `minimal`, `ultra`) when it named one; `no_effort: true` the model takes no thinking level, unlike an empty `efforts`, which is unknown; `image_input` / `tool_calls` whether it takes images and tools. Models the gateway marks as no chat model are left out. All of them are optional and kept with a provider's `models` when it is saved; a model sent back naming none of them keeps the stored ones, one that names any of them is saved as sent |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/catalog` | Built-in catalog lookup for model ids typed by hand, without a gateway, a key or stored state: `{ids:[string]}` → always 200 `{models:[{id, name?, context_window?, efforts?, default_effort?, inherited_from?, price?}]}` (`[]` when none is known; `price` as in the launcher's models list above, on exact entries only). Each id is trimmed, empty ones skipped and duplicates answered once, in request order; `id` is the id as sent (trimmed); an id is matched as discovery matches it (any case, a vendor prefix, `[1m]`, a date suffix; `inherited_from` as above) and left out when the catalog fills nothing for it (an unlisted id ending in `[1m]` still gets the 1M window, as in discovery). More than 100 ids, an id over 200 bytes, or a body that isn't `{ids:[string]}` 400; a body over 1 MiB 413 `too_large` |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/import/parse` | Read a pasted configuration (shell alias or exports, Claude Code `settings.json`, a `curl` request, a cindy v1 provider, a provider import link with `launcher_import_link`) into provider drafts for the wizard, without a computer or stored state (feature `launcher_import_parse`): `{text}` → always 200 `{format, drafts, notes}` (shapes under "Model providers and per-purpose configuration" above). No `text` or only blanks 400; over 256 KiB 413 `too_large` |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/{name}/check?machine=` | Test availability: actually sends a request → `{machine, check:{ok, agent?, model?, answer?, millis, error?}}`; an unknown `machine` uses the assistant's machine, and 400 if there is none; API-type providers managed by Persona are requested by the manager directly and return `{check}` without `machine` |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/{name}/restore` | Unhide a launcher from `~/.zshrc` → `{"ok":true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/launchers/{name}/uses` | What still names the launcher as its own, in words for the hide confirmation: Model configuration's purposes (extensions' too), scheduled tasks, model profiles and their tiers → `{"uses":[…]}`. Hiding an rc-file launcher only takes it out of the pickers; these keep running on it |
| GET | `/api/v1/launchers/{name}/quota?machine=&refresh=1` | Quota: `{machine, checked_at, quota}`, or `{machine, checked_at, error, unsupported}` when it can't be checked (still 200); that computer offline 503, no such launcher 502; cached for one minute, `refresh=1` re-reads |
| GET | `/api/v1/launchers/health?state=&machine=` | Launcher health-check records `{"records":[{machine, launcher, agent?, state, kind?, error?, model?, millis?, checked_at, source, fails?, repairs?, repair?, blocked_reason?, resets_at?, limit_models?, limit_resets?}]}`, filterable by state and computer |
| POST | `/api/v1/launchers/health/check?machine=&launcher=` | Check now: with no parameters checks all online computers, returns this run's `{"records":[…]}`, waits up to 10 minutes |
| GET | `/api/v1/todos` | All to-dos (newest first): `{"todos":[Todo]}`, each with `spaces` and `agents` (dismissed filtered out; current ones first by `linked_at` descending, then past participants by `released_at` descending); a to-do waiting for the owner also has `ask: {"outcome"?, "verdict", "recommend"?, "asked_at", "risk"?}`, the same as its `brief` item's `accept[]` row but for `risk`, gone once nothing waits; `risk` (additive, the list's alone: a `brief` row has none) is how risky answering it is: `open` when it cannot be undone or other people will see it (`why_owner` `irreversible` or `visible_to_others`, or the recommendation would be taken at a `deadline` that cannot be undone, also once that deadline was handled and `deadline` is no longer listed), else `safe`, and the view's decision reads it; when absent, clients read it as `open`; a decision (`outcome` `decide`) also has, all additive, `question` (what is to be decided), `why_owner` (`irreversible`, `visible_to_others`, `priority`, `acceptance`, `only_owner_knows`), `options: [{"label","leads_to"}]` (2 to 4, the recommended first), `cost_of_waiting`, `from: {"conversation","title"?,"main"?,"at","message"?,"by_assistant"?,"started_by"?}` and `stands` (where the task came from and where it stands, as the hub knows them) with `background` (both in one line, in the request's language), `deadline` (RFC 3339) with `default` (`taken`: the recommendation is taken at `deadline`; `never`: it is never taken by default, and `deadline`, when present, only reminds), `responses` (the fixed answers the accept route takes: `decide_yourself`, `not_what_i_asked`, `explain_first`) `response` (the fixed answer already given while it still waits) and `for_briefing` (`true` while a decision that can wait is held for the next briefing and nothing was pushed for it), and optionally `suggestion` (`RuleSuggestion`, "Tasks and the chat feed": the owner gave this go-ahead for this directory three times); an open task whose latest review and supervision state are `needs_user` also has `decision_review: {"review_at","dismissal_id"?}` (`review_at` is the latest review's `at`, not `ask.asked_at`; `dismissal_id` persists only for that review). A new review restores visibility; legacy note-only reviews keep their original explanation without invented choices. Dismissal storage read failure returns 503; a task the hub judged also has `check: {"verdict", "reason", "at", "work_since"}`, its latest automatic completion check, gone once the to-do is reopened or one of its Agents starts a new turn; a closed to-do whose code work went no further than its `stage` with nothing left to deploy also has `stage_done: true` (additive), and the clients end its stage strip with Done there instead of a current step; an open to-do nobody works on also has `orphaned: {"reason", "since"}` (`reason` `error`: its Agent ended on a model error and is closed, `closed`: its Agents' tabs are closed, `offline`: its Agent's computer is not connected; `since` RFC 3339, when the manager first saw it so), present while every Agent on it is closed or offline with no wake or continuation pending and absent otherwise; clients that do not know it ignore it. From a manager that names `todo_view`, every row also has `view` (`TodoSummary` in `schema/wire/todo-view.schema.json`: its phase, section, reason, line 2 as a key with string arguments, the times it began and next changes by time alone, the Inactive mark, its asks, its steps and its rank in its section; each ask also has `risk`, `safe` or `open`, and `lockscreen`, `answer` or `open_only` exactly when `open`, and a run's ask whose pending card the manager holds has that card's kind and its id as `interaction` (the session's own card before Persona's about its turn, then the oldest), answered through `POST /api/v1/interactions/{id}/resolve`) and the answer a top-level `counts` (`TodoCounts`: `open`, `needs_you`, `in_progress` and `sections`, every section named); every time in `view` is absolute, so while neither the to-dos nor their runs change (a working run's latest line is in its row's `view`) the list is the same bytes and the merged list's `ETag` holds. Ranks are per manager, so a merged section can hold equal ranks: clients order by `rank`, then `manager`, then `id`. Clients draw a row from its `view` and fall back to their own rules for a row without one (a manager without `todo_view`). `counts` cover every manager only while `features` lists `todo_view`: without it they may be one manager's (an older hub takes them from the default) or the newer managers' alone, so clients count by their own rules. An extension's token (`todos.read`) does not get a to-do it is not shown; every row it gets is a device's, and `counts` are a device's |
| GET | `/api/v1/todos/{id}` | One to-do as `GET /api/v1/todos` lists it, its `view` included → 200 `{"todo": row}`; the view is worked out over the whole list, so its `rank` and steps read as in the list. From a manager that names `todo_timeline` the answer also carries, beside `todo`, what the paper shows of the to-do's history (`TodoItemDetail` in `schema/wire/todo-view.schema.json`; `todo` stays the list's row, read as clients read a row): `rounds`, the rounds the paper shows, oldest first (the latest two that are not Background ones, the latest Background ones making up the rest; `[]` when it has none), `rounds_total` (how many its timeline has in all), `recap` (`TodoRecap`, what changed since `seen_at`; absent when it was never seen or nothing but the owner's own acts came since) and `results` (`TodoResult`s, newest first, at most 3; absent when none), projected from the conversation history; when its history cannot be read all four are left out and the row still answers. `rounds` can leave out Background rounds that began between or after the ones it lists, though `rounds_total` counts them. An extension's token gets the same detail fields where the to-do is visible; a to-do it is not shown answers it 404 `todo_not_found`, as every other route of the to-do does. No push of its own: clients read it again on a `{"type":"todos"}` or an `assistant_feed` whose `item.ref` is the to-do; missing 404 `todo_not_found`; to-dos not loaded yet 503; relayed to the to-do's manager as the other `/api/v1/todos/{id}` routes are. The row carries no `manager` (only the merged list stamps it): clients keep the list row's and send it as `?manager=`, since after a restart the hub knows a to-do's manager only from a list read. A hub or manager without the route answers 405, or 404 with another `code`: that is "not there" and clients keep the list's row; 404 `todo_not_found` is a to-do that is gone (or another manager's) |
| GET | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/images/{image}` | The private bytes of an image attached to the to-do, with validated MIME, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; full and answer-role devices through the same authenticated manager route as the to-do, anonymous callers and extension tokens rejected; missing to-do or image 404 |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos` | Create a to-do `{"title","notes"?,"images"?}` → 200 `{"todo":Todo}`; `title` can't be empty (400); read-only device 403. Each optional image is `{"id","mime","data","name"?}`: a UUID, `image/jpeg` or `image/png`, and base64 of a complete decoded image of that type, at most 1 MiB; at most 50 images. Invalid content 400, oversize or excess 413; the to-do, repository bindings and all images commit atomically. The row's additive `images` metadata has `id`, `mime`, dimensions, manager-relative `url` and optional name/size, never image bytes or a local path. `X-Persona-Op-Id` uses the `todo_create` receipt ("Operation receipts (client_ops)") **only when at least one image is supplied**, replaying the first result without creating twice; an image-less create takes no receipt even with the header |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/todos/{id}` | Edit a to-do `{"title"?,"notes"?,"done"?,"due_at"? \| "due_date"?,"remind_at"?,"priority"?,"project"?,"part_of"?,"after"?}` → 200 `{"todo":Todo}`; only supplied fields change; `part_of` / `after` are checked by the manager (refused 400, `""` / `[]` clear them); `null` (or `""`) clears a due date or reminder, either due field replaces the other; `priority` is `""`, `"high"` or `"low"`; `done: true` marks it done, `false` reopens it; missing 404; read-only device 403 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/todos/{id}` | Delete the to-do and its links (the Agents themselves are untouched) → 200 `{"ok":true}`; missing 404; read-only device 403 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/spaces/{mid}/{space...}` | Attach a whole workspace project to the to-do → 200 `{"ok":true,"linked":N}`; `space` is the URL-encoded project name (caught by the wildcard); done 409, missing 404, read-only device 403 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/spaces/{mid}/{space...}` | Detach the whole group (physically deletes the space-linked Agents for that project under the to-do) → 200 `{"ok":true}`; missing 404, read-only device 403 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/agents/{mid}/{sid}` | Link an existing Agent → 200 `{"ok":true}`; if the same Agent was attached elsewhere, that link is marked released; clears dismissed; done 409, missing 404, read-only device 403. An extension's token: an Agent its computer does not list yet is 409 `agent_not_listed` with `Retry-After` (an Agent just started is answered before its computer lists it: try again), one it is not shown 404 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/agents/{mid}/{sid}/attach` | Attach an available Agent without moving it from another to-do (409 `todo_agent_link_conflict`); attaching it again to the same to-do succeeds without changing the link. Full access only. |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/retry` | Retry a task that failed to start: starts an Agent again on the same to-do according to this task in the plan (machine, directory, prompt, launcher / model, permissions, title); the to-do is reopened immediately (`done_at`, `start_error` cleared, `reopened_at` recorded), this task's `error` in the plan is cleared and `task_plan` is pushed, and the Agent starts in the background → 200 `{"todo":Todo}`. Already reopening or already started is also 200 (returned as is, not started again); if it fails again, `done_at` + `start_error` are written back as usual and the plan's `error` is updated, without appending a second receipt. Target machine offline 409 `“{name}” is offline. Try again once it’s connected.` (to-do unchanged); not a task dispatched by the assistant, or not a start failure (e.g. completed manually) 409, missing 404, read-only device 403. **Unfinished tasks** are not restarted: if an Agent is stuck on a model API error (`turn_error`), it is sent "Continue" and the to-do is returned as is with 200; repeated taps on the same interruption send it only once; that computer offline 409; no interrupted Agent (working, waiting for you…) returns 200 as is and sends nothing. An optional body `{"launcher","model"?}` (feature `task_retry_launcher`) starts a failed start on that launcher of the same computer instead, with `model` or its default model, in the same directory and workspace: the plan task names it from then on, its tier is dropped, its permission mode kept when the launcher runs the same agent as the one that failed and settled again for another agent, its `why` says what changed, and the task's history gets a `start_remedy` item (`by: "user"`, `launcher_from`: the launcher the failed start ran, which a tier or a start-defaults policy may have chosen and the plan task's `error_args.launcher` names, `launcher_to`); checked before the to-do is reopened, a refusal changes nothing: 409 a launcher the computer does not list (naming those it has), one its health record says cannot run there now, one that does not hold a read-only task read-only, and, with nothing started on it, while another start of the task is on its way or once it started since (rather than 200 as is); 400 a `model` without `launcher`, or one that is no model ID. The launcher the plan task names itself (with no tier), or no body, retries on that launcher; then, when the last start stopped on a question in a tab its computer still keeps (`shell_waiting` / `agent_start_stalled` with `kept_until` ahead), the retry starts in that tab (`in_pane`) rather than a new one. A client sends the body only while the hub lists the feature: an older hub ignores it and starts the launcher that failed again |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/start/answer` | `{"choice":"n"}` → 200 `{"todo":Todo}` (feature `todo_start_answer`, see "Answering a start's question"): the answer to the startup question a planned task's failed start stopped on, one of its plan task's `error_args.choices`; the node types it into the kept tab (`start.answer`) and the task starts again in that tab (`in_pane`) as Retry does there, the same to-do reopened at once, and the task's history gets a `start_remedy` item (`action: "answer"`, `by: "user"`, `choice`; `action: "answer_not_typed"` when the node typed nothing, its reply's `typed: false`). `full` only (a read-only or answer-only device, or an extension's token, 403 `read_only`); no short word as `choice` 400; missing 404; machine offline 409. Refused with nothing typed and nothing changed (409, the code's words in the request's language): `start_not_waiting` (not a failed start, or its last start did not stop on a question: it started, is starting again, or the assistant still remedies it), `start_tab_gone` (`kept_until` passed: Retry opens a new tab), `choice_not_offered` (a password prompt is offered `cancel` alone), `node_outdated` (the computer's node has no `start_answer`), and the node's own `start_tab_gone`, `choice_not_offered`. A question no longer on the tab's last line (answered at the computer) is no refusal: nothing is typed, the task starts in the tab all the same, and its `start_remedy` item says `answer_not_typed`, not `answer` |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/accept` | Verify a to-do from a `brief` item's Accept button `{"asked_at"}` (the item's `accept[].asked_at`, the to-do's `ask.asked_at`, or a `TODO_DECIDE` push's `todo.asked_at`) → `{"ok":true}`; when no Agent can receive a recorded decision, the same 200 carries `delivered:"none"` and the supervisor gets the choice; a decision also takes `{"asked_at","option"}` (the label of one of `ask.options`: the recommended one is the plain press, another goes to the task's Agent as the owner's choice; no such option 400) or `{"asked_at","response"}` (`decide_yourself`, `not_what_i_asked` or `explain_first`: nothing is taken and the task's supervisor is told; any other value, or both `option` and `response`, 400); `asked_at` missing 400; the round that waits now is the one named: a button of an earlier round, a to-do already verified, never asked or unknown 409 ("already handled"); another delivery failure answers 502 with code `accept_not_taken`, in the request's language with the reason and takes nothing (`delivered: "none"`); a send whose answer never came, or that the node isn't sure of, 502 `send_in_doubt` (`delivered: "unknown"`, or `"yes"` when it reached the Agent and what followed failed): the recommendation may be with the Agent already, so look before taking it again (the round still waits, the button works again); the stored asks could not be read or the acceptance could not be saved 503 (nothing taken, the button works again); read-only device 403 |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/decision-dismiss` | Persistently hide the current decision (Don't handle): `{"review_at"}` → `{"review_at","dismissal_id"}`. Requires the exact open latest `needs_user` review and state, with or without a real ask. Takes no option, closes no task and sends no message; a dismissed decision cannot take its timed default, and a valid explicit answer given later undoes the dismissal once it is taken. Rejected or failed answers leave the dismissal in force; a recorded choice handed to the supervisor when no Agent can receive it still counts as taken. Same-round repeats return the same receipt; dismissing after Undo makes a new receipt. Invalid fields 400, changed/ended review or missing task 409, read-only device 403, unavailable storage 503 with rollback |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/decision-undo-dismiss` | Restore only the named dismissal: `{"review_at","dismissal_id"}` → `{"review_at"}`. Requires the same open latest `needs_user` review and receipt. Repeating that Undo is idempotent; an older receipt cannot undo a newer dismissal. Invalid fields 400, stale review or receipt 409, read-only device 403, unavailable storage 503 with rollback |
| POST | `/api/v1/later/{id}/handled` | Take a question that can wait out of the queue, from a `brief` item's Handled button (the item's `later[].id`) → `{"ok":true}`; an `ask_user` nobody answered ends with it (its to-do is closed as `PATCH done: true` does); a question already handled, dropped (its to-do ended, or 7 days) or unknown 409 ("already handled"); a queue, or such a to-do, that can't be read or written 503, and the question stays; read-only device 403 |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/done-check` | Run the delivery judgment once against the current state, without writing to the database → `{"verdict","reason","would_close","skip","replies","signals"}` (`would_close` is wire-compatible and always false); with `{"apply":true}` (Re-check) it first moves the stage from the agents' last replies, then records the judgment and routes delivery / owner-wait without closing, adding `"applied"`, `"stage"`; judgment failed 502, missing 404, to-dos not loaded yet 503, read-only device 403 |
| PUT / DELETE | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/seen` | Got it on a Delivered · awaiting review to-do, or opening it (`PUT`): `seen_at` is now; Undo (`DELETE`) clears it → 200 `{"todo":Todo}`; not activity (`updated_at` stays); `{"type":"todos"}` is broadcast; missing 404; read-only device 403. | PUT | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/thread` | Bind the to-do to a chat thread `{"channel","chat_id","thread_id","title"?}` → 200 `{"todo":Todo}` (with `thread`); the three ids required (trimmed, at most 256 characters, else 400); another to-do holds the thread 409; missing 404; read-only device 403 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/thread` | Unbind it → 200 `{"todo":Todo}`; a to-do with no thread is left as it is; missing 404; read-only device 403 |
| GET | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/decisions?all=1` | Decision list `{"decisions":[Decision]}`, in chronological order; by default only those in effect, `all=1` also includes superseded ones; missing 404, hub without a database 503. A to-do an extension's token is not shown answers it 404 |
| POST | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/decisions` | Record one manually `{"question","choice","reason"?,"supersedes_id"?}` → `{"decision":Decision}`; empty question or choice 400, bad `supersedes_id` 400; to-do missing 404, hub without a database 503; read-only device 403 |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/decisions/{did}` | Mark it as superseding after the fact `{"supersedes_id"}` (empty string undoes; omitted 400) → `{"decision":Decision}`; to-do or decision missing 404, hub without a database 503; read-only device 403 |
| POST | `/api/v1/task-plans/{id}/start` | Start a plan `{"tasks"?:[PlanTask],"remember"?:bool,"schedule_grant"?:bool}`: `tasks` overrides, by index, the fields the user changed on the card (empty ones unchanged), and `remember` remembers "Start These Directly" for this kind; `schedule_grant` adds the kind to the start grant of the scheduled task whose round made the plan (its tasks' `schedule`, set by the hub with `schedule_title` and `schedule_basis`; ignored without one or once the schedule's prompt or target changed); creates a to-do per task (`origin`, `plan_id`) and starts the Agents in the background → 200 `{"plan":TaskPlan}`; already started or dismissed 409, missing 404, read-only device 403 |
| POST | `/api/v1/task-plans/{id}/dismiss` | Don't start → 200 `{"plan":TaskPlan}`; a plan already started, dismissed or withdrawn also answers 200 with the plan as it is (its `state` says which), so a client that missed the event updates its card; unknown 404 |

Paginated responses additionally always include `next_cursor` (`""` means complete); legacy responses omit it. The cursor freezes the initial change window (`since`, `until`) and advances `(at,id)` without repeating older sent/dismissal updates; invalid or cross-conversation cursor, or cursor combined with since, returns 400 → `{"items":[FeedItem],"plans":{"plan_…":TaskPlan},"task_cards":[TaskCard],"views":{"view_…":AssistantView},"view_actions":{"<key>":ViewAction},"view_blocks":["<item id>/0"]}` (plans and views are the current state of referenced objects; `task_cards` are stable task-row upserts for this page, not a replacement list, see "Tasks and the chat feed"; views, view_actions and view_blocks are always the full snapshot for the chat, not limited by since, and updates don't move the original feed position; view_blocks only holds the keys of body cards registered on the server, without resending the body). | POST | `/api/v1/assistant/feed/{id}/dismiss` | Decline one task-progress reply draft `{"draft":"<original body.draft>"}` → `{"item":FeedItem,"dismissal_id":"<decision id>"}`. The body gains `dismissed_at`, `dismissal_id`, `dismissal_updated_at`; task decision audit commits atomically. No send, Inbox filing, task completion or Agent closure. Missing/non-message 404, stale/sent/filed 409 `task_draft_stale`, read-only 403, storage failure 503 |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/feed/{id}/undo-dismiss` | Undo `{"dismissal_id":"<decision id>"}` → `{"item":FeedItem}`. Removes dismissal fields, keeps the original draft unsent, writes a superseding decision. A newer same-ref draft in this conversation, a later dismissal, sent/filed or already-undone card rejects with 409 `task_draft_stale`; ordinary Agent activity without a new card does not invalidate toast Undo; missing 404, read-only 403. Both routes use ordinary per-manager routing. Incremental chat feeds include dismissal and Undo changes without changing the card's original `at` |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/views/{key}/actions` | One reply on a live card or a registered body card (feature `assistant_views`): request body `ViewActionInput` `{action,page?,values?,client_msg_id,confirmed?,expected_version?}` → `{action:ViewAction}`. Without it (only for actions without confirm), the version the hub read when validating the binding is used. A version different from the saved one returns 409 `view_changed`: `{error,code,version,view?}` (`ViewChangedError`, `version` is the current version, `view` is the `AssistantView` envelope); the client keeps the draft, refreshes and has the user confirm again, and **must not resend automatically with the new version**. The submission locks the card inside a transaction before comparing versions, so concurrent with `view_update` it can only bind to the version still saved at submit time. Another submission 409 `already_answered`, with the existing action; retrying with the same client_msg_id / action / values / version returns the original record. The key is URL-encoded as a whole (including `/` and `#`); read-only device 403 `permission_denied`, extension token 403 `permission_denied` |

| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/rule-suggestions/{id}/always` | The owner's **Always** on a suggested rule (`RuleSuggestion`, "Tasks and the chat feed"), no body. The manager counts the answers again and makes the rule only if they still earn it → 200 `{"ok":true,"kind","creates"}` plus, by kind: `plan_start` `"creates":"tasks.trust","key"` (the `tasks.trust` entry); `standing_authorization` `"creates":"standing_authorization","authorization","revision"` (the grant as stored); `delegate` `"creates":"","setting":"agents.delegate"` (nothing stored).
