| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/route` | Talk to a task directly `{"todo_id","text"}`: the hub sends it to the task's most pressing Agent that has not stopped (waiting for you > working > unread > most recent) and appends a `routed` entry → 200 `{"item":FeedItem}`; the entry names the run it reached in `machine_id` and `session_id`. When every Agent of the task has stopped (read-only), it starts a new Agent for the task instead, on the computer, in the directory and with the launcher of the latest one, linked to the to-do, the text as its first message after who worked on it before; the `routed` entry carries `new_agent` (its session id) and `new_agent_machine`, and names that Agent in `machine_id` / `session_id` too when its start named a session; not this chat's task, or no running Agent 409; a body without `todo_id` or `text` 400; read-only device 403. Every refusal says `delivered`, and all but the 400 and the 403 are 409: `"none"` when nothing was typed (code `conflict`; a node's refusal and a send that never left are among these), and `send_in_doubt` with `"unknown"` when the text may be with the Agent (the send's or the new Agent's start's answer never came, or the node isn't sure) or `"yes"` when it reached the Agent and what followed failed (its `routed` entry could not be written, or the Agent's conversation was deleted meanwhile; with `asked_at`, the decision could not be recorded, worded as an answer's), cases in `spec/fixtures/todo-writes`. Optional `X-Persona-Op-Id` (`todo_route`, see "Operation receipts (client_ops)"): the same id gets the first answer back instead of the text going to the Agent again, the hub relays it as a send (cut off while the manager had it: 502 `assistant_in_doubt`, `delivered: "unknown"`), and says Processing on the socket as soon as it has the message (`todo_send_state`, "Message feedback") |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/todos/{id}/agents/{mid}/{sid}` | Remove an Agent (soft removal: sets `released_at` and `dismissed_at`; the row is no longer returned and isn't re-attached automatically) → 200 `{"ok":true}`; missing 404; read-only device 403 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/dirs?path=` | Directory browsing: `{"path","parent","entries":[{"name","path","is_git"}],"recent":[{"path","name","last_used"}]}`; with an empty path, entries is home |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions?machine_id=&manager=` | `{"sessions":[Session]}`, including running ones (herdr) and offline sessions from the last 7 days |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions?include_inactive=1&since=&until=&cursor=&limit=&machine_id=&manager=` | Sessions active in a time window, archived, finished and offline ones too: `{"sessions":[history row], "history":{since, until, complete, next_cursor, sources}}`. See "Session history" below; without `include_inactive=1` the list is unchanged |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions` | `{"machine_id","cwd","launcher","agent_type"?,"model"?,"prompt"?,"resume_session_id"?,"workspace_id"?,"desktop_project_id"?,"permission_mode"?,"effort"?,"launcher_default_effort"?,"speed"?,"ultracode"?,"goal"?,"tab_name"?,"async"?,"name_hint"?,"todo_id"?}` → `{"session":Session}`. `goal` is a one-line condition (at most 2000 characters) for a new Claude Code start in a terminal; the node sets it with `/goal` after the first message is in (see "A goal set at the start"); a node without `start_goal`, a resume, another agent, a screenless host or a start without `prompt` answers `409 start_goal_unsupported` and the start goes on without it. Optional `X-Persona-Op-Id` hooks into the persistent `start` receipt. `desktop_project_id` selects an exact Codex App project or a Claude directory project by its catalog source ID; Claude named-environment selections are refused. Selection limits, desktop creation and partial-start recovery are described under "New session". `model` is optional: the model picked in the new-Agent sheet (the `id` from `…/launchers/{name}/models` above, or a model ID the user typed: letters, digits and `. _ - / : @ [ ]`, starting with a letter or digit or with `~` and then one (a gateway's `~vendor/model-latest`), at most 256 characters, `proto.ValidModelID`; anything else 400 in the request's language), for this one time only, overriding **Model Settings › Agents** (the manager's `agents.start_params`, see "Agents" under "Bus"; when the manager isn't connected the hub waits for it a while, and if it doesn't come, applies **Model Settings › Agents** itself and doesn't generate a tab name). With an explicit launcher, `launcher_default_effort: true` uses its native effort when `effort` is omitted. `speed` is the optional start speed (`standard`, `fast` or `ultrafast`; see "Agent start speed"). `todo_id` is optional: attached within the same request after a successful start (missing 404, done 409, read-only device 403); with `prompt`, the background of the project the directory belongs to and the to-do's decisions are prepended to it; without `prompt` (`async`), they're prepended to the session's first message. `tab_name` is the herdr tab name; if not given, the manager uses the small-task model to make a short English name from `prompt` (`assistant/agents_start.go`, about 2 seconds; if it fails or the manager isn't connected, no name), and the node falls back to `agent-<n>`, adding `-2`, `-3` for duplicates in the same space (`node.tabLabel`). When a new space is created, its first tab also gets this name. The assistant's `agent_start` names tabs automatically the same way. For terminal starts that can be acknowledged before the conversation is ready, `"async": true` returns the session right away (new session id, directory, launcher, `starting: true`) and opens the tab and waits for Claude to be ready in the background, see "New session" below; Codex, `agy` and desktop starts are synchronous: they wait for the conversation identity or desktop acknowledgement before returning. In the asynchronous case the hub doesn't wait for naming, the tab is called `agent-<n>` first and `session.rename` follows once the name is ready. `name_hint`: when the web app sends the first message as a normal message (so it shows up immediately), it's used for naming and not put into `prompt`. The answer has `launcher_note` when the Agents default (or a profile tier) is a launcher the computer lacks and another one starts it instead, and, where the start's engine runs only its own launchers (Paseo), when one of its providers of the same kind runs in place of the launcher asked for, a model it does not offer is dropped, or an effort its model does not offer goes down to one it does; `instead` carries what was asked (the node's answer). A launcher none of its providers is the kind of is refused: 400 from the manager, or 409 `launcher_kind_missing` from the engine. An extension's or a scoped token's `resume_session_id` of a chat its computer lists in a track, in a folder set to Hide, or deleted by the owner answers 404, as for a chat that does not exist (as every session control does for those tokens). A scoped token's must name a chat its computer lists (404 otherwise); an extension's may also name one its computer does not list and the owner did not delete: the hub passes the start on with `resume_outside_health` to a node that announces it, which resumes the chat only when it has it outside a track, else the same 404 (`409 engine_missing` first, whatever the id, while the computer's engine runtime is away, as for the owner); toward an older node such a resume answers 404, or `503 sessions_not_listed` (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`) while the hub has had no list of that computer's sessions since it started, or no word of its node. The hub decides an extension's resume after every check that holds for any id (the computer's trust, the agent type, the manager's `agents.start_params`), so those answer alike whichever chat the id names. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items?before_seq=&turns=2` | History paging `{"items":[Item],"has_more":bool}` (ascending by seq). `turns`: go back far enough to get N complete "user question + answer" turns; injected supervision, scheduled prompts and background wakes remain in history but do not consume this budget, and client cache tails use the same rule. The page starts with a user question (at most 2000 items; when one turn is very long and going back would mean parsing tens of MB, the page is shorter with `has_more: true`, and paging back continues from there; but as long as there is earlier content, a page contains at least one item, since an empty page with `has_more: true` would leave the web app with no seq to page back from); a `limit` request counts items. With `lazy_images=1`, images carry no data (`image: {mime, lazy:true, size, width, height}`) and are fetched when displayed. With `after_seq=N`, returns new content with seq > N (for background sync, about 500 items per page, never splitting the items of one line; `more_after: true` means there's more, fetch again from the last item's seq, or fetch the latest page instead). With `fold_work=1`, pages going back from the end fold the work; with `from_seq=&through_seq=`, returns the items of those lines (for expanding a fold, about 1000 items per page, `more: true` means `through_seq` isn't reached yet). See "Folded work" |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items?strict=1&before_seq=&limit=80&lazy_images=1` | Private CLI export's backward page. The hub forwards `strict_read: true` with `session.items` and requires the node to acknowledge it. A node reading its local transcript first opens the source and propagates refresh failures. The successful page includes `strict_read: true`, `history` when the source has recorded lines, and `from_seq` / `to_seq` as its coverage. The first page's `to_seq` is the snapshot high-water mark. For an earlier page `to_seq` is `before_seq-1`. `from_seq` is zero when there is no earlier page, otherwise one less than the first item's sequence. Same-sequence siblings remain together. A node or runtime that cannot acknowledge the request gets `409 node_outdated`; an older hub's response without the acknowledgment cannot be treated as a fresh read. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items/{item id}/full?strict=1` | Export's full item uses the same fresh-source requirement. It returns the normal item with `strict_read: true` and `source_text_bytes`, the node's full text size before hub presentation transforms. A missing acknowledgment is refused the same way as for the strict page. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items?user_inputs=1` | Web navigation contract: `{total, inputs:[{id,seq}], history}` for all genuine human inputs, oldest first, independent of the loaded transcript page. Text/image siblings share one position; genuine queued inputs and user-authored contexts count. Supervision, scheduled/wake/loop inputs, peer/conversation deliveries and tool-result images do not. No bodies, previews, image bytes or model calls. The hub relays the node's position-only `session.items` mode; runtimes use their existing item pages. An incomplete or rewritten read is an error, not a partial total. Older nodes leave the web's loaded-only compatibility rail. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items/{item id}/image` | The raw bytes of an item's image (Content-Type is the image type, cacheable forever); the item id contains `#` and must be percent-encoded |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items/{item id}/visualization` | A Codex visualization item's self-contained HTML fragment (`text/html; charset=utf-8`, cacheable forever, at most 1 MiB). The node only serves files under its visualizations tree that belong to this session (symlinks resolved), and clients run the fragment in their offline HTML sandbox with no bridge |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items/{item id}/full` | An item's full text (`Item`, without images and without `full_size`; at most 1 MB): fetched when the user taps "show full text". The node re-reads and parses that line |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/messages` | `{"text":"…","images":[{"mime","data"}]?,"client_msg_id"?,"clear_draft"?,"todo_id"?,"via"?,"approval_reply_to"?}` (`via`: as on a new assistant conversation, below; `approval_reply_to` is only the explicit exact-reply target on a full owner's own proposal reply, never model or extension metadata); `todo_id` is optional: attached after a successful send (missing 404, done 409, read-only device 403), and the to-do's decisions are prepended to `text`; for a session created with `todo_id` and no `prompt`, its first message (within 15 minutes, with or without `todo_id`) also gets the project background prepended; if the session is offline, it is first started with the original launcher via `--resume`; an assistant chat's message may carry `launcher` / `model` / `effort` for that message alone, else it runs on the chat's `model_pick`: one that can't run on its computer any more refuses the message (409 `launcher_out_of_scope` / `launcher_own_service` / `launcher_missing` / `launcher_other_kind`, or 400 when the launcher can't run assistant chats) and is never swapped for another; a `client_msg_id` beginning `start:` is the manager's own (a conversation's first message) and is refused 400 `client_msg_id_reserved` before anything else is done with the request; for rejections see "Sending messages" below. An exact owner proposal reply containing only `text`, `client_msg_id` and `approval_reply_to` answers `200 {"ok":true,"approval_reply":true,"interaction_id":"<same proposal id>"}` after its durable decision, and sends nothing to the node/model; any other proposal proof or receipt fails closed. → `{"ok":true}`; to a Claude outside Persona's terminals that took it while a permission prompt or another dialog only the computer can answer holds it, also `"waits_on_computer":true` (a reply to a question the session asked answers that question instead): delivered into its queue, read once that is answered at the computer, which the web app says on sending (a retry answered from the hub's send record leaves it out); to such a Claude, the owner's own message also says how it went in, `"delivered_as":"user_input"` (through Persona's plugin, as the person's input) or `"relayed"` with `relay_reason` (through its inbox, where the Agent may not take it as the owner's approval; the web app says so unless the reason is `no_plugin`), with the same caveats; to a Codex waiting for its first message (`awaiting_first_message`) also `session`, the thread that message began (left out when it could not be told apart), where the conversation goes on: its row replaces the waiting one in the same pane. A delivered message to one of the assistant's chats whose configured launcher can't run there answers `launcher_note` too: which launcher of the same kind ran it instead, and why, in the user's language. A message with a `client_msg_id` to one of the assistant's chats that could not go in before anything was typed (its process did not start, its computer was away: a 5xx with nothing delivered), or one sent while older ones to that chat are kept, answers **202** `{"delivered":"later","undelivered":{…}}` instead of the failure: the chat's manager keeps it and sends it again by itself, once, and the row's `undelivered` shows it; a retry of the same id answers `{"delivered":"later"}` and sends nothing. A manager that cannot keep it (an older one, away) leaves the failure as before. A message with a `client_msg_id` from a person's full device whose client declares `agent_message_hold` (client_hello `features` or `X-Persona-Features`) to an Agent (not one of the assistant's chats; not one with `todo_id`, a fresh to-do start's first message or `apply_switch`) whose computer is not connected, or one sent while older held messages of that Agent wait, also answers **202** `{"delivered":"later","undelivered":{…,"computer":"…"}}` from a hub with `agent_message_hold`: the manager that connects the computer holds it and sends it once, when the computer is back; a try whose outcome is unknown is never repeated by itself. An older manager leaves the failure as before; one that cannot store a message that has to wait behind held ones answers `held_not_kept` with `delivered: none` (nothing typed: send it again). A person's message from a client that does not declare the feature is never held: while older held messages of that Agent wait it answers 409 `held_ahead` with `delivered: none` (nothing typed) instead of going ahead of them. At most 50 messages are held per Agent; another answers 409 `held_full` with `delivered: none`. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/agent-messages` | Feature `agent_terminal_send`. Read-only preflight for a full paired device. Confirms the exact machine and session are a listed Agent with `{machine_id,session_id}`. The listing can be kept while the Agent's computer is offline. Persona conversations, unknown and archived targets are refused. |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/agent-messages` | Feature `agent_terminal_send`. Same Agent eligibility check before claiming the required `X-Persona-Op-Id` and again before delivery. Full paired devices only. Body `{text, hold_when_away}` with the boolean matching the client's explicit `agent_message_hold` header declaration, if any. Executes the ordinary message send and returns the same results. The hold flag is included in the stored operation digest. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/info` | Session info: `{session_id,transcript_path,cwd,model,launcher,git_branch,version,permission_mode,effort,context_tokens,output_tokens,compactions,turns,usage_unknown?,started_at,last_activity,stop_cause,task_id?,task_workspace_id?,workspace_label?}`. `usage_unknown: true`: nobody gives the session's counts (a runtime's session with no transcript on its computer: Paseo's other providers), so clients leave out Context, Output, Turns and Compactions; the counts stay `0` beside it. `cwd` is as on the Session: an Agent's latest directory, an assistant or track chat's own directory where it started. Node `session.info` reports the saved `stop_cause` (empty means unknown), including when a Codex source has no history. Explicit assistant resume of an archived stopped Agent verifies this node-owned value instead of trusting the archive snapshot; missing/unknown/user/unsupported causes or a failed read never authorize resume. The node rechecks eligibility when starting; the original launcher and permission mode are unchanged |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/queue` | `{keep:[indexes]}`: takes back the queued input and keeps only the given items, in the order given, returns `{queue}`; used for editing, deleting and reordering (a permutation of the indexes); doesn't go through client_ops. In a Persona chat `keep` indexes the user's own queued messages (the first `len(queued) - queued_relayed`). The node takes them out of its headless Claude with `cancel_async_message` (only the ones that have to move or go) and writes the kept ones again in the new order, and answers `{queue, images}` (`proto.QueueEdit`, samples in `spec/fixtures/wire/queue.json`): `images[i]` are message i's photos (`{mime, data}`, base64) for the composer, null for a message without any, and the key is left out when none has. 409 `queue_taken` (a message to take out went in meanwhile; nothing is written twice), `queue_changed` (an index past the queue), `queue_unsupported` (a Codex chat: nothing waits), `queue_edit_unsupported` (a Claude Code outside Persona's terminals with no pane; nothing changed, the messages go in order), `assistant_control_failed` (a Claude Code without the request) Runtime sessions with `capabilities.queue_edit` return the same `{queue, images?}` shape. |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/queue/send-now` | Gives the agent what waits in Claude Code's queue now (node `session.queue.send_now`): Claude Code's own send-now, so a command it runs moves to the background and goes on, and a reply it is writing is asked again with the message (Esc would stop the command). The node presses it only while the screen offers it, with the keys the hint beside a queued message names: `ctrl+enter to send now` → ctrl+enter (Claude Code 2.1.311 to 2.1.321 in a terminal with extended keys, such as a herdr pane, the hint on the line under the message), `ctrl+x ctrl+s to send now` → ctrl+x ctrl+s (2.1.319, and 2.1.311 to 2.1.321 inside tmux or screen or a terminal without extended keys). The hint is read by its shape: the keys of any binding, an optional separator, `send now`. A fullscreen Claude Code scrolled up has the hint off screen; the node first presses the scroll-to-bottom key its "Jump to bottom" pill names (else ctrl+End), which sends nothing, then looks again. That is the queue at that moment, which the transcript reports about a second late. → `{sent:true}` once the queue is gone from the screen. 409 `nothing_queued` (nothing queued on the screen), `send_now_unsupported` (not a Claude in a terminal, such as one in Claude's desktop app), `send_now_unrecognized` (something is queued but the screen shows no send-now hint the node knows, even at the end of a scrolled-up transcript, or one naming keys a terminal can't send (cmd, fn, a click), which the node's message quotes; nothing was pressed), `send_now_in_doubt` (`delivered: "unknown"`: the key went in, the queue is still shown); an older node: `node_outdated`. It sends the whole queue. In a Persona chat it is Claude Code's `interrupt` with `send_now` over stream-json: the waiting messages start the next request at once, and the step it was on stops or, when it can, goes on in the background; 409 `nothing_queued` when nothing waits, `assistant_control_failed` when that Claude Code refuses Runtime sessions with `capabilities.queue_send_now` handle this through `session.queue.send_now`. |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/seen` | Mark the session as seen, returns `{ok:true}`; `seen` can also be sent over WS |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/interrupt` | Send Esc. When the Esc went to a Claude Code session in a pane whose turn was already over while its background work still runs (a background command, a background subagent, a workflow: the row is Working by `background_working`), it interrupted nothing: 409 `turn_over_background`, with words in the request's language saying the turn had ended and the background work still runs. The Esc is pressed either way |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/start/continue` | `{"choice":"n"}` → `{"session":Session}` (feature `start_continue`, see "Answering a start's question"): the answer to the question the session's start stopped on (`start_error_code: shell_waiting`), one of `start_error_args.choices`; the node types it into the kept tab and the session is `starting` again, under the same id, in that tab. Routed to the machine's manager (`internal/devices`), `full` only (an answer-only device or an extension's token 403 `read_only`); a choice that is not a short word 400 `bad_request`; offline 503 `machine_offline`; a node without capability `start_continue` 409 `node_outdated`. The node's refusals, nothing typed (409, `delivered: none`): `start_not_waiting` (no failed start waits on a question: it started, expired, or another answer started it again), `choice_not_offered`, `start_tab_gone` (the tab expired or an agent runs there), `secret_env_gone` (a start with a hand-off's values cannot run again; such a start lists no `choices`). A question no longer on the tab's last line (answered at the computer) is no refusal: nothing is typed and the session starts again in that tab all the same |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/screen?lines=60&source=visible` | `{"text":"…","status":"working"}` (`lines=40` with `source=visible` is a screen card's read: on a pane herdr can't send 40 plain rows of, fewer); `source=recent` also reads the pane's scrollback (lines up to 20000; fewer lines returned than requested means it reached the top); `format=ansi` includes colors (SGR, lines end in `\r\n`; old nodes don't understand it and return plain text as before) |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/screen/before` | `{"anchor":["the top few lines on screen"],"lines":200,"format"?:"ansi"}` → `{"text","has_more","at_limit"}`: a stretch of scrollback before the anchor (located by content, the anchor compared as plain text; herdr keeps only about 1000 lines, `at_limit` means it reached the top) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/spaces/{wid}/rename` | `{"name"}` → `{ok, name}`: `herdr workspace rename` (a Paseo space, by its id or one of its workspaces': the Paseo project's name, runtime ↔ node `workspace.rename`), and updates "machine/old name" in pins / mutes to the new name: the one the node's `space.rename` answers it shows now (a named herdr session's space has `<session> · ` in front), else the one given. The old name is the space's sessions', or a runtime session's whose `workspace_id` is `wid`. A space no engine of the computer lists any more (the default engine Paseo, no terminal host listing it) is refused with 409 `space_gone` |
| (node RPC) | `session.start` `plan_then` | For a start with `permission_mode: "plan"`: the mode the session goes on in once its plan is approved, wherever that happens. The manager fills it in; a start that names it keeps its own. Ignored for any other mode. |
| (node RPC) | `session.start` `session_id` | A manager-started Claude session may carry the id it wants the new session to use (a v4 UUID). The node starts Claude with `--session-id <id>` and answers that session, so when the start's answer never comes back the manager reconciles it by this exact id instead of guessing from launcher and directory. A start that goes to a runtime (Paseo, the machine's engine) passes it on as runtime ↔ node `session.start`'s `session_id`, and Paseo gives its session that id. Optional and backward compatible: a node or runtime that does not honor it generates its own id, and the manager falls back to the pre-start snapshot heuristic, which takes a runtime's session only when its row says `started_by_persona`. |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/modes` | `{"permission_mode"?, "effort"?, "model"?, "launcher"?, "ultracode"?, "ultracode_dismiss_lost"?}` or a separate `{"service_tier":"<advertised id>"}` request: change a running session's permission mode / reasoning effort (`effort` is `auto` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`, `auto` being the model's own default); `model` is only for Claude Code terminal sessions: the node types `/model <id>` into its input box (with the same checks as sending a message: `dialog_open` / `input_draft` reject, Agent working rejects, and the screen is read afterwards to confirm), the id comes from `GET /machines/{mid}/launchers/{name}/models` or is one the user typed (the same rule as a start's `model`, `proto.ValidModelID`; the node refuses anything else), and within one request the model is switched first, then the rest; the session list's `model` shows this choice until a new model appears in the transcript; `permission_mode` and `effort` in the session list are the current values. A Claude Code agent's `bypass_available: true` says it can switch to `bypassPermissions` while it runs (its claude was started with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, read off the process by the node); without it, a terminal Claude Code the node can restart (one in a pane of a terminal host that can start an agent there, on a launcher and in a folder Persona can tell) takes the pick anyway: the node restarts it in that mode once its turn is over, resuming the same conversation (`bypass_pending: true` on its row until then); any other mode picked meanwhile drops the restart, and so does the end of the claude process it was picked for. Elsewhere only a new start or the assistant can pick that mode. Sessions with `efforts` (Codex via app-server or the Codex App) accept `effort` from `efforts` and separate speed requests when `service_tiers` are advertised ("Codex sources and capabilities"). `POST /api/v1/sessions` and `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` also accept these two fields, as the starting values. `ultracode` calls the separate `session.ultracode` method after model and effort changes; `ultracode_dismiss_lost:true` only dismisses the resume notice. See "Claude Code ultracode". `launcher` (feature `launcher_switch`) other than the session's own records a switch to that launcher that the user's next message (`apply_switch`) carries out, with `model` and `effort` for it; its own launcher drops one; `from` is the launcher the client saw. See "Switching a running Agent to another provider" |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/rename` | `{"tab_name"?, "title"?}`: the tab uses `herdr tab rename`; the session name sends `/rename <name>` to the running claude (it writes `custom-title`), and if it isn't running, appends the same `custom-title` line to the transcript directly. For assistant chats, `title` is also recorded as the user-given title (the hub's `assistant.titles`, never overwritten by automatic titles); Codex assistant chats are only recorded on the hub. With an extension's token the title is only a hint: the hub still names a chat it started after its first turn |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/mutes` | Mutes, same structure as pins, plus `allowed` (Agents with notifications turned on individually while their space is muted). Rule: the Agent itself in sessions → muted; in allowed → not muted; otherwise go by its space. Muted Agents / spaces get no notifications at all (done, needs you) and are shown dimmed in the list; cached in hub memory, updated on PUT. GET returns the cached list when available; a failed initial read returns 500 (`code: internal`) without a mute list and is retried on the next read. Clients keep their previous copy on failure; only a successful read may replace it |
| GET | `/api/v1/hub/update` | The hub's version and update state: `{version, build, channel, can_update, why_not?, latest?{version, build, released, notes, newer, bad, held?}, state, progress?, busy:[{machine_id, machine, session_id?, title}], error?, auto, auto_notice, last_check?, confirmed}`; `state`: `idle` / `checking` / `available` / `downloading` / `waiting_idle` / `restarting` / `confirming` / `updated` / `rolled_back` / `failed`; `busy` lists what a restart would interrupt (chats working or waiting for an answer, machines being redeployed); `auto_notice`: the user hasn't been told "automatic updates are on" yet; `latest.held`: why automatic update won't install this newer version (its code may not include the commit this hub is running), though a manual update still can; a Docker hub also has `image{name, tag, pinned}` (the image it runs; `pinned`: the tag is a version number, so `.env` must be changed first), `latest` is the newest release on the registry (`build` is 0, no `released`), and `POST …/check` asks the registry; all `/api/v1/hub/update` endpoints return 503 `internal` with a localized unavailable message when persisted update settings cannot be read. Failed reads are retried, and no settings/history write or automatic update proceeds from unread settings |
| POST | `/api/v1/hub/update/check` | Check now, returns the same as above |
| POST | `/api/v1/hub/update` | `{"now"?: true}` start updating: download, verify, wait until the assistant and Agents are idle, replace, restart; `now` is "update now" after a second confirmation and doesn't wait for idle. Not a release build (`dev` / `docker`), or no newer version 409 (`error` explains; for Docker it gives the `docker compose pull` command) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/hub/update/settings` | `{"auto"?: bool, "auto_notice_seen"?: bool}`: the automatic update switch (on by default); changing the switch also counts as having told the user; a failed save returns 503 `internal`. Retrying after storage recovery preserves update history and the bad-build list |
| GET | `/api/v1/hub/update/history` | `{"history":[{from_version, to_version, to_build, started, ended, result: updated\|rolled_back\|failed\|held, reason?, auto}]}`, newest first, keeps 50; `held`: the newer version wasn't installed automatically (`reason` says why), recorded once per version |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/skills` | Full-access-only ordinary Agent skill catalog, routed to the machine manager. No client execution overrides. Requires node capability `session_skills_v1` and returns `{catalog_version:1,skills:[{id,name,description?,source}],complete}`. References bind manager, machine, session and actual execution environment; unavailable environments fail explicitly. |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/mode-changes` | A session's permission mode changes, oldest first, its latest 200: `{changes: [{kind, from?, to?, applied?, actor_kind?, device_id?, device_name?, reason?, at}]}`. For the owner's devices only (a full role; 403 for an extension's token, which no scope opens). Routed to the machine's manager; an empty list where it keeps no record |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/skills` | Web assistant mention catalog, per-manager routing. Optional `machine_id`, `session_id`, `launcher`; the manager owns cwd/profile/identity. Returns `{catalog_version:1,skills:[{id,name,description?,source}],complete}`; instruction-file paths stay on the node, while human-readable source labels can identify roots. Unsupported, unavailable or old environments fail explicitly; ordinary chat remains independent. Selected references are revalidated on send. |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/pins` | Pins in the dev list: `{"spaces":["server/app"],"sessions":["server/<session id>"]}`; spaces use "machine/space name" (herdr workspace ids change after a herdr restart); stored in Postgres settings |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file?path=&cwd=&offset=` | Read a file (file viewer): `{"path","name","size","mime","text"\|"data","truncated","offset","next","is_dir","entries"?}`. Text files at most 2 MB per call, read from `offset`; if not finished, it stops at the end of the last complete line, and `next` is where the next page starts (0 when done); binary files are given whole (up to 2 MB) and can't be read from the middle; directories give the first 500 entries. `~` is home, relative paths are inside `cwd`; iCloud is refused. With `stream=1` (hub feature `file_stream`), binary files return only a descriptor `{"stream":true,"revision",...}` without `data`, and the content goes through `/file/download`; `mime` comes from a fixed extension table, then sniffing the leading bytes (see "File preview" below) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/download?path=&cwd=&inline=` | The raw bytes of the complete file, authenticated with the same Bearer; the web's `<video>` / `<audio>` / `<img>` can't send headers, so they use `?token=` (the hub never logs query strings); the hub reads via the node's `file.chunk` at most 1 MiB at a time, and a single request never holds the whole file in memory. Supports HTTP Range / Content-Range (including suffix ranges), with Content-Length, ETag and an attachment file name; empty path 400, old node 409 `node_outdated`, non-regular files, iCloud and read errors are refused. Later chunks must match the size and version from the first read. A chunk whose read failed because the node's connection dropped is asked again at the same offset and version once the node is back, for up to 30 seconds; if the file changed, the node is not back in time, the read fails otherwise or the request is canceled, the download is aborted (HTTP/2: the stream is reset; HTTP/1.1: the connection closes short of Content-Length), so the client sees an error, never a short file that ends as if complete. The old `/file` 2 MiB binary preview is unchanged. `inline=1` only applies to images, audio/video and PDF (`Content-Disposition: inline`); everything else is still an attachment; everything except PDF carries `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/thumb?path=&cwd=&size=` | A file's thumbnail (hub feature `file_thumb`, node `file.thumb`): long side at most `size` pixels (default 256, 32–1024), JPEG when opaque, PNG when transparent; JPEGs are turned to their EXIF orientation first; `ETag` is "processing version-file version-size" (a node that draws differently answers a new one), `If-None-Match` gets 304, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Can't render 404 `no_thumbnail` (the client shows an icon), old node 409 `node_outdated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/convert?path=&cwd=&to=pdf` | Convert a document to PDF with that computer's LibreOffice (hub feature `file_convert`, node `file.convert`, the web's Office fallback): returns `{"path","size","mime"}`, where `path` is the PDF in the node's cache, then read with `/file/download?path=<it>&inline=1`. Cached per file version, cleared 7 days after its last use; one conversion at a time, 90-second timeout; the input is first copied to a fixed file name and a temporary profile directory is used, so it doesn't fight with a LibreOffice the user has open. Not installed 404 `no_converter`, old node 409 `node_outdated` |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file-transfer/settings` | The computer's file transfer switch, off by default (the manager's, settings key `machine_file_transfer`): `{"enabled": bool}` → `{enabled, inbox?}`; full devices only; see "File transfer switch" |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/blob?cwd=&path=&rev=` | A file's content at some revision (hub feature `git_blob`, node `git.blob`, for the web's diff): `rev` is `HEAD`, `INDEX` (the staging area), a commit hash or "hash^" (its parent), `path` is relative to the repo root. Returns `{"path","size"}`, where `path` is a file in the node's cache named by blob id (with the original extension), then read with `/file/download`; if the file doesn't exist at that revision, `{"missing":true}`. Up to 200 MB, cleaned 7 days after its last use |
| GET / POST / DELETE | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/browser/cookies` | Sign-ins in ego lite (plugin ego): GET lists sites `{"sites":[{"domain","count","expires"?}]}` (no names or values); POST `{"cookies":[{name,value,domain,path?,expires?,secure?,http_only?,same_site?,host_only?}]}` imports and returns `imported`, `skipped`; DELETE `?site=a&site=b` or `?all=1` clears and returns `removed`. Only accepts the user's own device tokens (pairing tokens etc. 403); the hub stores nothing; target Mac offline 409 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/stat?paths=&cwd=` | Whether paths mentioned in a session exist on this machine: `paths` one per line (also accepts `path=a&path=b`), at most 200 → `{"stats":[{"path"(as given),"kind":"file"\|"dir"\|"denied"\|"missing","size"?}]}`. `denied` is a folder macOS won't let personad read (opening it explains how to grant access); relative paths without `cwd`, paths in iCloud, and sensitive files (see below) are always `missing`; waits at most 3 seconds per call, and anything not answered by then (a hung network drive) is also `missing`. The web turns file / dir / denied paths into links |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/fs?path=&cwd=` | File tree: `{"path","entries":[{"name","dir","symlink","size","mtime","ignored"}],"truncated"}`, directories first, at most 2000 entries; iCloud is refused; `ignored`: Git ignores it (the node runs `git check-ignore` once over the names on this page; outside a repo or without git nothing is marked and the field doesn't appear) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/fs/find?cwd=&limit=` | All files under a directory (node `fs.find`, for the web's ⌘K file search): `{"cwd","files":[relative paths, "/"-separated],"truncated","source":"git"\|"walk"}`. Inside a git repo (including subdirectories) it uses `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` (ignored files and files deleted on disk aren't listed); otherwise it walks breadth-first from `cwd` (skips `.git`, `node_modules` and various cache directories, doesn't follow symlinks into directories, capped at 5 seconds), so when over the limit the shallowest files are kept. At most `limit` files (default and maximum 50,000); sensitive paths are not listed (same as `fs`: ssh keys, the hub's token, etc.), and iCloud and sensitive directories are refused entirely. The node reuses the result for the same directory within 10 seconds. Same permissions as `fs`: full role only, answer-only devices can't |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/status?cwd=` | `{"is_repo","root","branch","head","upstream","gone","ahead","behind","files":[{"path","orig_path","index","worktree","added","deleted","binary"}],"stashes","commits":[latest 30]}` (read-only, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; `gone`: the upstream is configured but its ref is missing, e.g. deleted on the remote and pruned, so `ahead` / `behind` are 0 and mean nothing; left out otherwise) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pull` | `{"cwd"}` → `{"status": GitStatus, "updated": bool}`; only allowed on a normal branch with an upstream and a clean worktree, runs `git pull --ff-only --no-rebase --no-autostash --no-recurse-submodules`. Divergence, uncommitted changes, no upstream, auth failure or timeout all report an error; it never stashes / merges / rebases automatically; the pull command gets at most 60 seconds, the node 75 seconds total, the hub 90 seconds. Full role only |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/diff?cwd=&path=&staged=0\|1` | `{"path","diff","truncated"}`; untracked files are diffed against /dev/null, at most 512 KB: the node stops reading there, and a longer diff ends after its last whole line within it, with `truncated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/show?cwd=&hash=` | `{"commit","files","diff","truncated"}`; the diff is capped like `git/diff`'s |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/log?cwd=&skip=&limit=` | `{"commits":[…]}` paged |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/review?cwd=&scope=&base=&path=` | Hub feature `git_review`, node `git.review`: every file a scope changed, with its hunks, for the web's Review panel. `scope` is `uncommitted` (the working tree against HEAD), `branch` (against where the branch left the default branch, or the branch named in `base`) or `commit` (against the commit in `base`); new files Git does not track yet count as added. → `{"root","scope","base":{"hash","short","subject","ref","empty"},"head":{"hash","short","branch"},"files":[{"path","old_path","status","untracked","added","deleted","binary","generated","refused","big","revision","hunks":[{"header","old_start","new_start","lines"}]}],"truncated"}`. `path` (repeatable) asks for only those files (a `big` one, which came without its hunks; a rename with both paths). Fields left empty are left out: a hunk with no function context has no `header`, a repository with no commit yet a `base` with no `hash`. Refusals are 409 with `code`: `not_git`, `no_folder` (the folder is not there), `bad_scope`, `bad_base`, `no_default_branch`, `no_merge_base`; an older node is 409 `node_outdated` |
| POST / GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/review` | Hub feature `session_review`, manager-owned independent review. POST (full role only) explicitly starts a fresh reviewer with `permission_mode: "plan"` on the same computer, in a disposable snapshot of the source directory. It answers `{"running":true,"reviewer_session_id":"…","started_at":"…"}`. Refusals are 404 `no_session` or 409 `session_busy`, `review_running`, `no_change`, `read_only_unsupported`, `not_supported`, each localized. GET answers `{"running":bool,"has_changes":bool,"started_at":"…"}` for the menu; it never starts work. The finished `question` interaction with `tool_name: "persona_session_review"` carries `review_report`, `review_count` and `reviewer_session_id`; answer Send/Dismiss through `/api/v1/interactions/{id}/resolve` as above |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/branches?cwd=` | `{"branches":[{"name","remote","current","upstream","hash","subject","date"}],"default"}`: local branches, then remote ones without a local branch of the same name, newest first, at most 300; `default` is the remote's default branch as git knows it (`origin/HEAD`, without the remote's name), left out when git doesn't know it (and by an older node). Full role only |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pr?cwd=` | Through `gh` on that machine as it is signed in: the current branch's pull request `{"branch","pr":{"number","url","title","state","draft","base","head","mergeable","merge_state","review","auto_merge","checks":[{"name","state":"pass\|fail\|pending\|skipped","url"}],"checks_state":"passing\|failing\|pending","threads":[{"path","line","outdated","comments":[{"author","body","url","at"}]}]}}` (`threads`: the unresolved review threads only); `"pr":null` when the branch has none. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/stage` · `…/git/commit` · `…/git/push` · `…/git/switch` · `…/git/stash` | The Git panel's writes, each a click the client confirmed; answer `{"status": GitStatus, …}`. `stage {cwd, paths, unstage?}` (`git add` / `git restore --staged`; paths `file.read` refuses are refused); `commit {cwd, message}` commits what is staged (nothing staged is refused, never `-a`; hooks run, the hub waits up to 5 minutes) → `+ commit`; `push {cwd, set_upstream?}` pushes the branch to its own upstream branch by an explicit refspec with no `+` (a forcing refspec in the config does not apply), a branch without one only with `set_upstream` (to `origin`, same name) → `+ output`; `switch {cwd, branch, create?, from?}`: uncommitted files the target has differently are listed and nothing is switched, other uncommitted changes go along; a remote-only branch gets a local branch tracking it; `stash {cwd, op: push\|list\|apply\|pop\|drop, index?, oid?, message?, untracked?}` → `+ stashes:[{index,oid,message,date}]`. Nothing forces, resets, stashes on its own or skips a hook; one write at a time per repository. A refusal is a 409 with `code`: `git_not_repo`, `git_detached`, `git_nothing_staged`, `git_hook_failed` (its output is `error`), `git_identity`, `git_no_upstream`, `git_no_remote`, `git_push_rejected` (pull first), `git_auth`, `git_conflict` (`files`), `git_busy` (another git holds the lock), `git_no_branch`, `git_no_stash`, `git_stash_stale`, `git_stash_unsupported`, `git_stash_conflicted` (`files`: an apply / pop stopped on merge conflicts, so the stash's content is in the tree with those files unmerged and the entry is kept), `git_failed`. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pr` · `…/git/pr/merge` | `{cwd, title, body, base?, draft?}` opens a pull request for the current branch (pushed, nothing left to push, else `git_not_pushed`); `{cwd, number, method: squash\|merge\|rebase, auto?}` merges it now or sets it to merge when ready, `{cwd, number, auto_off: true}` takes that back; the branch is never deleted (gh would switch the checkout). Both answer as `GET git/pr`. `gh` missing: `no_gh`; not signed in: `not_signed_in`; no pull request: `git_no_pr`; no GitHub remote: `git_not_github`. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/fork` | Branch into a new chat: body `{at_item_id}` (the item id of a reply; empty means the whole thing) → `{session_id}`. The node copies Claude's transcript up to the end of the turn that reply is in, under a new session id, leaving the original session untouched; the new session is an offline session, and the next message `--resume`s it as usual. Only supported when the session has `can_fork: true` (Claude Code, with a transcript, not an external source / Codex; a runtime's session only when its runtime names a Claude transcript on that computer, Paseo's agents running Claude Code: the copy is of that transcript, named after the session, and the machine's engine continues it), otherwise returns `code: fork_unsupported`; branching from the turn still being written returns `fork_turn_running`. Limits: only the conversation itself is copied; the file snapshots `/rewind` uses (`~/.claude/file-history/<id>/`) and subagent records are not, so `/rewind` in the branch can't go back to changes made before the branch |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/restore-model` | Back to the configured model after a refusal fallback: no body; a relay of the session id to the node's `session.restore_model` (see "Going back to the configured model"). Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/close` | Quit claude and close the tab (any Agent in herdr, including manually started ones; for a split tab only its own pane is closed) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}` | Delete a chat: close a supported idle Agent on its computer, then remove the conversation from the lists on every device. The hub stores the deletion time in `sessions.deleted` under the conversation ID (for an Antigravity pane, its first alias), so the note still applies when the pane's row gives way to the conversation's own row. Offline history and failed starts can be removed without contacting the computer. The transcript stays; later activity brings it back. Returns `{"ok":true}` after the hub saves the note; a close error prevents the deletion. Active work or queued messages return 409, assistant chats return 400 (use archive), an unknown session returns 404, and read-only access returns 403. |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant` | `{"machine_id","launcher","cwd","timezone","timezone_picked"?,"notes"?,"notes_effective","main"?,"main_tasks_quiet","main_background_folded","idle_close_hours","archive_closed_days","interject_background","claude_interactive","agent_tasks","close_ended_terminals","inbox_signals","next_suggestions","owner_reply_approval","persistent_owner_action_cards","owner_reply_approval_phrases","main_supervises_own_tasks","background_supervisor"?,"conversations":[Session]}`: `main_supervises_own_tasks` is the legacy background-supervisor setting retained for wire and settings compatibility; new assistant-dispatched tasks are supervised by main regardless of it, and `background_supervisor` is that conversation's session id once it has been made (on the assistant's computer; read-only, with `background_supervisor_machine_id` and `background_supervisor_at`); `next_suggestions` is the effective "suggest the next message" switch for chats without a suggestion of their own (`false` if never changed); `owner_reply_approval` enables exact one-shot connector replies and `persistent_owner_action_cards` keeps their unanswered proposals until a decision (both `false` if never changed), and `owner_reply_approval_phrases` is their exact phrase list (default `["发","同意"]`; see "Exact owner replies for connector batches"); `agent_tasks` is the legacy switch for supervising manually linked user to-dos and reporting-Agent compatibility (`false` if never changed; it does not adopt manually opened Agents); `inbox_signals` is the effective "tell a task's supervisor about new Inbox messages on it" switch (`false` if never changed); `claude_interactive` is the effective "run Claude chats in interactive Claude Code" switch (`false` if never changed); `interject_background` is the effective "move running work to the background when I interject" switch (`false` if never changed); `notes` is present only if saved in the web app; `timezone_picked` is present once a client said whether the user picked `timezone` by hand (below); `main_tasks_quiet` is the effective value of "notify tasks dispatched by the main chat only in the main chat" (`true` if never changed); `idle_close_hours` is the effective number of hours an idle Agent Persona started stays open before the hub closes it (default 12, 0 is off); `archive_closed_days` is the effective number of days a closed session stays listed before the manager archives it by itself (default 3, 0 is off); `main_background_folded` is the effective "fold background rounds" switch: the web app folds the main chat's rounds that another chat, a scheduled task or a follow-up started into one line (`true` if never changed); `main` is the main chat's session id (on the `machine_id` machine); archived chats are not listed by default, `?archived=1` includes them (`archived: true`). `?tag=<tag>` keeps only chats carrying that exact user tag (a row's `tags`, below; an unknown tag lists none). `?space=<slug>` lists chats in a track, with `cwd` being the track's directory; without `space` only the assistant's own are listed, not the track chats; any other `space` returns 400. An extension's token is listed no track chat, in either space. A conversation row carries `tags: string[]` only when it has user-defined labels (omitted otherwise): at most 10 trimmed, de-duplicated tags of at most 32 runes each, pushed with the same snapshots as titles and archives |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/history` | Full role only. GET returns `{enabled,stats:{conversations,items,payload_bytes,summary_bytes,incomplete}}`; PUT requires `{enabled:boolean}`. Database-first assistant history defaults to enabled; false rolls reads and collection back to the runtime without deleting data. |
| GET | `/api/v1/remote-image?url=&size=` | A picture a reply names by address, fetched, checked and scaled by the manager (`remote_images`); see "Remote images" |
| GET | `/api/v1/avatars/{source}/{value}?size=` | A person's or a conversation's picture the lists name (`avatar_url`), drawn by the extension manager from the source's ref or an https address; see "Avatars" |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant` | `{"machine_id"?,"launcher"?,"timezone"?,"timezone_picked"?,"notes"?,"main"?,"main_tasks_quiet"?,"main_background_folded"?,"idle_close_hours"?,"archive_closed_days"?,"interject_background"?,"claude_interactive"?,"agent_tasks"?,"close_ended_terminals"?,"inbox_signals"?,"next_suggestions"?,"owner_reply_approval"?,"persistent_owner_action_cards"?,"owner_reply_approval_phrases"?,"main_supervises_own_tasks"?}`, stored in Postgres settings; only the fields present are changed; Values are checked (`400` otherwise; `idle_close_hours` is 0–8760; `archive_closed_days` is 0–3650; an empty string for `notes` also counts as a change; `main` of `"-"` clears the main chat (sent together when switching machines); `timezone_picked`: `true` with a `timezone` the user picked by hand (without one, the zone in effect becomes the picked one), `false` to follow the devices again; while the saved value is `true`, a `timezone` sent without `timezone_picked` (a device syncing its own zone) is left out and the answer still has the picked zone. `owner_reply_approval` and `persistent_owner_action_cards` accept booleans; `owner_reply_approval_phrases` accepts the validated exact phrase list, including an empty list. The response carries the saved values |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks/input-context` | Resolve the effective execution environment for a draft with the same execution fields as task save. An existing task supplies its `id`. A missing managed default directory is prepared on the selected computer. An explicit path is validated there. The response includes `execution`, `task_input`, and an opaque `skill_scope` for comparing the resolved conversation and profile choice across preview and discovery. When the node cannot accept selections, `input_error` describes the reason. With `task_input:true` and a request for `catalog:true`, the response also includes the applicable skill catalog or a discovery error. |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/conversations` | `{"prompt","images"?,"launcher"?,"model"?,"effort"?,"service_tier"?,"purpose"?,"machine_id"?,"main"?,"space"?,"report_tasks"?,"via"?}` → `{"session"}`: writes CLAUDE.md, then starts a new session in the assistant directory. `via` marks a prompt that the user did not type; any non-empty value marks it, and such a message never counts as the user's own words for a secret hand-off's Always rule, and the same field on a message to an assistant conversation (`…/messages`) does the same. `launcher` / `model` / `effort` are the first message's, as a message's pick: `service_tier` (feature `assistant_start_service_tier`) is the native speed ID advertised by the selected Codex model's `service_tiers`, currently `priority` for Fast; it is independent of `effort` and is acknowledged through `thread/settings/update` before the first `turn/start`, including when a warm thread is adopted. Omitting it makes no per-request speed override, so Codex's configured default remains effective; later messages omit it and the native thread retains its acknowledged setting. An existing-session send gets 409 `assistant_service_tier_start_only`, a non-Codex start 409 `assistant_service_tier_unsupported`, and a native refusal 409 `assistant_service_tier_refused`, all with `delivered: "none"` and no turn. A native refusal stops the cold or warm-adopted process before conversation, mode or recovery state is saved. These coded summaries are localized in en, zh-Hans and ja, without exposing the native English diagnostic as person-facing detail. A nonempty value requires the node capability `assistant_service_tier` and returns 409 `node_outdated` before starting on an older node. A manager without `assistant_start_service_tier` in its hello gets no relay and the client gets 501 `assistant_service_tier_manager_outdated`; an older hub ignores the unknown field, so capable web clients neither offer nor send it without the hub feature and default manager. `model` is any model ID (`proto.ValidModelID`, else 400; a typed one the list lacks is kept), for `launcher` or else the purpose's launcher; 400 when that launcher sets its own model (`locked`) or its agent takes none, before anything starts; a `launcher` that isn't on the computer falls back to the purpose's, its `model` dropped. Without `purpose` or `guest`, a named `launcher` or `model` (with `effort`) is kept as the new chat's `model_pick` (in the answer's `session` too) so its later messages keep it (feature `assistant_model_pick`); an `effort` alone, nothing named, or a fallback keeps nothing. A `main: true` start after `/clear` starts on the cleared main chat's pick unless it names a launcher or model (its `effort` is then the first message's only); when it names neither, the manager discards an explicit `service_tier` rather than applying it to that carried pick, so a client choosing Fast must name the launcher or model whose displayed setup it belongs to; a carried pick that can't run any more refuses that start once (409 `launcher_out_of_scope` / `launcher_own_service` / `launcher_missing`, or 400) and is dropped, so the next start runs on the default. `space: "health"` starts it in a track's directory (the health CLAUDE.md); together with `main: true` it's 400, and any other `space` is 400. `purpose`: which model purpose to use (one the hub knows, e.g. `lark.agent`; unknown 400; empty means `assistant`); `machine_id`: which of the hub's machines to run on (empty means the assistant's; unknown machine 400). The plugin's /agent uses these two. `report_tasks: true`: tasks dispatched by this chat (`task_plan`, `agent_start`) are, like the main chat's "quiet tasks", not pushed separately; their status changes are sent into this chat as task notifications; the plugin's /agent sets it. `guest: {"tools": [...]}`: starts a guest conversation: it can use only these 1–8 connector tools, runs in its own directory with no built-in tools and no live snapshot, can't be combined with `main` / `space`; 400 when the node is too old. The answer has `launcher_note` when the configured launcher can't run there and one of the same kind runs it instead. |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/assistant` (Agent naming) | `agent_auto_naming` (effective default `true`), `agent_auto_naming_max` (effective default `1`, integer 1–1000), `agent_auto_naming_interval_hours` (effective default `0`: periodic updates off; integer 0–8760). A sparse PUT requires full credentials and an explicit assistant in `X-Persona-Manager` or `?manager=`; conflicting or missing targets are rejected. The success response includes the owner and effective values. The count is successful automatic name changes per session, including periodic refreshes; refresh requires new output tokens and never overrides manual titles. Older managers omit these fields, so clients must not infer support. |

An encoded payload over 3500 bytes, or `machine_id` / `session_id` over 128 bytes, returns 400. Callable with full-access credentials and extension credentials with the `notify` scope; a non-extension credential sending `actions`/`ui`/`state` gets 400. If the hub's push grading holds the alert, it returns `{"sent":false,"held":true,"reason":"ln_p1_held"\|"ln_p2_silent"\|"ln_dedup_12h"}` without delivering to `ws_notify` or Web Push; if no recipient is selected on either channel, it returns `{"sent":false,"reason":"no_device"}` when no device has a usable push route and no capable WebSocket connection is online, or `{"sent":false,"reason":"filtered"}` when all reachable recipients are excluded by notification preferences (including manager switches) or desktop suppression. `{"sent":true}` only means it was handed to push, a capable WebSocket connection or a browser's Web Push, not that it was delivered; asynchronous push or relay failures do not change this reply |
| GET | `/api/v1/personas` | Avatars: `{"personas":[{"id","rev","bytes","manifest":{persona.json as is}}]}`; the packages under `~/.persona/personas/` that pass the checks (all files present, id matches the directory name, within the size limit); `rev` is a hash of the whole package content and changes if any byte changes, and clients cache by rev. An empty list when there are no packages |
| GET | `/api/v1/personas/{id}/{file…}` | One file from the package (PNG / SVG / persona.json); only regular files inside the package directory (no following symlinks, no dotfiles); extension avatars only serve files named in the manifest, and SVGs are sanitized (with CSP); when `?rev=` is the current rev, `Cache-Control: immutable` is set |
| GET | `/api/v1/looks` | All avatars: `{"looks":[{"id","source":"builtin\|hub\|extension","name","names?","subtitle?","subtitles?","app_icon","extension?","extension_name?","rev?","bytes?","manifest?","uploaded?"}],"current":{"id":the chosen one or null,"effective":the one to show,"updated_at?"}}`; built-in avatars first, then avatar packages and extension avatars (`/api/v1/personas` lists them too); a database read failure returns 500 `internal` without reporting a default choice |
| PUT | `/api/v1/looks/current` | `{"id", "if_unset?"}` choose an avatar (stored on the hub, synced across clients), returns the new `current`; not in the list 404; with `if_unset`, if the hub already has a choice it's returned unchanged. A change broadcasts `look`; with `if_unset`, a database read failure returns 500 `internal` without saving or broadcasting a choice |
| POST | `/api/v1/looks/uploads` | `{"name", "subtitle?", "image", "choose?"}` makes an avatar from an image: `image` is base64 (or a `data:` URL) of a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 8 MB and 40 million pixels, at least 64 px a side; clients send it cropped square and upright, and the hub crops a non-square one to its centered square. The hub writes a format-1 package `personas/u-<hex>/` (avatar at 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 px, a still dot frame per state, `source.kind: "upload"`) and returns `{"look": <as GET /looks lists it, "uploaded": true>, "current?"}`; with `choose` it is chosen too (`current`, broadcast `look`). Broadcasts `personas`. Refusals carry `code`: 400 `no_name` / `bad_name` (1–40 characters, no control or bidi formatting characters) / `bad_subtitle` (≤ 80) / `no_image` / `not_image` / `too_small`, 413 `too_large` / `too_many_pixels`, 409 `too_many` (50 uploaded avatars). Full credentials only |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/looks/uploads/{id}` | Deletes an avatar made from an upload and returns `{"current"}`; when it was the chosen one, the default is chosen (broadcast `look`). Broadcasts `personas`. 404 `not_found`; 409 `not_uploaded` for any other package (placed by hand, built in, an extension's). Full credentials only |
| GET | `/api/v1/plugins` | The hub's plugins: `{"plugins":[{"id","name","kind","status","error"?, "version", "source", "enabled", "contributes", "needs_setup"?, "nodes"?, "node_status"? …}], "can_install"}`; `status` is `disabled / needs_setup / incompatible / stopped / starting / running / error` — for an extension whose program runs on computers, while the hub runs no process of its own, `status` is aggregated from its machines and `node_status` carries the counts; only present when `features` has `plugins` |
| GET / PUT / DELETE | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/-/…`, `/api/v1/plugins/-/…` | Plugin details, switch, config and secrets (full-access devices), preview / install / upgrade / rollback / uninstall (main token over loopback only); only present when `features` has `plugin_manager` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}` | Port probe: `{"port","listening","http","title"?}`, only looks, doesn't allow |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}/open` | The user taps a port in the web app that doesn't belong to any Agent: if something is listening it's allowed for 24 hours and returns the same as above; nothing there 404; read-only device 403 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}/connect` | Port forwarding: upgrades to a WebSocket whose binary messages are the bytes of one TCP connection (the client listens locally and connects once for each connection the browser opens). The port must be in `ports` of some session on this machine or have been opened, otherwise 403; not listening 404; read-only device 403; machine offline 503; more than 64 concurrent per machine 429. For the live screen (5900 with `pair`) a client may offer the subprotocol `persona-screen-link.1`, and `attach=1` to rejoin a live session; the hub selects it only when the node answers with a screen session, and a session to rejoin that is gone is 410 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/servers?cwd=` | Dev servers of a session's folder (feature `preview`): `{file?, servers: [{name, port?, url?, command?, env?, cwd?, listening, title?, problem?}], error?, browser?}` from its `.claude/launch.json`; a node without previews 409 `node_outdated` |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/start` | `{cwd, name, workspace, kind?}`: runs that `launch.json` entry in a new terminal tab of the workspace → `{pane, terminal, port}`; read-only device 403. A runtime's workspace (a Paseo session's `workspace_id`, which has no terminal) runs it in the terminal engine's workspace holding the entry's folder, else in a new workspace there; a computer whose engines open no tabs answers 409 `preview_no_terminal` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/connect?port=&path=&w=&h=&dpr=&mobile=1` | A dev server preview: upgrades to a WebSocket of JSON text messages and binary pictures. Same port rules as `…/ports/{port}/connect` (403, 503, 429) and 409 `node_outdated`, before the upgrade; when the node cannot open it, after the upgrade one message `{t: "error", code, error}` and the close (`port_gone`, `no_browser`: no Chrome / Chromium / Edge / Brave on that computer, `browser_failed`, `offline`, `failed`), since a browser cannot read why a WebSocket was refused |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/messages?cursor=&limit=` | Messages of one personal-Agent session (`id` is `<source>:<sessionKey>`, percent-encoded in the path) → `{session?, messages, hasMore, nextCursor?}`; to page back, pass the previous `nextCursor` |
| POST | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/messages` | Send a message `{"clientId"?,"text","origin"?}` → `{outbox, duplicate, upstream?}`; if `clientId` isn't given the hub generates one, and resending the same one won't send twice (`duplicate: true`); `origin` defaults to `app`; empty text or a `clientId` that isn't a UUID 400, over 20000 (counted in UTF-16) 413; `clientId` already used on another session, or the session can't send right now (`canSend=false`) 409 |
| POST | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/read` | Mark this session as read → `{"ok":true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/avatar` | The session's avatar image as is, with `ETag`; a matching `If-None-Match` returns 304; cached for a day |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/outbox?session_id=&limit=` | The personal Agents' outbox `{"outbox":[{clientId, sessionId, preview, length, origin?, status, error?, attempts, createdAt, updatedAt}]}`; `status` is `sending` / `sent` / `failed` / `deleted` (resending a `failed` one with the same `clientId` is safe) |
| Any | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/-/machines/{mid}/{path…}` | HTTP to the plugin's program on computer `mid` (`node.http`), WebSocket too: the hub opens a stream via `plugin.node.dial` and forwards, stripping `Authorization` and `token`; full-access devices only; plugin not enabled on this machine 404, machine offline 409, program not responding 502 |
| Any | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/{path…}` | Forwarded as is to the plugin's `/{path…}` (except paths starting with `/-/`) (WebSocket too), stripping `Authorization` and `token`; read-only device 403. |

**Limits on reading files by path** (`file`, `file/download`, `file/thumb`, `file/convert`, `stat`, `fs`; the node's `pathguard.go`): only for authenticated clients (device tokens). Symlinks are resolved one segment at a time and **each segment is checked before it is looked at**, so anything reached through a link is blocked too, and the target is never touched:
- **iCloud** (any segment containing `Library/Mobile Documents`, case-insensitive): touching it on a locked Mac hangs, so `stat` treats it as nonexistent and reads are refused.
- **Sensitive files**: the whole directories `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, `.azure`, `.kube`, `.docker`, `.password-store`, `Library/Keychains`, `.local/share/keyrings`, `.config/gcloud`, `.config/gh` under home,
  `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.credentials.json`, `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` in every Claude Code config directory the node knows (`~/.claude`, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, those seen in running claudes or listed by the hub), `auth.json` in every Codex home it knows (`~/.codex`, `$CODEX_HOME` of the configured and discovered homes), private keys named `id_rsa` / `id_ed25519` etc. anywhere, and the data folder's credentials where they are written, in any `.persona` / `.persona` folder and in the folder `PERSONA_HOME` names: directly in it or in a manager's folder (`managers/<id>/`), the files whose names start with `hub.json` (including backups `hub.json.*`), `link.json`, `tailcat.json`, `tailcat-hub.json`, `daemons.json`, `manager.json`, `apns`, `relay.json`, `relay.secret`, `devices.json`, `mail_accounts.json`, and the `.key` / `.p8` / `.pem` / `.crt` files; and `launcher-settings/`, `tls/`, `link-tls/`, `extensions/data/` (the extensions' own data, their sign-ins and tokens among it), `extensions/staging/` (what an uninstall or an upgrade sets aside of it), `plugins/` (paths through it are refused, use `extensions/`) and `node-plugins/` (the programs extensions run on a computer and their data), whole, the folders themselves included; a link standing where one of these, or a folder on the way to one, is named is not followed. The rest of the folder (a `.pem` deeper in it) stays readable, and so does a project's file of the same name elsewhere (with `PERSONA_HOME=~`, a project's `link.json` or `certs/dev.pem`). `stat` treats them as nonexistent; reading, listing and downloading are all refused.
- The Git panel reads the same files' content: `git/diff` and `git/blob` refuse these paths; `git/review` lists them with `refused` and without their hunks or line counts (both sides of a rename that has one); `git/show` still lists every file of the commit but leaves the refused ones (both sides of a rename or copy that has one) out of `diff` (with no working tree to check the names against, a bare repository or a `cwd` inside `.git`, `diff` is empty).
- **A manager's folder anywhere** (`personad manager join/run --dir`): a folder holding a manager's `manager.json` (one naming its hub and token, or one that doesn't read but may hold a token) has the same credentials refused as a data folder's (`manager.json` and its copies, `secret.key` and the other keys, the same folders), also when they are not in the working tree any more. The folder is only looked at for such names, once the links up to it are followed; a link named `manager.json`, or a placeholder of one that is not downloaded, counts as a manager's without being opened.
- Links are followed at most 40 levels deep (a loop stops it). This is basic protection, not a sandbox: a device token can already have an Agent read these files.

For mail, see "Mail API" below. For the HTTP error format and optional fields, see "Error body" above.

### Computer trust (feature `machine_trust`)

A signed-in device can add a computer itself (feature `machines_add`); an added computer starts out **pending** (`trust: "pending"`) and is confirmed only when the user taps **It's mine**.
Trust is stored in the Postgres table `machine_trust`, and **no record = confirmed**: machines added via `/admin` and via `hub pair --machine` are confirmed directly. A pending computer:

- Doesn't receive Persona-managed providers (the assistant's `pushManaged` and `launchers.catalog` / `launchers.managed` on new connections all skip it, and `launchers.pull` is refused); all its requests to the manager (`assistant.context`, MCP tools) are refused;
- Isn't an assistant machine (`defaultAssistantMachine` and hello's `assistant.machines` exclude it), isn't in the assistant's `devices.list` (dispatch, starting Agents and to-dos don't see it), and the hub doesn't forward the assistant's `device.call` to it;
- `POST /api/v1/sessions` starting an Agent on it returns 409 `machine_pending`;
- Is still listed in the machine list (the web app shows the confirmation), with `error` set to "Waiting for you to confirm this computer is yours in the latest app or on the web", followed by the original `error` in parentheses;
- Is deleted automatically if not confirmed within 24 hours (the hub.json entry and the record; its Persona Link credential and unused pairing codes are revoked), the same as `reject`.

After rejection or timeout deletion the record is gone (so it looks confirmed), but until the manager disconnects it (config changes take a moment), the hub still keeps it out as pending, and the machine list no longer lists it, so hello won't treat it as a just-confirmed computer and push keys to it.
When the hub can't read pending computers (database unreachable), every computer is kept out as pending (the machine list doesn't mark `trust`), re-read every 5 seconds until it succeeds; no timeout deletion happens during that time. When the manager can't read them, requests from computers are refused with the error "the hub's database isn't responding", without saying the computer is waiting for confirmation.
`error` for `confirm` / `reject` is localized by `Accept-Language` (403 `forbidden`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `not_pending`).

Once confirmed, hello's machine list includes it, and the assistant then pushes keys to it. Issuing a code, redeeming, confirming, rejecting, timeout deletion and deleting it in the admin console (`remove`) are all written to the `machine_audit` table (who, when, what was done, no credentials).
How a device adds a pending computer: see "Computer pairing codes" under "Temporary pairing" above.

### Renaming a computer (feature `machine_rename`)

`PUT /api/v1/machines/{id}/name` `{"name"}` → `{"ok": true, "name"}`: a signed-in full device (as for `confirm`) gives the computer another name; `""` is its id again. The admin page does the same with
`PUT /api/v1/admin/machines/{id}` `{"name"}`, and the computer's own Persona Link with `rename` on its link. Only the name changes: the id, and everything kept by it
(pins, mutes, trust, credentials), stays.

- The hub writes `name` into the hub.json entry (or, for a computer its manager keeps in its own list, into that list through
  `devices.machines.put`) and takes it at once: no restart (the admin page's restart list doesn't count it), no reconnect (the manager keeps the machine and its connection when only the name
  changed). Every client gets a `machines` event with the new name; the computer's Persona Link gets `endpoints` with `machine_name`; the hub's own texts (notifications, errors, the assistant's `devices.list`) use it.
- Names are one line, at most 40 characters: 400 `invalid_name` otherwise; 404 `not_found` for an id hub.json doesn't have (a linked hub's computer is renamed on its own hub, and the center follows its record);
  403 `forbidden` for a device that isn't a full one. `error` is localized by `Accept-Language`.
- The manager's `devices.rename` `{machine_id, name}` → `{name}` carries a Persona Link's request: only for a machine of its own, refused with code `pending` while the user hasn't confirmed the computer.
- Each rename is written to `machine_audit` (action `rename`, detail `{from, to, via}`; `via`: `admin` / `device` / `link` / `system`).
- A computer that pairs while its name is still its id is named once after its system (`system_name` in the pairing request, `POST /api/v1/auth/tokens`, via `system`).
- Clients show a rename entry only when hello's `features` has `machine_rename`.

### Start defaults

An optional policy of what a task Agent starts with beyond what its caller named, by the kind of work; with no policy,
an expired one or no rule that fits, a task starts exactly as without the feature, apart from the Codex goal default
below. It is one setting on the assistant
(`start_defaults` in `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/assistant`, full credentials; empty rules clear it) and has its own route,
`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/assistant/start-defaults`, open to full credentials and to an extension token granted
`assistant.start_defaults` (an extension's policy must expire within one hour). Its shape:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "applies_when": {"supervisor": ["main"], "role": "worker", "readonly": false},
      "then": {
        "candidates": [{"name": "<preset>", "priority": 10, "weight": 2}, {"name": "<other preset>"}],
        "effort": "max",
        "ultracode": true,
        "goal": "done_when",
        "plan_first": false
      }
    }
  ],
  "expires_at": "2026-11-15T10:00:00Z"
}
```

- `applies_when`: every field optional, an empty one matches anything. `supervisor` takes the dispatch policy's classes
  (`main`, `leader`, `background_supervisor`, `scheduled`, `other`) for the conversation that follows the task up,
  stored as its distinct classes (a repeated class is accepted and deduped, so an accepted policy always fits the
  write body limit on its dual-name read); `role` is `worker` or `leader`; `readonly` true or false. `when` is
  accepted as another name for `applies_when`: writes accept either, reads answer both with the same value, and a body
  that names both must make them agree.
- `then`: every field optional. `candidates` are Agent presets (see
  `GET /api/v1/assistant/worker-presets`): the highest `priority` with at least one usable candidate wins, and within
  it the first usable one, or one of them by `weight` when weights differ. An omitted `priority` is 0; a candidate the computer cannot start is passed
  over and named in the task's `why`, and a whole unusable priority group falls through to the next. `presets` is
  accepted as another name for `candidates`, handled like `when`. `effort` one of `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`;
  `ultracode` a boolean (`true` turns it on for a task that did not set it; `false` asks for nothing); `goal` either
  `done_when` (a goal from the task's `done_when`) or `off` (no start goal, which turns off the Codex default below);
