| `github_comment` / `github_review` | hub (GitHub connector) | write: goes through `connector_gate`; by default each one is confirmed in the web app. The card states repo#number "title", the full text and who will see it; approvals start with [Approve] |
| `<connector id>_*` | hub (connector) | only for the assistant, and only for connectors whose status is `ok`. Read-only tools run directly; writes first go through `connector_gate` in the manager's manager.json, which by default creates a `permission` interaction (the card states who will see it), and run only after approval in the web app (`server/internal/connector`) |


## Connector API

Feature `connectors` (in the `features` of `/health` and the WebSocket hello).

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors?all=1` | `{"connectors":[{id, name, status, account?, via?, error?, guide?:[…], last_sync?, last_event?, capabilities:[…], hosts?:[…], enabled, inbox?}]}`: connectors registered on the hub. Without `all=1`, Lark (`lark`) and mail (`mail`) are excluded, because each has its own row; with it they are listed too (their status is also readable from `/api/v1/lark/status` and `/api/v1/mail/accounts`). `guide` is a one-sentence-per-step fix when something's wrong (how to enable permission on that Mac when the Messages connector lacks it). `status` is `ok` / `not_configured` / `not_signed_in` / `no_permission` / `rate_limited` / `error` / `disabled` (the user turned it off in settings; `enabled` is false); `via` says where the sign-in comes from ("gh sign-in from <machine>"); `error` is one human-readable sentence, without secrets; `capabilities` are drawn from `status` / `tools` / `actions` / `events` / `hosts` / `inbox` / `archive` / `login`; `hosts` are the hostnames of this connector's links (the web app uses them to recognize links); `inbox` is whether "Send to Inbox" is on, only present for connectors with the `inbox` capability |
| GET | `/api/v1/subscriptions?connector=&extension=` | source subscriptions → `{subscriptions: [Subscription], features: {deliver, generate}}`; `Subscription`, its `state` (`off` / `ok` / `failing` / `not_connected` / `rate_limited` / `needs_recipe`) and `error {code, message}` are. Every device may read |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions` | `{connector, source, recipe?, recipe_origin?, label?}` → 201 `Subscription`, both destinations off; a recipe that fails its checks is 422 with its code and `dry_run`; `recipe_origin: "model"` records a model's draft taken as it was |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions/-/ui` | the subscription pages as declarative UI, with an extension page's request and answer (`context`, `state`, `action`, `values` → `{view}` or an action's result). Every device may draw them; an `action` needs full access (403 `read_only_device`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/thread?thread=&before=&limit=` | connectors with the `threads` capability: one page of messages of an Inbox thread (the entry's `connector.thread`) → `{chat: {id, name, kind, url?, avatar?, members?, reply?, state?, author?, labels?, branch?, body?, body_format?}, messages: [{id, at, sender: {id?, name, avatar?}, mine?, event?, text?, format?, media?: [{kind, ref?, thumb?, mime?, name?, size?, duration?, width?, height?, emoji?}], reply_to?: {id, from?, text?}, edited?, url?, kind?, review?, code?, check?}], before?}`, oldest first; `before` pages back, and its absence means the start was reached; `limit` defaults to 30, at most 50. `chat.members` is a group's member count / a channel's subscriber count, given only on the first page (without `before`) and omitted when unknown. A lark-cli page takes `kind` (`dm` / `group`) and `name` from the chat's own record (`im chats get`, read beside the messages and kept an hour; one that is refused is asked for again a minute later): its message list says neither. A direct chat's record has no name, so the page is named for the other person in it. Not signed in or switched off 409 (`code: unavailable`); the source refused 403 (`code: no_permission`); rate limited 429 (`code: rate_limited`, `error` says how much longer); no such connector 404. An item with no conversation of its own, a source subscription's (its `source` is the subscription's id, its thread `sub:<subscription>:…`, deleted since or not) or a connector's without `threads`, answers 200 with `{chat: {id: <thread>, name: "", kind: "none"}, messages: []}`: the web shows what the hub collected (the item's `context`) as for any page that is neither a chat nor GitHub's thread, with no error |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/media?ref=` | passive media behind `avatar` / `ref` / `thumb` in a page. Fresh and cached bytes must identify JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or one of the passive audio/video containers listed; `Content-Type` comes from the bytes, never the connector's declared MIME. Unsupported bodies (including HTML and SVG disguised as images) receive 415 JSON; empty or over-4-MiB connector answers remain 502. Responses written by this handler, including errors, carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`. Accepted bodies keep `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`; the hub stores them in `<hub directory>/cache/connector-media/` (at most 256 MB, oldest deleted first), and many concurrent requests for the same ref ask the connector only once |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/thread/reply` | `{thread, action, text, reply_to?}`: reply in the thread using the action given by the page's `chat.reply` (params `{chat, text, reply_to}`) → `{ok, result}`. Requests from the user's own devices (full device token) run directly without `connector_gate`; other identities such as pairing tokens still go through the gate, and refusals are 403 (`code: declined`). Rate limited 429 |

## Mail API

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/accounts` | `{"accounts":[MailAccount]}` (no passwords) |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/accounts` | add an account (password / authorization code): saved only after a successful connection test → `{"account"}`; `auth:"oauth2"` always returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}?mailbox=INBOX` | `{"message":MailMessage}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}/attachments/{attachment_id}?mailbox=INBOX` | download by account, mailbox, UID and the stable attachment ID from the details; same Bearer authentication as mail reads; supports `Range` / `If-Range`, returning `Accept-Ranges` / `Content-Range`, 206 or 416 |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}/flags` | `{"mailbox","seen"?,"flagged"?}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/send` | `{"account_id","to":[],"cc":[],"bcc":[],"subject","text","html"?,"in_reply_to"?,"references"?}`; `references` is a space-separated Message-ID string, but a string array is also accepted (the hub joins it with spaces) |

The mail details page first reads the body and attachment list, then submits `{"mailbox":"INBOX","seen":true}` via `/flags`. The details GET uses `BODY.PEEK`, so reading a message does not mark it read. Attachments include a stable `id`, filename, MIME type and decoded size; IDs bind the MIME order, file metadata and decoded content, so attachments with the same name can be distinguished. Downloads also use read-only `BODY.PEEK`, with no dependency on extensions such as BINARY; the server streams decoded content into a temporary file, then returns byte ranges of the decoded content via HTTP Range. Unknown attachments or changed content return 404; an account the manager doesn't have is 404 `mail_account_unknown`, with an `error` that names the account in the request's language (`/test` still answers `{"ok":false,"error"}`); a mailbox that couldn't be reached even after reconnecting once is 502 `mail_unreachable`, its `error` in the request's language.

```jsonc
// MailAccount
{"id":"acc_…","name":"Gmail","email":"me@example.com","provider":"gmail|feishu|imap","auth":"password|oauth2",
 "username":"…","imap_host":"imap.gmail.com","imap_port":993,"smtp_host":"smtp.gmail.com","smtp_port":465,
 "smtp_security":"tls|starttls","status":"ok|error","error":""}
// Extra field on add: password. With provider feishu, the supplied servers are ignored; the hub tries both imap/smtp.larkoffice.com and imap/smtp.feishu.cn (993 / 465, SSL), saving the first pair that signs in successfully
// MailSummary
{"account_id","mailbox","uid":123,"message_id","subject","from":{"name","email"},"to":[{"name","email"}],
 "date","snippet","seen":false,"answered":false,"flagged":false,"has_attachments":false}
// MailMessage = MailSummary + {"cc":[…],"text":"…","html":"…","attachments":[{"id","filename","mime","size"}],
//                               "in_reply_to","references":[…]}
```

## Inbox API

The hub collects Lark, mail and connector data in the background and hands it to the manager (assistant) to aggregate into entries (entries in `server/internal/assistant/inbox.go`, sources in `server/internal/extmgr/inbox.go`). The hub forwards these endpoints to it; when the manager isn't connected they return `503 assistant_offline`.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox` | `{items:[InboxItem], as_of, triage}`: unhandled entries + the newest 200 of the entries handled in the last 3 days (by `done_at`, then `id`; the rest are on `GET /api/v1/inbox/done`), newest `updated_at` first; excludes `context`. Defaults to Lark and mail only; connector entries (GitHub…) with a `connector` block require `?sources=all`. `triage`: `{state, reason?, waiting, sources?:[{source, name, state, reason, waiting, read_error?, read_reason?}]}`, how many new plugin-connector entries haven't entered the Inbox because they couldn't be triaged (and had no fallback) or weren't reached this round, and why; a source (a mail account as `mail:<account id>`, named by its address) the latest round couldn't read has `read_error` (`timeout` / `rate_limited` / `login_refused` / `failed`) and `read_reason`; when none, `{"state":"ok","waiting":0}`. `as_of` is when this list was read (hub clock, RFC 3339), sent back when handling in bulk by filter (`/bulk`). Each entry may also carry event fields: `status` (unhandled sections `action` / `working` / `fyi` / `noise`, falling back to `tier` when absent), `urgent`, `recap`, `handling`, `suggestion`, `chain` (handling chain, at most the latest 50 entries), `related`. An assistant row (`source` `assistant`) also has `body`: its text as Markdown, line breaks kept, which the detail draws; its `summary` and `preview` are the same words without the marks on one line |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/done` | `?before=&before_id=&limit=&sources=all` → `{items:[InboxItem], next?:{before, before_id}}`: done entries the manager keeps (90 days), newest `done_at` first, ties by `id` descending; entries as in the list. `before` (RFC 3339 `done_at`) and `before_id` start after that entry (pass `next` back as is); without `before`, from the newest. `limit` 1–200, default 50. `next` only when the page is full (the page after may be empty). `sources=all` as in the list. A bad `limit`, a `before` that is not RFC 3339, or `before_id` without `before` is 400. One manager's page: the one named (`X-Persona-Manager`), else the default; items carry `manager` but pages are never merged, so ask each manager and merge by `done_at`. Answer-only devices can't call it; extensions need `inbox.read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/done/days` | `?tz=<IANA zone>&sources=all` → `{tz, days:[{day, count}]}`: how many done entries the manager keeps (the same as `/api/v1/inbox/done` pages) fall on each calendar day in `tz` (`day` is `YYYY-MM-DD`), newest day first; days with none are left out. `tz` is required and must be a zone name the hub knows (`Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`; not `Local` or an offset), else 400: a day follows the zone's own offset on its date, across daylight saving. `sources=all` as in the list. The web's Done shows each day's count with it and jumps to a day with `/api/v1/inbox/done?before=<the day's end>` (no `before_id`: the entries done before that moment). One manager's counts, routed as `/api/v1/inbox/done`; answer-only devices can't call it; extensions need `inbox.read` |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}` | one entry, with `context` (plain text of the chat / email, for AI); mail also carries `reply_target:{uid,version}`. Also answers a done entry of the history (`/done` above) the list no longer has |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/done` | `{done: bool, dismiss?: bool}`: mark handled / reopen; returns the entry. With `dismiss` true, this is "Ignore" (`done_by=dismissed`). Reopening also brings back a done entry of the history the list no longer has (as do `/done` with `done:false` and `/bulk` `reopen`); marking one of those handled again is 404 (`missing` in bulk) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/done` | `{done: bool, items:[{id, version?}]}` → `{changed:[InboxItem], unchanged:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}]}`: mark multiple entries at once (mark all handled, all seen / clear all, and their undo), one database write and one `inbox` push. `version` is the entry's `version` from the list: when marking handled, a mismatch (new messages merged in since listing) leaves it unmarked, with `reason=changed` in `skipped`; a missing entry has `reason=missing`; one already in that state goes in `unchanged` without changing `done_at` (retries or simultaneous taps on another device don't write twice). Reopening doesn't compare versions. At most 1000 entries; more returns 413; no `done` returns 400. Only recorded in Persona, not written back as read to the source; `/bulk` below is the general form |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/bulk` | Clear all: `{action, items?:[{id, version?}], ids?:[id], filter?, as_of?}` → `{action, changed:[InboxItem], ids:[id], unchanged:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}], undo?:{action:"reopen", ids}}`. `action` is `done` (handled, `done_by=user`) / `dismiss` (ignored, `done_by=dismissed`) / `reopen` (reopen, for undo); clients send only `dismiss` for Clear all, keeping `done` for sections. **Either** provide `items` / `ids` (`ids` is shorthand without versions; both can be supplied): handle only these, with the same rules as `/done` (version mismatch on marking: `skipped reason=changed`; missing: `missing`; already in that state: `unchanged`); **or** provide `filter` + `as_of`: handle unhandled entries selected by `filter`, using the `as_of` returned by `GET /api/v1/inbox` (or `/refresh`); entries arriving after it, or with new messages merged after it, are left alone (`skipped reason=changed`). `filter`: `{sources?: "all", source?, account?, tier?, kinds?:[]}`, where `source` is lark / mail / connector id, `account` is `feishu` or a mail account id, `tier` is action / fyi / noise / untriaged, and `kinds` is a list of `kind` values; without `sources:"all"`, connector entries are excluded as in the list. Client-side filters such as search use `ids`. `reopen` only accepts `ids`. `ids` lists what changed this time; POSTing `undo` back as is undoes it (reopens only what changed this time). One database write and one `inbox` push for the batch; only recorded in Persona, not written back as read to the source. At most 1000 entries (413); unknown `action`, supplying both or neither of `ids` and `filter`, `filter` without `as_of`, `reopen` with `filter`, or unknown `tier` all return 400. Answer-only devices can't call it (403); extensions need `inbox.write` |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/merge` | Merge rows by hand: `{items:[{id, version?}]}`, 2 to 20 → `{item: InboxItem (the survivor, with merged_from), members:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}], undo:{id}}`; fewer than two mergeable left: 409; fewer than two sent: 400. Extensions need `inbox.write` |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/merge/undo` | `{id}` (the survivor) → `{changed:[InboxItem]}`: the members get their rows back; 404 when it has none |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/todo` | Add rows to to-dos: `{items:[{id, version?, title?}], due_at? | due_date?}` (the client works the due time out: a moment, or a day for all day) → `{changed:[InboxItem], unchanged, skipped, failed, todos:[{item:{id}, todo:Todo}], undo?:{items:[{id, todo_id}]}}`; each filed row is `done_by=todo`, a row not filed gets no to-do. `item` is an object |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/todo/undo` | `{items:[{id, todo_id}]}` → the bulk result: the to-dos are deleted and the rows reopened |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes` | `{mutes:[{id, source, source_name, tag, value, name, created_at}]}`: the user's mutes (`tag` is `repo` / `chat` / `sender`). Each entry in the list carries `mutes:[{tag, value, name}]`, saying how it can be muted |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes` | `{item_id, tag}` → `{mute, settled}`: mute this entry's value under `tag` (the hub reads it from the entry), settle open entries covered by it in the same source (`settled` count), and settle future arrivals; only one copy of each mute exists |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes/{id}` | unmute: future entries arrive normally; already settled entries don't return |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/policies` | `{policies:[{id, source, source_name, tag, value, name, tier?, twin?, created_at, updated_at}]}`: the user's policies: `tier` is `action` / `fyi` / `noise`, `twin` is `first` / `never`. An entry's policy is the one whose `source` and `tag` + `value` match one of its `mutes` options, `sender` before `chat` before `repo` |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/policies` | `{item_id, tag, tier?, twin?}` → `{policy, applied}`: set the policy of this entry's value under `tag` (read from the entry; nonexistent entry 404, unknown tag / tier / twin 400). A policy for the same target is updated; one left with neither `tier` nor `twin` is removed. Open triaged entries it covers get its tier at once (`applied` count) |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/inbox/policies/{id}` | `{tier?, twin?}` → `{policy, applied}`: set both parts as given; neither removes it; unknown id 404 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/inbox/policies/{id}` | remove a policy: entries keep the tier it gave until new content is triaged again |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/draft` | `{instruction?}` → `{text}`: draft a reply in the user's voice (not sent); `503 model_unavailable` when no model the hub can call directly is set up for drafting |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/reply` | `{text, changes?, client_id?, expected_uid?, expected_version?}` (if the assistant connection breaks mid-send: 502 `assistant_in_doubt`, `delivered:"unknown"`; it may already have been sent, and retrying the same one won't send twice; a send that did not go out answers why, `delivered:"none"`: `409 inbox_cannot_reply`, `503 inbox_source_unavailable` / `inbox_source_signed_out` / `inbox_send_unrecorded`, `502 inbox_send_denied` / `inbox_send_failed`, `429 inbox_send_rate_limited` with `retry_after`): send to the original Lark chat / as a mail reply / as a cloud-document comment (where `doc.reply` points), and mark handled (`done_by=replied`); returns the entry. For cloud documents, `changes:[{ref,field,value}]` changes statuses before commenting; `text` may be empty for status-only changes. With `client_id`, a receipt is saved, and Lark passes it through as upstream `clientId`; without it, `clientId` is computed from the entry id and text (UUIDv5), so retries after a hub restart don't duplicate it either. A Lark entry's same reply is sent only once: replies to the same entry are queued; an entry already handled by reply with the same text returns success directly without sending again. Different text is sent normally. Lark destination: DMs go into the chat; non-empty `lark.thread_kind` replies to `reply_to` within its topic; group @mentions (`kind=mention`) reply quoting `reply_to`; other groups and data without `reply_to` still send into the chat |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/suggestion` | `{version, action, text?, client_id?}`: act on the current suggestion (submitted by the manager's handling chat): `confirm` (execute as is, or after editing when `text` is supplied) / `reject` (return to the handling chat) / `instruct` (`text` required, return for a new suggestion) → this item. Confirmed replies use the same send-once path as `/reply`, but do not mark done (`handling.state=waiting`). Reply attempts are retained in optional `item.suggestion_attempts` with version, outcome, safe code/retryability, frozen actual text, update time and conversation; internal send identity and target bindings are not listed. Only confirmed retryable non-delivery may retry the same current version and frozen payload/identity. Sending or unknown attempts refuse a fresh-ID retry, including after reload. Error responses can include the authoritative `item`; a new suggestion is not overwritten by an older attempt completing. `409 {code:"suggestion_stale", error, item}` when `version` is not current or no suggestion remains; `409 inbox_item_done`; `400`; `403` for answer-only devices except text confirmation of replies or conclusions; `502 assistant_in_doubt` and the send-failure codes as in `/reply` |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/retry` | No body. Asks the owning manager to resume an open item with failed AI twin handling. Returns the updated item once the request is saved, with `handling.state` set to `looking` or `agent`. `409 {code, error, item}` with `inbox_retry_stale` if the item has moved on or `inbox_retry_disabled` if settings or policy prevent the retry. `404` unknown item, `403` answer-only device, `503` manager or storage unavailable. Extension scope `inbox.write`. |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/handoff` | Hand to AI with write-back, in two forms. `{text, client_id?, reuse_pending?}` sends `text` after a block naming the item to its main conversation (`session.send_once` with `client_id` as the message id; without one, a UUIDv5 of the item and text), or starts the main conversation with it. `{session:{machine_id, session_id}, kind:"agent"|"conversation", title?, client_id?}` without `text` only records a hand-off the client already sent: nothing is sent or woken, processing and done state stay unchanged, and the chain gets `agent` or `handling` with the session link and `via:user`. Both forms record `handoffs` so that conversation may write back with `inbox_suggest` `item`, and answer `{item, session:{machine_id, session_id}}`. The sending form's optional `reuse_pending:true` is for default Wrap up: reveal a waiting suggestion or reuse pending work for the same incoming item without another model message. New incoming work is distinct, and explicitly typed instructions keep normal handoff semantics (the default is false). Older managers may ignore this optional field. The same `client_id` again answers as before without recording or sending again; the record-only form derives a missing id from the item, session and kind. For the sending form, the hub keeps a receipt by `client_id` as for `/reply`, and answers `502 assistant_in_doubt` when the link to the manager breaks mid-request (retrying the same one won't send twice). `400` without text in the sending form, or with text / missing session ids / an invalid kind in the record-only form; `404` for an unknown item. A failed send or start records nothing and is answered as `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` answers it (a refusal the node codes `409` with its code, offline `503`, otherwise `502`, a work machine included). Not for answer-only devices (403) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/doc/status` | `{ref, field, value}`: set this row's status in a cloud document to `value` (must be an option for that column); read the latest value before writing (if someone just changed it, fails with 409); returns the reread entry |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/refresh` | collect once immediately, returning the list and `triage` (`?sources=all` as above); new plugin-connector entries enter the list after background triage finishes, without waiting for it. When the collect call itself fails, nothing was read now and it answers `502 {code:"inbox_refresh_failed", error, detail, retryable:true}` instead of the list (`error` a sentence in the request's language, `detail` the collect's error), so a refresh never looks like it worked when it did not; a source that could not be read within a round that did run is still `200`, named in `triage.sources[].read_error`. |
| PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/parent` | `{kind, id}` sets this entry's parent (`kind` is `inbox` / `todo` / `session`); `null` or `{}` removes it → this `InboxItem`; missing entry or parent 404, invalid parent 400, would create a cycle 409 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/folder` | `{folder}`: a `/`-separated path files the entry there by hand (`folder_by: user`), `""` takes it out of every folder, `null` hands it back to the model → this `InboxItem`; missing entry 404, a path that normalizes to nothing 400 |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/folders` | Folder settings and the folders in use: `{enabled, rules, folders: [{path, count, open}]}`; PUT takes `{enabled?, rules?}` and answers the same |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/tree/{kind}/{id...}` | a node's trail: `{node, item?, ancestors:[{kind, id, item?}], children:[InboxItem]}`, children ordered by start time; missing entry 404, invalid `kind` / `id` 400 |
| POST | `/api/v1/translate` | `{texts:[string]≤30, target}` → `{texts}`, preserving order; missing model outputs are empty strings. target is BCP 47 (zh-Hans, en, ja…). Like the Inbox, this belongs to the assistant (forwarded through the hub), using the "Translation" use in model configuration |
| POST | `/api/v1/translate/message` | `{text, target}` → `{text}`: translates one complete reply through purpose `translate`, preserving Markdown. Accepts 1–32000 characters; empty or oversized input is 400 (never silently clipped). Uses the existing translation model/cache, partitioned from clipped short texts and invalidated when its model binding changes. An empty model answer is 502. |
| POST | `/api/v1/translate/mail` | `{account_id, uid, mailbox, target}` → `{subject, text, clipped?, model_fingerprint?}`: the assistant asks the hub to read this mail (HTML-only mail becomes text preserving paragraphs and links), then translates it itself; returns the Inbox's existing translation if it used the same model; body at most 12000 characters. An account the manager doesn't have is 404 `mail_account_unknown`, as on the mail routes; other failures to read or translate the mail are 502 |

Mail replies may carry `expected_uid` and/or `expected_version` from the details response. The version binds the account, mailbox, UID in the thread, message identifier and sender. A changed target returns HTTP 409, `code=mail_reply_target_changed`, `delivered=none`, `retryable=false`; nothing was sent this time. The web app keeps the draft, loads the latest mail, and after the user confirms the new recipients makes a new request with a new `client_id`. When the network result is unknown, it checks the receipt using the original request, target and `client_id`. Omitting the validation fields skips the check.

`InboxItem`: `id`, `source` (lark / mail, or a connector id: github), `kind` (dm / mention / group / bot / mail; connectors define their own: review_requested / mention / team_mention / author / ci_failed / assign), `account` (`feishu` or a mail account id),
`account_name`, `title` (chat name / mail subject), `sender`, `avatar`, `preview` (latest message), `count`, `started_at`, `updated_at`,
`tier` (action / fyi / noise, empty before triage), `summary`, `reason`, `read` (seen elsewhere), `done_at` (the history's order and cursor, `GET /api/v1/inbox/done`), `done_by` (user / dismissed / read / replied; dismissed means the user chose "Ignore"), `version` (what this entry currently contains; changes when new messages merge in; sent back when marking handled in bulk),
`lark{account_id,ol_account,feed_id,is_group,is_topic,start_position,read_position,mention_position,at_all,reply_to,thread_kind}` (`account_id`: the Lark gateway account number this chat belongs to; `ol_account`: present for a non-default account, the `ol_account` to pass when opening the chat or calling Lark endpoints; `read_position`: this chat's read position in Lark, refreshed on every collection; `reply_to`: id of the last message sent by someone else; `thread_kind`: where it is, empty = in the chat, `topic` = a topic in a topic group, `thread` = a threaded reply in a regular group; these two refresh when new messages are collected), `conversation{source,id,account?,start_position?,read_position?,mention_position?}` (present in the list: where to open a Lark entry in the messaging source; `source` is the connector id, `account` is the `account` to pass for a non-default account), `mail{account_id,mailbox,uids,message_id,from,direct,thread}`,
`translations{<target language>:{subject,preview}}` (foreign-language mail the hub translates ahead of time), `doc{url,link,type(docx/doc/sheet/base/other),notice(mention/comment/reply),notice_id,rows:[{ref,table,title,fields:[{name,value}],status:[{field,name,value,options:[{name,color}]}]}],reply{kind(thread/record/cell/doc),label,…},error}`
(`kind=doc`); `agent.changes:[{ref,field,value}]` are status changes the AI twin proposes with its draft;
`connector{thread,label,url,open_url,reply_to,can_reply,rule_tier}`: a connector entry; the web app draws only this block, without knowing the specific source:
`label` is the row label, `url` opens inside the web app, `open_url` is handed to the system (`sms:` and similar), `reply_to` says where a reply goes and who can see it, and `can_reply` false means replies aren't allowed (CI failure).
When the list changes, WebSocket pushes `{"type":"inbox"}` (no content; the web app fetches it).

## Lark bot

`/api/v1/bots/feishu` (read status / change credentials, toggles and features), `…/pair` (pairing code), `…/owner` (DELETE unpairs).

## Messaging source API (`/api/v1/messaging`)

Sources from the `messaging` extension point (the first is Lark): `/api/v1/messaging/{source}/…` handles chats, messages, sending and so on. After authentication, the hub forwards to the extension and validates responses against the schema. `/api/v1/lark` below is the Lark-specific API the web uses.

## Lark API (Lark gateway)

These routes aren't the hub's own code: the hub has no direct connection to the Lark gateway, and `server/internal/lark` contains only the `lark` config (the manager's manager.json). `/api/v1/lark/…` is provided by the Lark plugin's `api` contribution; `lark` is a prefix being migrated out of the hub (`migratablePrefixes`, `server/internal/extmgr/extension_api.go`), and the plugin's contribution takes precedence. The hub authenticates first, removes `Authorization` and `token`, adds `X-Persona-Device` / `X-Persona-Role`, then forwards as is to the plugin, which asks the Lark gateway. Without a plugin providing them, these routes return 404. Below is the endpoint contract plugins must follow; "hub" mostly means the plugin the hub forwards to. The hub wraps plugin-declared `receipts` with send receipts.

All routes below accept the query parameter `ol_account=<Lark gateway account number>`: which Lark account this request uses (invalid returns 400). Without it, the plugin's default account is used, decided by the plugin's own Lark gateway config: the hub doesn't hand manager.json's `lark.account` to the plugin; it is only used for the assistant's Inbox (`server/internal/lark/config.go`). Media URLs for other accounts already carry it. For supported GET list and profile responses the manager also supplies the account-bound avatar paths described in [Avatars](#avatars).

On a Lark gateway error, the plugin returns 502 `{"error"}`; when the gateway itself lost its Lark sign-in (`AUTH_*`), it returns `{"error","code":"lark_not_logged_in"}`, which the web app uses to prompt the user to sign in to Lark again in the gateway. `/raw/…` is an exception: it forwards the gateway's own response as is.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/accounts` | `{"accounts":[{"id","name"?,"avatar"?,"tenant"?,"user_id"?,"signed_in","primary"?,"unread","quarantined"?}],"default"}`: Lark accounts signed in on the gateway (in gateway order; `signed_in` is false for quarantined accounts) and the default account number. A gateway without an account list returns only the default account |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/status` | `{"configured","connected","name","error","last_event_at"}`: Settings › Connectors › Lark. configured comes from the plugin's own Lark gateway config; connected asks the gateway's `/accounts` on every request; last_event_at is the latest live event (Unix seconds) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/message-display` | `{"account_id","anti_recall","show_edit_history"}`: display settings of the selected Lark account; returns only these two switches and the actual user ID, no script / auto-send config |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/message-display` | `{"account_id","key","value","expected"}`: key is `anti_recall` or `show_edit_history`, value/expected are booleans; full device permissions, body ≤1 KiB, unknown fields rejected; a restricted PATCH through the gateway preserves other fields. Account / old-value conflicts 409, unauthorized 403, gateway without the endpoint 404; expired sign-in 502 + `lark_not_logged_in`. Success returns the same structure as GET and pushes a `lark` event with `settings_changed=true`; unknown results aren't retried automatically |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations?scope=&cursor=&limit=` | `{"conversations":[LarkConversation],"next_cursor"}`; scope: `chats` (default, Lark "Messages": excludes completed / folded chats and filters by label display rules), `unread`, `done` (completed), `label:<id>`, `inbox`, `mentions`, `muted`, `p2p`, `group`, `thread`, `later` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/pinned` | all pinned chats (keeps reading the pinned head of inbox + done, merges and dedups, then sorts by pin time); pagination anomalies return an error rather than treating a truncated set as success |
| GET | `/conversations`, `/pinned` above with `account_bound=1` | additionally returns the actual selected `account_id`; an empty collection is `[]`; intermediary caching prohibited. May carry expected `account_id`; identity changes before / after the request or an expected-account mismatch return 409 `lark_account_changed` with no chat data. Not signed in still uses `lark_not_logged_in` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pins?account_id=&cursor=&limit=` | in-chat Pin list: `{account_id,items:[{id,message_id,message?:LarkMessage,operator_name?,created_at}],next_cursor,total}`. limit defaults to 50, max 100. Preserves upstream pagination fully; repeated / missing cursors return errors. This read clears the gateway's unread Pin marker, so home-page prefetching is prohibited |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pin-messages/{message}?account_id=&topic=` | locate a Pin: `{account_id,target:{message,root?,page}}`, with page in the same shape as chat / topic pagination. A regular message returns an around window; a reply returns the topic root and a reply window containing the target (at most 20×100 entries). A target that cannot be located returns 409; the client keeps the current window |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pins` | `{account_id,message_id,pin_id?,remove}` → `{account_id,pinned}`. remove=true requires the corresponding pin_id; before writing, verifies message feed, capabilities, Pin ownership and actual account. An unknown result returns `lark_pin_result_unknown`, requiring a reread to confirm, not an automatic retry. All three Pin APIs are `no-store`; account switch returns 409 `lark_account_changed` without data; missing original messages `lark_pin_not_found` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/labels` | `{"labels":[{"id","name","count"}]}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/unread-count` | `{"count"}`: "Unread N" (excludes muted chats) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/flags` | flags: `{"conversations":[LarkConversation],"messages":[{"feed_id","chat_name","chat_avatar","flagged_at","message":LarkMessage}]}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/labels` | `{"label_ids":[…],"labels":[{"id","name"}]}` (labels this chat belongs to / available labels) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/settings` | `{"done"?,"pinned"?,"flagged"?,"muted"?,"label_ids"?}` → gateway `PATCH settings` (isArchived / isShortcut / isFlagged / isMuted / labelIds; labelIds is the full set) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/unread` | `{"unread":true}` marks unread / `false` clears unread |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/messages?before=&after=&around=&limit=&topic=` | `{"messages":[LarkMessage],"has_older","has_newer","older_cursor","newer_cursor"}`, oldest→newest; no cursor = latest page; `around=<read position+1>` opens from the first unread message; `topic=1` fetches a topic group's topic list (backward paging only) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/thread?before=&limit=` | messages in a topic / reply thread, same format as above; supports only backward paging with `before`, reading the latest page without a cursor; no `after`, since upstream provides no forward pagination or cursor |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/messages` | `{"text","client_id"?,"mentions"?}` sends as the user, returning `{"ok":true,"message_id"?}`. `client_id` is a client-generated UUID passed as is to the gateway's `clientId` and stored with a receipt on the hub: resending the same message with the same id sends only one; missing or non-UUID values are generated by the hub. `mentions` is `[{"user_id","name"}]` (at most 100; exceeding the limit or missing `user_id` / `name` returns 400); `text` must contain literal `@name`; the hub doesn't rewrite text and passes it as is to the gateway's `mentions`; @everyone is `{"user_id":"all","name":"所有人"}` ("everyone") |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/replies` | `{"text","thread"?,"client_id"?,"mentions"?}` replies to this message as the user, returning `{"ok":true,"message_id"?}`. `thread=false` (default) quotes it in the original chat; `thread=true` sends into its topic (a top-level message in a regular group becomes the root of a new topic; in a topic group it goes into its topic). Proxies gateway `POST /messages/{id}/replies`, passing `client_id` as is as `clientId` and saving a receipt; `mentions` as in the previous row. The target may be a root message or a reply in a topic; upstream resolves topic ownership. Empty `text` returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/members?q=&limit=` | members for @mentions: `{"members":[{"user_id","name","avatar"?}]}`. Empty `q` lists members; non-empty searches names / group nicknames / pinyin; `limit` defaults to 50, at most 200; `name` prefers the group nickname, falling back to display name |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/images` | `{"client_id","name","mime","data"}`; data is base64, decoded size at most 7.5 MiB; image format validated; returns `{"message_id"}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/files?client_id=&name=&mime=` | raw `application/octet-stream` bytes, Content-Length required, 1 byte to 100 MiB; returns `{"message_id"}`; streamed through the hub |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/read` | `{"position","badge_count"?,"message_ids"?}`: report viewed messages (highest position, that message's badge_count, and unread message ids sent by others in between); only sent after messages actually appear on screen |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/read-states` | `{"message_ids":[…]}` (at most 100; more returns 400): read receipts for these messages, returning `{"states":[{"message_id","read_count","unread_count"}]}`. Messages the gateway provided no receipt for (still sending, unknown) don't appear in `states` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/media/{key}?size=` | images / stickers / avatars / videos / files forwarded as is (`size` returns a thumbnail when a multiple of 24 and ≤624) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/media/{key}` | message-scoped media (as above) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/emojis` | `{"emojis":{"<lowercase key>":{"label","url"}}}`, including skin-tone variant keys; cached by the hub for a day |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/card-actions/{actionId}` | press a card callback button as the user (body passed as is to the gateway) |
| GET / POST | `/api/v1/lark/raw/{path...}` | read-only proxy for gateway `/agent/v1/<path>`, forwarding queries and allowed read-only POSTs; not a general write endpoint |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/reactions/quick` | `{keys}`: quick reactions |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/reactions` | `{key,remove?}`: add or remove a reaction, returning `{ok:true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/users/{id}?feed_id=` | user profile, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/users/{id}/chat` | open a DM, returning `{feed_id}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/url-preview?url=` | link preview within a message, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments` | `{url, content, mentions?:[{user_id,name}], quote?, block_id?, client_id}`: post a new document comment as the user. Without `quote`, a whole-document comment; with `quote` (and its containing block `block_id`), a comment on that body passage. Each @mentioned person in `content` is written as `@name`, as in messages. Returns `{ok, threads, anchored?}`: `threads` is all threads read back after writing (same shape as `documents/comments`; null if unreadable, but the comment was sent); a comment on a passage also carries `anchored` (`false`: the containing block couldn't be found, so the passage is quoted in a whole-document comment instead). Body anchors use the gateway's inline comments; the plugin finds the block by `quote` in the document JSON (if the client knows `block_id`, it sends it directly). These routes exist only when the plugin declares `lark_doc_comments`; writes from the user's own device bypass the AI gate; recorded in receipts (receipt id derived from `client_id`, so retries with the same id don't send twice) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments/{thread}/replies` | `{url, content, mentions?, client_id}`: reply to this comment thread, returning `{ok, threads}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments/{thread}/resolve` | `{url, resolved}`: mark resolved (`true`) or reopen (`false`), returning `{ok, threads}`; invalid content and documents that don't support such comments return 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/documents/people?url=&q=` | `{members:[{user_id,name,avatar?}]}`: candidates for @mentions in comments, searched by name (same shape as group `members`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/moments/posts/{id}` | single-post content, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/moments/posts/{id}/comments` | single-post comments, upstream JSON forwarded as is |

The optional `client_id` for Lark sends, threaded replies and Inbox replies can be used directly for retries, with no extra request header required. The hub derives an internal receipt UUID from the operation kind and original ID, reusing Postgres `client_ops`; the same ID with the same target and params returns the original HTTP status and response body without sending again, even if the Inbox entry changed or the hub restarted. Reusing an ID with different params, target or authenticated device returns `409 {"code":"op_id_reused"}`. Recorded upstream errors are also returned as is, to avoid duplicate sends when the result is uncertain; execution not yet finished returns `202 {"state":"pending"}`, and execution left over after a restart without a result returns `202 {"state":"unknown"}`, which clients must verify. Receipts use the `client_ops` retention policy. When a request carries both `client_id` and `X-Persona-Op-Id`, the receipt derived from `client_id` wins.

Threaded replies use the separate operation kind `lark_thread_reply` with the same receipt rules. Before sending, the client keeps the topic draft and original request; on `202` or a lost receipt it stays pending confirmation, and submits the same target, text and `client_id` again to check the original result, never generating a new ID to resend. `ok:true` means upstream accepted it; the topic list is then reread.

Without `client_id`, the upstream client generates IDs for Lark chat sends, and the hub generates a stable ID per entry for Inbox Lark replies.

```jsonc
// LarkConversation
{"id":"<feedId>","name","avatar":"/api/v1/lark/media/…","is_group","is_topic","unread","marked_unread","at_me","at_all","muted",
 "pinned","flagged","done","tags":["外部"|"公开"|"会议"|"机器人"|"AI"…],"preview","preview_sender","is_mine","updated_at", // gateway tag values: External | Public | Meeting | Bot | AI
 "read_position","mention_position"}
// LarkMessage
{"id","position","sender_id","sender_name","sender_avatar","sender_type":"user|bot","is_mine",
 "type":"TEXT|POST|IMAGE|CARD|SYSTEM|FILE|MEDIA|STICKER|MERGE_FORWARD…","text":"plain-text preview","created_at",
 "recalled","retained"?,"edited","reply_count","thread_reply_count","badge_count","at_me","is_read",
 "parts":[MessagePart],                       // gateway content as is (see below); media URLs rewritten to /api/v1/lark/
 "olk"?:{…},                                 // encrypted projection: status, public cover text, authorized decrypted body, key distribution info
 "edit_history"?:[{"edited_at","text","parts"?,"olk"?}],
 "reply_to":{"id","sender_name","text","recalled","retained"?,"parts","olk"?},
 "reactions":[{"key":"THUMBSUP","count":2,"mine":true,"users":["Example member A","Example member B"]}]}
// MessagePart (the gateway's MessagePart; field names unchanged)
{"kind":"text|at|link|image|file|code|emotion|media|card|docs|interactive|table",
 "text","url","refId","metadata":{…}}   // the card's entire element tree is in metadata.body / header; rich-text block ancestors are in metadata.blocks
```

Sending attachments requires full device permissions (unavailable to answer-only devices) and uses the Lark gateway account bound to the plugin; callers can't override the account. The plugin declares `lark_attachments`, which the hub merges into hello/health features.
`client_id` must be a UUID and stay the same across retries of the same message; message reads also preserve optional `client_id`, `local_state`, used to remove late echoes after send timeouts. `local:` and pending/failed copies don't count as send confirmation.

Media rewrite rules: throughout parts JSON, `"/api/media/` → `"/api/v1/lark/media/`, `"/api/messages/` → `"/api/v1/lark/messages/`
(including messages nested inside merged-forward cards).

`retained=true` means the gateway retained the recalled original content, not that permissions are restored; display still keeps `recalled`, and this must not enable replies, reactions or card writes. Neither display switch deletes server-retained data or restricts existing message-read permissions; when settings are off / unknown, clients hide recalled originals and edit-history entry points. OLK projections in history, quotes and forwards use current authorization; when locked, only public content is shown and decrypted bodies are cleared from the client cache.

## Personal Agent source status

The hub has no personal Agent sources of its own; all sources come from `agent_sources` of running extensions.
With no such extension running, `GET /api/v1/agents` returns `{"sources":[]}` and `GET /api/v1/agents/sessions` returns `{"sessions":[]}`, both HTTP 200.
With sources, `GET /api/v1/agents` has one entry per source: `{"sources":[{"source":"<contribution id>","enabled","error"?,"setup"?,"providers":[…],"accounts":[…]}]}`;
the Lark plugin picks its own source id; keeping the same id across upgrades keeps session ids unchanged.
`setup` explains why the source is reachable but has nothing to list yet; clients turn it into a notice when the session list is empty:
`missing` (the backend doesn't support personal Agents, such as a gateway without agent-bridge), `disabled` (supported but not enabled, such as agent-bridge being off on the gateway),
`no_accounts` (enabled but no accounts connected yet); these states mean the source has no sessions. Other failures (such as unreachable, or an extension still waiting for its own settings) go in `error`, from the last failed `agentsrc.sessions`, and clients show them when the session list is empty. When other sources list sessions, the web shows the same lines as a notice above the list. Without `source`, listing, paging, counting and searching skip a failing source when other sources exist or when it has not listed since it was registered, and answer 200; a lone source that has listed before returns its error, so clients keep the rows they have. With `source`, the source's error is returned.

## Personal Agent list preferences

`GET /api/v1/agents/prefs` / `PUT /api/v1/agents/prefs` (replaces the whole set), stored in the hub's settings table (key `agents.prefs`), used by the web:

```json
{"pins":["<sessionId>"],
 "view":{"group":"date|provider|none","sort":"updated|unread|name","show":"all|unread|sendable","providers":["grok_bot"]},
 "sections":[{"id":"s1","name":"Work"}],
 "assign":{"<sessionId>":"s1"},
 "hidden":{"<sessionId>":1762500000000},
 "updatedAt":"…"}
```

- Omitted fields = defaults (group by date, sort by latest update, show all, all sources). `pins` is ordered and deduplicated; `assign` entries pointing to missing sections are dropped.
- `hidden` is what the user removed from the list (session id → when, ms). It changes only through `POST …/hide` / `…/unhide` below: a PUT keeps the stored set whatever it carries, so saving pins cannot bring removed conversations back.

### Removing a personal Agent from the list

The conversation belongs to its source (the Lark gateway through its extension), which can't delete or archive one, and the hub pulls the list from it again every minute. So removing is Persona's own: the extension manager (`server/internal/agents/hidden.go`) keeps the id in `hidden`, and leaves it out of `GET /api/v1/agents/sessions` (whole list, pages and counts, its unread included) until the source reports a message after the removal (`rankTimeMs` past the stored time). Then it is back by itself, like a deleted Agent session that is used again.

| Request | Response | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/hide` | `{"ok":true,"hidden":true}`; a conversation no source lists 404 | full |
| `POST /api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/unhide` | `{"ok":true,"hidden":false}` | full |
| `GET /api/v1/agents/hidden` | `{"sessions":[Session]}`: the removed ones the sources still list and that got nothing new since | full |

Each write broadcasts `{"type":"agents"}` (the list) and `{"type":"agents.prefs"}`. Extension tokens can't use these routes. The web offers **Remove from list** in a personal Agent row's ⋯ and right-click menu (with Undo in the toast), and a folded **Removed (N)** section with **Restore** at the end of `/a`.

The web shows a prefs change at once and then PUTs it. When the PUT fails (other than a 404 / 405 from a hub without the route, where the change stays in localStorage only), it puts back the value from before unless a later change came, shows "Couldn't save the list settings: …", and reads `GET /agents/prefs` again once its PUTs are done, so a change the hub did not store never looks saved.
- Pinned sessions always appear in "Pinned" at the top, followed by custom sections, then groups from `view.group`.
- After a successful PUT, broadcasts `{"type":"agents.prefs"}`, and other clients GET again. When the hub lacks this endpoint (404), the web stores preferences only locally.

## Navigation

The page the web app opens on, the sidebar's arrangement and Overview's (its extension cards, and its own sections): `GET /api/v1/navigation` / `PUT /api/v1/navigation`, answered by the default manager
(`server/internal/assistant/navigation.go`, relayed by the hub like the other `assistantwire.Routes`) and kept in its
settings table under the key `navigation`, `{"start":"<page>"}`. A hub has one owner, so this is the user's choice and
every device of theirs follows it.

- `start` is `""` for the default, the main conversation, or a page's key as the web's sidebar names it (`web/src/lib/persona-nav.ts`
  `NAV_PAGES`: `home` for Overview, `inbox`, `messages`, `todos`, `routines`, `machines`,
  `terminal`, `settings`), or `p:<extension>/<page>` for an extension's `nav_page`. The
  manager checks only the shape (a lowercase word of at most 64 characters, or `p:` and two parts of at most 128 characters
  without spaces or `/`): which pages there are is the web app's business, and it opens on the default for a key it does not
  know or a page that is not there now, keeping the choice.
- `start` is left out of the answer until a PUT stores one; `""` once the default was chosen. The web PUTs the choice it kept
  when the answer has none.
- `pages` is the sidebar's arrangement, as the web keeps it (`web/src/lib/sidebar-pages.ts`):
  `{"order": [<page>], "shown": [<page>], "hidden": [<page>], "groups"?: [{"id", "title"?}], "assign"?: {<page>: <group id>}, "removed"?: [<group id>]}`.
  `order` is the user's order; `shown` / `hidden` the pages switched into the sidebar or put under More; `groups` the groups in
  their order, where `""` is the built-in **Pages**, `u:<id>` a group the user made (a title is required) and any other id an
  extension's `nav_page` group (a title renames it); `assign` the group a page was moved
  to; `removed` the extensions' groups the user removed. The manager checks only the shape (at most 256 keys a list and 256 moves,
  32 groups, titles of at most 40 characters, ids once). Like `start`, it is left out until stored.
- `overview` is how the user arranged Overview's extension cards (`overview_card`),
  as the web keeps it (`web/src/lib/overview-cards.ts`): `[{"extension", "id", "hidden"?: true, "span"?: "half" | "full"}]`, the cards in
  the user's order, each named by its extension's id and its card's, hidden or not, and half a row (the default) or the whole row.
  Which cards there are is the web app's business: a card the list does not name (an extension installed later) comes after the
  named ones, half a row and shown, in the hub's order (by extension, then the manifest's); an entry naming a card that is not
  there now is passed over and kept until the user saves another arrangement, which names only the cards there are then.
  Overview's own sections are entries of the same list, `{"section", "hidden"?: true}`, among the cards in the user's
  order: `needs_you`, `waiting_on_computer` (Stuck), `in_progress` (Tasks in progress), `working`, `unread` and `computers`, above
  the cards in that order by default (the cards last). A section has no card's fields, so it can never be taken for a card, nor a card for it.
  Needs you and Stuck are never hidden, only moved: their rows need the user (`docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` 3.4), and the web
  draws them whatever the list says. A section the list does not name (one added later) comes right after the one before it by
  default (Needs you: first), so a section the user put first stays first; a card it does not name, when it names none, at
  the end, where the cards are by default. One naming a section the web app does not have is passed over and kept where it is
  when the arrangement changes. The web writes the sections only once one is moved or hidden, and from then all of
  them until Reset.
  The manager checks only the shape (at most 256 cards and sections, ids of the shape an extension's and a UI contribution's
  have, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`, a section's `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, each card and section once, `span` of `half` or
  `full`, and only on a card). `[]` is the default chosen (Reset), kept as such, sections included. A PUT whose list names
  cards and no section while the stored one names sections keeps the sections where they are and gives the cards the stored cards' places in the new order (one it did not
  have after the last of them; none: at the end, where the cards are by default), and the manager stores and pushes that. Like the others, it is left out until stored.
- PUT `{start?, pages?, overview?}` (at least one) changes only the fields it carries and pushes only those, so a client with an unsent
  change of another field keeps it. It requires `full` (an `answer` credential gets 403; extension tokens never reach it,
  `extwire.RouteScopes` does not list it); and broadcasts `{"type":"navigation","start"?:"<page>","pages"?:{…},"overview"?:[…]}`.
- When the route answers 404 the web keeps the choice in the browser only and says so in the setting.

## Tags in messages (parsed by clients)

| Tag | Written by | Meaning / display |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<attached_images>` one path per line `</attached_images>` | node (images sent from the web app) | images attached to the message; square thumbnails above the bubble. Only lines starting with `/` or `~` are photos. For Claude Code the node adds a `path:<path>` line after each path (Claude Code turns a line that is only an image path into `[Image #n]` and drops it, so its transcript keeps only the `path:` lines; readers take both `path:<path>` and `path: <path>`); `path:` lines are for the agent and never shown |
| `<persona-context kind="context\|edit\|doc\|instructions" title="…" url="…">text</persona-context>` | web (text selected in a link card), hub (Lark /agent instructions and context) | not written by the user: all blocks gather into one "Context · N items" row beside the bubble (with one block, "Context · title"), collapsed by default; expanding shows a title list, each opening the body and link. Attributes may be in any order or omitted (`url` is often absent); attributes a reader has no field for are kept and never drawn, so a block can carry ids for the model (the subscription pages' Set Up with the assistant); only text outside the tags is user-written |
| `<persona-context kind="workspace" title="…" url="" machine="<machine id>" cwd="<folder>" branch="…">` | web (a workspace picked in the assistant's @ menu) | shown like the other blocks. Before the assistant gets it, the manager replaces the block (same tag, `branch` dropped) with where to dispatch by default and recent Agents in that folder; a block naming an unknown computer is passed on as written |
| `<persona-context kind="context" title="…" url="persona://session/<machine id>/<session id>">` | web (another session picked in the @ menu) | shown like the other blocks. Before an Agent (not an assistant conversation or a guest) gets it among the leading blocks, its node ends the block's body with the session's address and how to read it with `a2a_read` or message it with `a2a_send`, naming the node's executable for a harness without the Persona MCP tools; a block that already ends with that note is passed on as written |
| `<persona-context kind="skill" title="…" url="" ref="<opaque id>">source and description</persona-context>` | Web Assistant and Agents composer | an explicit selection, only recognized among leading context blocks; never inferred from `@name`, email, file paths or quoted/later prose. The current manager and node resolve `ref` against the target environment's catalog, never a client path or display name. Draft/queue/outbox/history keep this text. Node-generated `kind="skill-instructions"` carries Claude's exact-file reading adapter and is hidden by Web transcript/queue readers, not restored as a user selection. |
| `<persona-context kind="forward" title="…" url="persona://session/…?at=…" msg="…" role="…" author="…" chat="…" project="…" machine="…" time="…">` | web (Forward on a message; several at once) | the user forwarded a message (or several, one block each) from another chat: a card at the top of the user's bubble that opens the original; see "Forwarded messages" below |
| `<cross-session-message from-name="…">…</cross-session-message>` | Claude Code (cross-session messages) | a left-side "From name" card, body rendered as Markdown |

The web composer keeps a typed @ selection visible in the sentence and still sends its original leading context tag.
The tag carries `inline_label` and `inline_start`. The latter is a zero-based UTF-16 offset into the trimmed message body.
The web hides the separate context card when that range still matches its label. Agents read the original structured
reference, including the existing A2A session address. Contexts attached directly keep their cards.

### Quote and comment blocks at the start of messages

Web "Quote" and "Comment" use no tags or structured fields: on send they become `> ` blocks at the start of the message (`withQuoteBlock` in `web/src/lib/drafts.ts`, `web/src/lib/comments.ts`); the assistant and Agents on computers read them as text, and any other reader simply sees `>` lines.
At most one quote block starts a message (the quoted words; for a task card, the first line is `任务「标题」（todo id: …）`, meaning `Task “title” (todo id: …)`), followed by any number of comment blocks, separated by blank lines, and finally the user's typed text:

```text
> Quoted words                  ← quote block (optional)

> Comment 1                     ← comment on selected text: number, original text (nested in another `> `), blank line, comment
> Selected text:
> > The selected lines
>
> State the source clearly here

> Code comment 2                ← code comment: number, location, optional Side / Diff / Truncated, fenced code, comment
> File: src/app.ts:12-14        ← path relative to the session directory (original path if outside it); line numbers are from the new file, with `Side: old` when only deleted lines are selected
> Diff: staged                  ← absent for comments on files; staged | unstaged | commit <first 8 chars>; a session review's: uncommitted | branch since <base> | since <base> (Git's short hash); code lines carry `+`, `-`, space, and the fence uses `diff`
> Truncated: the first 60 of 80 lines
> ```ts
> const a = 1;
> ```
>
> Why not use a constant?

> Element comment 3             ← an element picked in a dev server preview: number, page, selector, optional Component (with its source) or Source, Text, Truncated, the element's HTML, comment
> Page: http://localhost:5173/settings
> Element: main > form > button.save
> Component: SaveButton (src/settings/SaveButton.tsx:14)
> Text: Save changes
> ```html
> <button class="save">Save changes</button>
> ```
>
> Make it the primary color

The user's typed text
```

Limits: comments up to 4000 characters, attached code up to 60 lines (extra lines are counted in `Truncated` but not included); the fence has one more backtick than the longest run in the code. Numbers follow the order of comments above the input, starting at 1.
On reading back, web only recognizes blocks after the first block whose first line is `Comment N` / `Code comment N` / `Element comment N` (`splitQuotes`), so ordinary `> ` quotes are unaffected; editing a sent message puts comments back above the input. The web code is checked against `spec/fixtures/comments`.

### Message source

`Item.source` is optional authorship metadata, independent of the runtime's `role`. New automated input keeps the model's existing user role and the legacy `injected` / `from` fields. Clients must not render any nonempty source kind as a user bubble, count it in user-only navigation or statistics, or match it to a user's pending send. Unknown kinds get a generic source label; they do not fall back to a user identity.

```json
{"kind":"conversation","conversation_id":"<sending conversation id>","title":"Research"}
```

| `source.kind` | Meaning | Optional fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conversation` | Input from `conversation_send` | `conversation_id` is the sending session's stable id; `title` is its title at send time |
| `patrol` | A repeating scheduled run, including daily routines and interval patrols | `title` is the scheduled task title; `conversation_id` is the originating conversation when recorded; `push: "asked"` marks a run whose normal completion stays quiet |
| `followup` | A one-shot scheduled follow-up, wake, or usage-limit continuation | `title` and originating `conversation_id` when recorded; `push: "asked"` as for `patrol` |
| `supervision` | A supervision dispatch | Existing `injected.level` and turn-folding behavior still apply |
| `scheduled_task` | An automatic input from an external scheduler, such as a Codex heartbeat | `text` is the visible task instructions, not the runtime envelope; no Persona `injected` follow-up or patrol is implied |

The manager persists explicit provenance in the native transcript with a leading context block, rendered by `shared/message_source.md`:

```text
<persona-context kind="message-source" title="">
{"kind":"conversation","conversation_id":"<sending conversation id>","title":"Research"}
</persona-context>
```

The original content follows the block. JSON is HTML-escaped when written so a title cannot close the block. This is metadata, not a selectable Context card: clients exclude `kind="message-source"` from Context groups. The block survives history reads, full-item reads, paging, subscription backlog and process restarts without depending on the 24-hour echo cache or a database migration. Queued relays retain their sender id/title in the existing persisted relay JSON; dispatch reconstructs the same source after restart. Scheduled runs receive a source whether they address an existing chat, reuse their own chat, or start a new one. A reference-only scheduled prompt also carries `schedule_run_id` in this metadata so the scheduler can identify the exact ended turn before retrying an empty response.

For compatibility, prefer explicit `source`, then persisted source context, then existing `injected`: `followup.daily|interval` maps to `patrol`, other followup states to `followup`, and `system.supervise` to `supervision`. `from` still names a native peer and is not converted into a conversation id. With no metadata, only the complete canonical relay context (`assistant/relay.md`, matching sender and reply ids, recognized relay tool and numeric hop limits) supplies a conversation id/title; an emoji, title, or ordinary user sentence never does. Existing generated task templates remain the narrow fallback for old transcripts. A message with `client_msg_id` is never text-inferred. User starts and web sends protect pasted source blocks or complete templates with an outer `message-source` block containing `{"author":"user"}`; this internal sentinel produces no source and prevents nested metadata or legacy recognition, even before the echo id arrives. Explicit source fields supplied by web input are removed.

### Forwarded messages

A message forwarded from one chat to another goes out as the user's own message in the target chat: a
`<persona-context kind="forward">` block that carries the original, then the note the user typed (with no note, a fixed
"Please look at the forwarded message above." in the sender's language). It is sent through
`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/messages` like any message, or as a new Agent's first message; there is no forward
endpoint, and nothing is written to the original chat. Only chats of the same hub are offered.

```text
<persona-context kind="forward" title="Forwarded from Claude · Network tests" url="persona://session/<machine id>/<session id>?at=<item id>" msg="<item id>" role="agent" author="Claude" chat="Network tests" project="weather › tests" machine="MacBook Pro" time="2026-11-11T10:24:00+08:00">
Retries live in `retry_policy.go`: 3 tries.
</persona-context>

Make the photo upload use the same retries
```

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | "Forwarded from {author} · {chat}" in the sender's language: what a reader that does not know `forward` shows, and the title the hub takes for a chat that starts with it |
| `url` | `persona://session/<machine id>/<session id>?at=<item id>`, the item id percent-encoded: the original, which clients open at that message |
| `msg` | The original item id |
| `role` | Whose message it was: `user` (the user's own), `persona`, `agent`, or `other` (a relayed or scheduled message, another session's Claude) |
| `author` | Who wrote it, by name; for the user's own, "Me" in the sender's language |
| `chat` | The original chat's title |
| `project` | The Agent's project (`space › tab`); absent for Persona's chats |
| `machine` | The computer's name (not its id); absent for Persona's chats |
| `time` | When the original was written, ISO 8601 with the sender's offset |

The attributes are written in this order after `kind`, `title`, `url` and `msg`; values escape `&`, `"`, `<` and `>`,
and readers keep attributes they do not know. The text is the original as the chat shows it: without message-source
metadata, photo notes or file tags; quote and forward blocks it opened with become `> ` lines led by their heading;
files sent with it are named, not copied; at most 20,000 characters, then a line saying it was cut. It goes through the
usual closing-tag removal. Photos the user sent with their own message go with the forward as the new message's images.

The web app draws the block as a card at the top of the user's bubble (the heading, the computer and time, the first lines
of the original) that opens the original chat at that message; a reader that does not know `forward` folds it like the
other context blocks ("Context · title"). The assistant's instructions say how to read it, and that `agent_read` and
`conversation_read` read the original chat from the ids in `url`. Shared cases: `spec/fixtures/forward`.

**Several at once.** Messages picked together go as one message with one block per message, in the original
chat's order (not the order they were picked), one per line, then a blank line and the note; with no note, "Please look
at the forwarded messages above.". Nothing new is written into a block. Each is cut at the smaller of 20,000 characters
and 60,000 divided by how many go (rounded down), and at most 30 go at once; the user's own photos go along up to the
box's limit, the earlier messages' first. Readers show forward blocks that sit next to each other and whose `url` names
the same session as one card: the chat, then each message with its author, time and first lines, each opening the
original at that message. Another session's forward or any other block starts a new card. Shared cases:
`spec/fixtures/forward/several.json`.

## Messages injected by Persona

The hub sends some model-facing messages into chats as "user input". In the transcript they have `role:"user", kind:"text"`, just like the user's typed words,
but aren't user-written: **the web app does not draw them as user bubbles or show the instructions for the model inside them**. The runtime role stays unchanged; generated content carries the source context above.
The hub preserves explicit provenance and recognizes legacy generated lines by template (`prompts.ParseInjected`, tested against rendering), adding `injected` to the item. Pagination (`/items`), pushes (`items` events and subscription backlog),
and `/items/{iid}/full` all carry the metadata. Messages without metadata keep the narrow template fallback. A line the web app sends with its own `client_msg_id` is never recognized as injected.

```jsonc
"injected": {
  "kind": "task_notice|followup|system",
  "state": "…",            // see the table below
  "title": "Remove the extension list from README", // task name / scheduled task title / what a wake-up is waiting for / the inbox item's title; may be empty
  "machine": "<computer name>",  // task_notice only: which computer the Agent is on (name; may be empty)
  "todo_id": "td_…",        // task_notice only: when the hub can identify the task (still open, unique title); may be empty, in which case the client looks for a task card in the same chat by title
  "line": "Task 'Remove the extension list from README' is done", // one human-readable sentence, displayed directly
  "detail": "…"             // followup once / daily / interval only: the task's own instructions (what the user wrote in the scheduled task), which can be shown collapsed; empty otherwise
}
```

| Source (template) | Start of text | `kind` | `state` | `line` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A quiet task dispatched from the main chat has a result (`assistant/task_notice.md`) | `🔔 任务「标题」做完了（电脑）` ("Task 'title' is done (computer)"), with `（这是 Persona 的任务通知，……` ("This is a Persona task notification, …") on the second or third line | `task_notice` | `done` / `needs` / `interrupted` / `failed` | Task "x" is done / waiting for you / interrupted / couldn't start |
| A scheduled task or follow-up is due (`assistant/task_run.md`) | `⏰ 标题（你之前安排的跟进）` / `（定时任务）` / `（定时任务，每 30 分钟）` ("title (a follow-up you scheduled)" / "(scheduled task)" / "(scheduled task, every 30 minutes)") | `followup` | `once` / `daily` / `interval` | Follow-up "x" is due / Scheduled task "x" starts running |
| Wake an Agent that is waiting (`agents/wake.md`, Agents chats) | Localized: `<persona-wake>{"title":"…"}</persona-wake>`; legacy Chinese: `⏰（Persona 叫醒你，第 N 次）` | `followup` | `wake` | Persona woke it: check whether "what it's waiting for" is ready |
| Continue an Agent once its subscription usage limit reset (`agents/limit_continue.md`, Agents chats; only the hub marks it) | `⏰（Persona 叫你接着做）订阅的用量额度已经重置了` ("Persona asks you to go on: the subscription's usage limit has reset") | `followup` | `limit_continue` | Usage limit reset: Persona told it to go on |
| An Assistant conversation is asked to give a missing reply (`assistant/answer_again.md`) | `<persona-answer-again />` | `system` | `answer_again` | Persona is asking for a reply again |
| A node restart lost background tasks (`assistant/lost_tasks.md`) | `⚠️ 运行你的 node 刚重启过` ("The node running you just restarted") | `system` | `lost_tasks` | The node restarted; N background tasks stopped |
| A supervision message in the main chat (`assistant/supervise.md`) | `📋 督办：你派出去的任务有 N 个要你处理` ("Supervision: N tasks you dispatched need your attention"), with `这是 Persona 的督办消息` ("This is a Persona supervision message") on the second line | `system` | `supervise` | Supervision: N dispatched tasks need attention |
| News of an inbox item for a chat it was handed to (`inbox/handoff_note.md`) | `📥 收件箱事件「标题」有了下文` ("Inbox item 'title' has news"), with `这是 Persona 的收件箱通知` ("This is a Persona inbox notice") on the second line | `system` | `inbox` | Inbox: an update on "title" |
| How a question a conversation asked without waiting ended (`assistant/ask_later.md`) | `🔔 你 <time> 用 ask_user 问过用户（wait: false，当时没有等回答）：` ("You asked the user with ask_user at <time>, without waiting"), ending with `（这是 Persona 的通知，不是用户在这里发的消息。）` ("This is a Persona notice, not a message the user sent here") | `system` | `ask_answered` / `ask_expired` / `ask_closed` | You answered: "answers" (`title`: the answers, joined with " · " and clipped to 60 characters) / The question timed out unanswered / The question was closed without an answer |

**Display**:

- Draw a lightweight centered system notice: icon + `line`, not a right-side user bubble, without exposing the original text. Clicking `task_notice` opens the task (`todo_id`, otherwise find a task card / to-do in this chat by `title`; untappable if neither is found);
  once / daily / interval `followup` can be opened to read `detail`; the rest aren't tappable.
- If a card for the same task (receipt, task card) is already above it in the main chat, this line can merge into the card instead of being drawn separately; never repeat the Agent's last words (already on the card).
- Doesn't count as user-sent: isn't treated as a turn start when matching pending bubbles (`client_msg_id` / text matching), and isn't counted in "what you said" statistics. Chat list previews, search results and copying "the user's words" use `line`, not the original text.
- A task notification still queued for sending already uses only `任务「x」的通知` ("Notification for task 'x'") in the `queued` field of `sessions`.

**Supervision turns**: `injected.state = supervise` additionally carries `level: info|triage|user`, read from the exact `<persona-supervision level="…" />` line in the generated message. A missing level means triage. Info is progress-only and does not dispatch a main-chat turn. Web defaults an entire triage turn to one muted, expandable record; original input, tool trace and replies remain inspectable in that record. User-level turns remain visible. A successful `supervision_finish` result with `visibility:user`, `notify_user`, `ask_user`, or user-facing `task_review` promotes the whole turn; failed calls do not. A pending ask_user remains visible while waiting for the user's answer. `fold.supervision_user:true` carries successful promotion across server-side work folding. Drawing the input as a system line alone does not hide its reply.

**Localized wakes**: the marker is one leading line containing canonical JSON (only `title`, the waiting
subject, with HTML characters/newlines escaped). It is followed by the localized prompt body. The hub recognizes
it after snapshot/source blocks and supplies `followup` / `wake` metadata; malformed markers are not inferred.
The model text is preserved and `injected.line` uses the viewer's language. Web-originated messages and protected
user-authorship blocks never acquire automated provenance from a pasted marker.

**When the hub sends no `injected`**, the web app recognizes by text (only lines with `role:"user", kind:"text"` and no `client_msg_id`; strip leading whitespace and `<persona-context>` snapshot blocks first):

- `task_notice`: the first line matches `^🔔 任务「(.+)」(做完了|在等用户|被模型服务出错打断了|没开起来)(?:（(.+)）)?$` (task title, done / waiting for the user / interrupted by a model service error / couldn't start, optional computer), and the full text contains `这是 Persona 的任务通知` ("This is a Persona task notification").
  Group 2 maps to `done` / `needs` / `interrupted` / `failed`; group 3 is `machine`.
- `followup`: the first line matches `^⏰ (.+)（(你之前安排的跟进|定时任务(?:，每 [^）]+)?)）$`: `你之前安排的跟进` ("a follow-up you scheduled") is `once`, `定时任务，每 …` ("scheduled task, every …") is `interval`, `定时任务` ("scheduled task") is `daily`;
  `detail` is the body after the first blank line (remove the trailing instruction paragraph starting with `（知识库`, "(knowledge base"). A first line starting with `⏰（Persona 叫醒你，第` ("Persona wakes you, attempt") is `wake`; `title` is the text inside `在等「…」` ("waiting for '…'").
- `system`: starts with `⚠️ 运行你的 node 刚重启过` ("The node running you just restarted"); the count of lines starting with `- ` is the number of stopped tasks. Supervision messages and inbox notices always carry `injected`; how a question asked without waiting ended (`ask_later`) is marked by the hub on every item it sends. None of these are in the shared fixtures, and the web app does not recognize them itself.
- Anything unrecognized stays a user bubble (better to miss recognition than hide the user's words).
- Shared fixtures: `spec/fixtures/injected/cases.json` (Go test `TestParseInjected` generates them from templates; `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites them): `input.text` → `expected` (`null` means not recognized); the web app runs its fallback recognition against these fixtures.

Other "not user-written" messages retain their own shapes: inter-chat input carries `source.kind="conversation"` as above; background for resuming the old main chat (`<persona-context title="接上旧主对话">`, "Resume the old main chat")
is gathered as "Context" by the tags above; background-task notifications use `kind:"notice"` + `task`; `/model`, compaction and similar notices use `kind:"notice"`.



### Workspace catalog lineage

Each `workspaces.list` / `GET /api/v1/workspaces` workspace may carry `parent_source_id` and `index` (host order).
