A parent identity is `(machine_id, source, parent_source_id)`, never the globally qualified workspace `id` or its directory. Optional `project_id`, `project_name`, `project_path` and `is_main` describe the host project separately: multiple root workspaces share one project ID, while a cross-project child still follows its explicit workspace parent. Project IDs are scoped to machine and source, and names are labels. Optional `head`, `unread`, `sidebar_status` and `workspace_kind` preserve host-owned sidebar presentation; they are not inferred Agent capabilities. Optional `pinned_at` is the host's native workspace pin timestamp (RFC3339; missing means unpinned/unsupported), keyed by the exact machine/source/workspace identity. The Agents workspace tree orders pinned workspaces and their repository ancestors first, newest native pin first, without changing Persona's independent session/project pins. Optional `owned` (an engine runtime's rows only) marks a worktree the runtime made and removes with its workspace: the web offers Delete worktree on a Paseo row only with it. The node preserves the host's user-visible title in `title` without changing session names or pin identities. Missing fields are tolerated. Workspace containers are independent of Agent sessions, including empty parents and multiple distinct workspaces in one directory.

`POST /machines/{mid}/worktree/prepare` advertises `choose_parent: true` when the host can select a sidebar parent independently of the Git source. Only then may the client send `parent_workspace_id` to `worktree/create`; `workspace_id` still names the repository/base checkout. Both IDs belong to that machine and host. Orca validates the selected parent before creating anything and returns `parent_workspace_id` with the result. Omission uses the source as parent; the web offers independent parent selection only when `choose_parent` is advertised. An explicit `workspace_id` in an Orca session start must still exist and contain `cwd`; a stale choice is refused instead of falling back to another workspace.

`POST /machines/{mid}/worktree/rename` is a full-device node action: `{workspace_id, name, kind?, locale?}` changes a listed worktree's display name through its host (its refusals in `locale`, which the hub fills in). It does not rename its branch, directory or Agents. The name is a trimmed single line of at most 80 characters. Orca uses `worktree.set` with only `displayName`; Paseo sets the workspace's title (runtime ↔ node `workspace.rename`); Agent tab names use `terminal.rename` instead. Missing or foreign targets are refused.


### Orca worktree composer and removal

Advanced worktree routes are full-device node adapters. The Hub validates named fields, applies authorization and forwards requests; creation retains the existing `X-Persona-Op-Id` receipt. It does not choose repositories, inspect Git, or decide removal safety.

Probe `POST /api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/prepare` with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",composer:true}`. Only a response containing `composer` enables advanced creation; old nodes may ignore the probe flag and return legacy metadata. Legacy explicit `{workspace_id,branch,path,kind?,parent_workspace_id?}` and generated `{workspace_id,auto_name:true,kind?,parent_workspace_id?}` creation retain their existing semantics. Never send an advanced mutation to a node that did not advertise it.

The advanced prepare response retains `root`, `repoName`, `branch`, `path`, `choose_parent` and `automatic_name`, and adds `composer:{project,base_ref,refs,presets,capabilities}`. Presets are `{id,name?,directories:string[]}`. Adapter capabilities are `create`, `source.github`, `sparse_presets`, `branch_override`, and optionally `folder_parent`. These names describe this adapter, not Orca runtime capability names. The adapter requires the runtime's `worktree.open-existing-branch.v2-request.v1`; folder parents additionally require `worktree.set.folder-parent.v1`, and `branch_override` requires `worktree.create.exact-name.v1`. Prepare reads actual repository metadata, refs and sparse presets; unsupported RPCs fail rather than fabricating choices. GitHub source queries can still fail independently because of provider configuration or authentication.

Advanced `worktree/create` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",composer:true,name?,branch_override?,base_ref?,parent_workspace_id?,no_parent?,note?,sparse_preset_id?,source_id?,source_url?,locale?}`. `auto_name:true` is accepted but unnecessary. Omitted name generates a name, with final naming and checkout placement owned by Orca. Legacy `branch` and `path` conflict with composer mode. The source workspace chooses the repository; the visual parent is independent and can belong to another local project. Omitted parent defaults to the source; `no_parent:true` conflicts with an explicit parent. The default Git base is the project's base, independently of the parent. Reusing a free local branch preserves its tip and sends `open-existing-v2` so a directory collision cannot select a different branch. A new explicit branch sends `create-exact`, refusing a collision rather than silently selecting a suffixed branch. A PR source cannot also reuse an existing branch. Results contain actual `{workspace_id,parent_workspace_id?,path,branch,tab_id?,pane?,terminal?}`; never reconstruct the returned path from a requested name.

`worktree/source` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",query?,locale?}` and returns `{items:[{type,number,title,url,branchName?,baseRefName?,isCrossRepository?}],errors?,warning?}`. This adapter exposes GitHub issues and PRs only. Creation uses `source_id:"issue:<number>"` or `"pr:<number>"` with the exact returned `source_url`; the node revalidates the selected item and resolves PR checkout/push refs through Orca. `worktree/preset` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",name,directories,locale?}`, with directories as newline-separated repository-relative paths, and returns the runtime's `{preset:{id,name?,directories}}`.

An unchanged creation intent retains one receipt UUID, body, connection owner and target across retries and dialog reopening. An unknown or pending receipt never authorizes a new create ID. Inspect `/api/v1/ops/{id}` or replay the exact original request with its original ID. The Hub preserves unknown outcomes and does not repeat the node call. Workspace creation and optional Agent launch are separate stages.

`POST /api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/delete` previews with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview:true,locale?}` and returns `{workspace_id,kind,host_id:"local",instance_id,path,branch,dirty,folder,preview_token}`. Confirm with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview_token,force?:true,delete_branch?:true,locale?}`. A token binds the exact node, local runtime instance, repository, branch, path, workspace kind, parent, checkout and Git-directory filesystem identity, HEAD and reviewed dirty content. Confirmation expires after ten minutes. Main or unknown-main workspaces, Git main checkouts, parents with children, ambiguous/missing/nonlocal identities and incomplete catalogs are refused. Confirmation re-resolves the target and rereads dirty state; changed content requires another preview even when `force` is true. Branches are kept unless explicitly requested otherwise. Raw `force` never waives archive-hook failure or unverified terminal-stop safety.

For `kind:"herdr"`, the same preview-confirm-reconcile route accepts `close_only:true` for workspace closure.
The preview returns `kind:"herdr"`, `host_id:"local"`, an empty `instance_id`, and `close_only:true` with `folder:true`.
Every confirmation and reconciliation repeats the same `close_only` flag. Closing keeps the checkout, files and
branches and accepts main checkouts and missing directories. A close token cannot authorize checkout deletion.
Omitting `close_only` removes a verified linked checkout through native `worktree.remove`. Its preview binds the
native workspace, socket instance, pane membership, checkout/Git-directory identity, branch, HEAD and reviewed dirty
contents. `force:true` acknowledges the previewed uncommitted files. `delete_branch:true` requests safe merged-branch
cleanup after observed checkout removal. The native catalog and checkout disappearance establish completion.
A dispatched token supports read-only reconciliation and retains the ten-minute confirmation and 24-hour reconciliation
windows. The web checks `worktree/status` before offering herdr checkout deletion. Closing remains available for a main
checkout.

Removal requires runtime `worktree.remove-branch-policy.v1` and `worktree.archive-failure-blocking.v1`; folder unregister also requires `folder-workspace.unique-id-mutation.v1`. Folder workspace keys use `folderWorkspace.delete` with `requireUniqueId:true`; folder-project children use host-qualified `worktree.rm`. Neither recursively deletes the user's folder. Git removal sends `runHooks:true`, `waitForBackgroundRemoval:true` and explicit branch policy without hook/PTY waivers.

Deletion returns `{workspace_id,removed,state,branch_deleted?}`. Only `removed:true,state:"removed"` is completion: the runtime result must agree with catalog absence and checkout disappearance (folder unregister checks catalog absence). Background acceptance returns `removing`; transport uncertainty returns `unknown`; reconciliation may return `present`. Use `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview_token,reconcile:true}` on the same route for read-only reconciliation; it never repeats removal. A dispatched token is consumed for mutation and retained for reconciliation for up to 24 hours. Node restart invalidates tokens; refresh the authoritative inventory and review the outcome before a fresh deletion attempt. Runtime refusals, including archive failures, remain errors. Orca does not currently accept an expected workspace instance or dirty fingerprint in `worktree.rm`, so checks protect stale confirmations but do not form an atomic transaction with concurrent external filesystem/runtime changes.

The advanced adapter supports only workspaces owned by the local Orca execution host. SSH, paired runtimes and cross-store parents are unavailable here. Runtime versions alone never imply support. All adapter error text has en, zh-Hans and ja resources under `worktree-composer`.

For `kind:"paseo"` the same preview-confirm-reconcile route deletes a worktree Paseo made (`owned` in its
`runtime.workspaces` row): a main checkout, a folder and a worktree Paseo did not make are refused at the preview, and
so is `close_only`; so is a row whose folder is gone, one git does not know as a worktree (its record in the repository
pruned) and a folder inside a worktree, each with its own reason. Neither the preview nor the confirmation goes on while
work could be lost: a session in the workspace starting, working, waiting for the user or in a state Paseo does not say,
or an Agent of any engine running in the folder (a herdr one that went there); idle, done and stopped sessions are what
the archive ends, as the preview showed. The preview returns `kind:"paseo"`, `host_id:"local"`, the bridge's instance
as `instance_id`, `folder:false`, and binds the runtime process, the workspace's identity (its id, folder, kind, `owned`
and repository: a new title or project name is the same workspace), its sessions (the archive ends them), the checkout
and Git-directory identity, branch, HEAD and reviewed dirty contents. One deadline, 145 s, covers the confirmation's
checks and Paseo's archive; past it the outcome is `unknown` and reconciliation tells. Confirmation has Paseo archive the
workspace (runtime ↔ node `workspace.archive`); Paseo removes the folder whatever is in it, so `force:true` is still
required for previewed changes. Completion is the workspace gone from the runtime's list and its folder gone; a
workspace archived with its folder left is `unknown`. `delete_branch:true` uses Git's safe branch deletion after
that; the branch is kept otherwise. Reconciliation reads the list and the disk, Paseo connected or not.

### Codex speed settings

Session rows may include `service_tier` (acknowledged native value, omitted while unknown) and
`service_tiers: [{id, name, description?}]` (native model choices plus `default` for Standard).
A standalone `service_tier` request to the session modes endpoint calls `session.speed {session_id, service_tier}`.
Only writable Codex app-server threads with advertised tiers support this request. Native errors are returned, and
a node without the capability returns `node_outdated`. Speed changes apply to subsequent turns independently of reasoning effort.

For a new Persona conversation, the launcher model list also carries each model's native `serviceTiers` as
`service_tiers`. While the default manager names `assistant_start_service_tier` in `manager.hello`, the hub lists that
feature and the web can send an advertised `service_tier` with `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations`; choosing another
manager disarms the pre-start draft. The node applies the tier through the same acknowledged `thread/settings/update`
after opening or adopting the thread and before its first `turn/start`; effort remains independent. Omission sends no
settings update and preserves the native default. A manager without the feature
gets 501 `assistant_service_tier_manager_outdated` before relaying an explicit one, and a node without
`assistant_service_tier` refuses a nonempty value with 409 `node_outdated` instead of silently starting Standard.
Resumed sends and non-Codex starts return coded 409 refusals; a native refusal returns
`assistant_service_tier_refused`, stops the unused new process and persists no conversation before the first turn.
New Agent starts do not take a speed setting.


## Agent directory visibility

Agent folder rules are the parallel list to blocked Claude config directories
("Blocking configuration directories"): both are per computer, kept in
the devices layer's settings beside each other (`claude_dirs_blocked/<machine id>`, `agent_dirs_hidden/<machine id>`), and use one pattern syntax and matcher
(`proto.DirPatternMatchedBy`). They differ in what they do:

| | Blocked Claude config directories | Agent folder rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matches | a Claude Code `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | a session's working directory (`cwd`), any runtime |
| Effect | the node does not scan it; its sessions are never collected | `action: "block"`: the node does not collect the sessions (below); `"hide"`: sessions stay collected and recorded, the manager leaves them out of Agents and the assistant's view |
| Switch | delete the rule | each rule has `enabled`; off keeps the rule and does nothing |
| HTTP | `GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/claude-dirs`, `PUT …/claude-dirs/blocked {"blocked": [...]}` | `GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/agent-dirs/hidden`, `PUT …/agent-dirs/hidden {"rules": [...]}` |
| `persona_settings` | `agents.blocked_claude_dirs` get / add / remove | `agents.hidden_dirs` get / add / remove |

`GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/agent-dirs/hidden` returns `{rules: [{pattern, enabled, action}], home?}` (`home` is the
computer's home for showing `~`, absent before its node first said). `PUT` replaces the computer's whole list and
returns the new state; only full access may call it. Offline computers can be set up. A rule is a path or
`filepath.Match` glob starting with `/` or `~/` (`~` is that computer's home, never the manager's; until it is
known a `~/` rule does not match), or a folder name glob starting with `*` (`*botfarm*`) that matches a folder of
that name anywhere in the path. A rule matches the folder and everything under it. Trailing slashes are dropped;
patterns that would cover home or the root, or that every folder matches (`*`, `/*`), invalid globs, duplicates, an
`action` other than `block` or `hide`, and more than 100 rules are refused (400). A rule without an `action` is stored and answered as `hide`, except that a `PUT` without `action` leaves an existing rule's action
as it is (so switching one rule does not turn blocks into hides); the web app and `persona_settings` make a new rule `block` unless Hide
is chosen. Matching is lexical and case-sensitive; a home reached through a link (`/home/me -> /data/home/me`,
`NodeInfo.home_real`) matches under either name, and the node also matches a working folder with its links
followed. Empty is the default.

**Block**. The manager sends the computer's enabled block patterns in `node.configure`
(`agent_dirs_blocked: [...]`, `[]` when none block) when its node connects and again whenever they change, then lists
again; when it cannot read the rules (before its first successful read), it sends `null`, which leaves the node's list
as it is rather than unblocking every folder.
A node that announces `agent_dirs_blocked` keeps them (also across restarts, `~/.persona/agent-dirs-blocked.json`)
and, for a session working there, with any runtime: leaves it out of every session list (`sessions.history`
included), so no row, count or
revision reaches the hub; pushes no `hook.event`, `session.items` or `session.delta` of it (a read the hub asks
for by session id, such as one of a chat opened before the block, is still answered); gives a Claude Code hook
no decision at once (Claude Code asks in its terminal); dismisses a runtime package's `interaction.create` at once
(handed back to the computer); leaves its Codex cards out of `codex.interactions` and creates no card for a shared
app-server's approval (Codex's own client decides); answers `personad ask` unavailable and drops `personad notify`;
and drops what standby kept of it instead of replaying it. The assistant's own conversations and the sessions the hub
keeps (`keep_sessions`) are never blocked, at rest as well as running. The manager still treats every enabled rule as hiding, so a node that does not announce `agent_dirs_blocked` and lists those sessions only gets them hidden.

`persona_settings` `agents.hidden_dirs` takes the same values as `agents.blocked_claude_dirs`: `add`
`{"machine", "pattern", "action"?, "enabled"?}` (`action` `block`, the default for a new rule, or `hide`; an existing
rule keeps its action unless one is given; `enabled` default on, on an existing rule it switches it), `remove`
`"<machine id>:<pattern>"`, and `get` lists each computer's rules with their action and how many of its listed
sessions each matches now (a block rule's are 0 once that node keeps them out). Every
change waits for the user's approval and is applied to the rules as they are then, so a change made
meanwhile is kept; the opposite switch or `remove` undoes it.

The Assistant manager annotates session rows with `hidden_by_directory: true` (otherwise omitted).
Bounded lists, counts, catalog and ranked search exclude those rows by default. Full inventories
retain annotated rows; the web app filters them before grouping and attention
counts. Exact user session access remains available. Temporary inspection uses `include_hidden=1` and does
not expose the rows to Assistant: `agents_list`, live snapshots, ambient triage, completion notifications,
needs-you cards and reminders exclude them. Hidden children do not affect visible parents' folded counts.
This is a visibility preference, not access control or transcript deletion.

Pending interactions have a separate authoritative inventory. `fleet.interactions` on reconnect always carries
all pending cards, including directory-hidden sessions: an omitted card means resolved to the hub. Assistant,
Feishu and attention summaries use a visibility projection instead. A blocked session's cards never reach this
inventory on a node that blocks. Saving any Agent folder rule change (the devices
tell the assistant, `devices.Options.HiddenAgentDirsChanged`) publishes the computer's updated session rows, then
replays pending `fleet.interaction` cards to connected clients. Replays preserve
delegation state and do not send notifications; a pending card stays actionable after revealing its session.


**Supervision boundary:** a session attached to an open task with an active supervisor stays visible even if
its directory matches. Its supervision and existing notification policy (including main-task quiet mode)
continue. This covers `task_plan`, supervised `agent_start` and adopted supervised agents; having once been
started by Persona is not enough. Once the task closes or the session is released, the ordinary directory
rule applies again. Assistant conversations themselves are exempt so their approval cards remain usable.
The first visibility check loads persisted task ownership before classifying a session. If supervision state
cannot be read, matching sessions remain visible until it can be read again.

Web: Settings › Agents starts with Hidden Agent folders (a computer picker, then that computer's rules), above the
per-runtime sections where Claude Code's blocked config directories are; Agents offers temporary inspection.
New labels and confirmation text ship in English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.

## Decisions raised outside a supervisor

`POST /api/v1/decisions` accepts this bounded JSON document (64 KiB at the HTTP boundary):

```json
{
  "ref": "nightly-2026-11-20",
  "todo_id": "todo_optional_parent",
  "title": "Publish the nightly build?",
  "background": "Checks passed; the release notes are ready.",
  "why_owner": "priority",
  "options": [
    {"label": "Publish", "leads_to": "Users receive the build"},
    {"label": "Hold", "leads_to": "No build goes out"}
  ],
  "recommend": "Hold",
  "cost_of_waiting": "The next nightly is delayed.",
  "reversible": true,
  "allow_default": false
}
```

`title`, `background`, `why_owner`, `recommend`, `cost_of_waiting` and `reversible` are required; `options` has 2–4 non-empty `{label, leads_to}` entries whose labels stay distinct after removing whitespace and punctuation, and the recommendation names one of them. `why_owner` is `irreversible`, `visible_to_others`, `priority`, `acceptance` or `only_owner_knows`. The recommended option is returned first. `todo_id` is optional and names an existing open to-do; omitting it creates a standalone decision. `ref` is an optional caller-stable idempotency key, at most 200 characters without `#`. Repeating the same normalized request with the same caller and ref returns the original decision with `inserted:false`; reusing that ref for different content is 409 `decision_ref_conflict`.

The reply is `{"decision": OutsideDecision, "inserted": bool}`. The decision contains `id`, optional `todo_id`, `ask_todo_id` (the separate backing to-do the existing Needs-you cards answer), `state`, authenticated `source: {kind, name}`, every rich request field, `default`, optional `deadline`, `created_at`, optional `withdrawn_at` and optional `answer`. `state` is `pending`, `answered` or `withdrawn`; `default` is `taken` or `never`. An answer has at most one of `option`, `response` or `text`, plus `answered_by` (`owner` or `default`) and `answered_at`. `response` is one of the three fixed answers `decide_yourself`, `not_what_i_asked` or `explain_first`; the last leaves state pending and suppresses the default.

Omitted `allow_default` preserves the reversible 24-hour recommendation default; explicit `false` disables it. Irreversible and visible-to-others decisions never default. This field does not change the action's `reversible` fact or its one-tap risk. A source is server-derived: `extension` with the authenticated extension id for HTTP, `script` with the node-derived session or working-directory name for a local script, or `app` for a full credential. Caller text cannot assert a source. Terminal control sequences are stripped before display.

An extension needs the explicit `decisions.raise` scope on all three routes. `todos.read`, `todos.write` and legacy every-scope tokens do not include it, and it grants no owner answer route. A full credential may use the routes; read-only roles cannot. Cross-caller polling and withdrawal are deliberately indistinguishable from an unknown id (404 `decision_not_found`). Other failures are 400 `invalid_decision`, 404 `todo_not_found`, 409 `todo_closed`, 409 `decision_closed`, and 503 `store_unavailable`. `POST /api/v1/decisions/{id}/withdraw` is idempotent while withdrawn; an answer after withdrawal is refused by the existing owner answer route. While a decision is pending, independently closing or deleting its backing to-do is 409 `outside_decision_pending`, so polling cannot be stranded without an answer; after an answer or withdrawal the row may be deleted without erasing the caller's durable history.

Local scripts use the same manager through node RPCs `decision.raise {decision, source}`, `decision.get {id}` and `decision.withdraw {id}`; The connected machine is the caller identity, so one computer cannot read or withdraw another computer's decisions. These are short requests, not resumable blocking interactions and not standby-spooled notifications. Answers never trigger an Agent, supervisor or model call. The manager owns validation, persistence, push/default handling, answering and withdrawal; the hub only authenticates and relays.

### Optional Todo repository metadata

The manager relays `GET /api/v1/todos/{id}/repositories` with `todos.read`, and
`PUT /api/v1/todos/{id}/repositories` plus
`PUT /api/v1/todos/{id}/repositories/{repo_id}/links` with `todos.write`.
Routing uses the Todo owner, including explicit-manager conflicts, just like
existing Todo detail routes. `POST /api/v1/todos` accepts optional atomic
`repository_bindings`; omitted fields preserve all legacy creation behavior.

A repository's `provider` may be `ext:<extension>/<contribution>`, a provider
extension's, with its name kept beside the identity as `provider_name`;
reads add `provider_state` and `link_kinds` to such rows only, and their stored
links open unchanged when the extension is gone.
A `source_snapshot.transport_origin` may also be `provider`: a row a new link
added clones from the address the provider answered. Right after a restart, a
save that needs a provider answers 409 `task_repositories_providers_starting`
(`repository_providers_starting` on the repository routes) when the extensions
are still starting at the end of its budget; it never reports the provider as
not installed.

### Delegated task instructions

Optional node capability `task_instructions_v1` adds `task_instructions` and `task_attachments` strings to `session.start`. The manager sends only stable framework rules in the former; assignment, caller-supplied `context`, criteria, project facts and effective decisions remain in `prompt`. The latter carries the already-authorized attachment suffix so a launcher fallback can append rules before it. Supported terminal launches use their instruction channel and retain it for resume; other launchers append the rules to the first message, with attachments last. Managers that cannot verify the capability keep the rules and attachments in `prompt`. The node adds no rules of its own on any platform. A computer whose owner wants standing rules for every Agent started there keeps them in `agent-rules.md` in the node's data directory; a new start (never a resume) carries that text after the caller's `task_instructions`, through the same channels.

Closeout blocks optionally carry `delivery: live|pr|merged|off|none` and `unblock: user|agent|other`. Their parsed values are additive fields of `work.closeout`; `missing` is the delivery gate and `waiting` its concrete dependency. A completed final report without an outstanding dependency may also carry one optional `next` line, up to 180 characters. It supplies the existing `suggestion` on the session and the owner can edit or send it. It never starts another turn on its own. Unknown enum values are ignored. A historical delivery line still wins, followed by explicit structured delivery, then the legacy merged/deployed/artifact inference. A to-do's `delivery.unblock` on the wire may also be `supervisor`: an owner hold on a supervised task that no review followed, its supervisor's until it opens a `needs_user` decision. Only `user` is the owner's; clients treat `supervisor`, like any value they do not know, as not waiting on the owner.

### Backend workspace naming metadata

| Node method | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace.naming.resolve` | `workspacenaming.Source` → `Preview {status, sample, plan?, diagnostics[]}`. The target supplies `NodeContext`; paths may be absent on disk. Version `workspace-naming/v1`. Local format validation only, with no resource creation, Git network access or Engine call. |

Legacy workspace resolution and `new/existing/none` do not call this method.
The Assistant view field `workspace_naming_version` advertises manager
support; an unavailable computer or unsupported method never falls back to an
Engine naming path.

## Backend task workspace RPC

The optional Node capability `task_workspace_v1` supports engine-independent preparation. Hub `device.call` retains machine ownership checks and additionally
binds the preparation plan's manager and machine to the authenticated route. It owns no preparation
state. Requests use `taskworkspace.Request`; results use `taskworkspace.Record`. All operation IDs
are stable and independent of transport IDs and engine workspace IDs.

| Node method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `task.workspace.capabilities` | Read-only probe → `{capability: "task_workspace_v1"}`. |
| `task.workspace.prepare` | Adopt or resume the exact saved naming plan and operation. Returns actual repository paths, private Git locations, frozen source commits, phases and structured errors. Every selected repository must be verified before ready. |
| `task.workspace.inspect` | Read-only physical observation. It does not fetch, reset, repair or adopt an unrelated directory. |
| `task.workspace.cancel` | Prevent the operation from preparing again; retain physical resources. |
| `task.workspace.cleanup` | Explicit worktree cleanup using `force?` and `delete_branch?`, both false by default. Returns removed flags and retained Git paths. |
| `task.workspace.acquire` | Register `use_id` against ready resources after physical inspection; prevent cleanup. |
| `task.workspace.release` | Release the exact `use_id` after use stops. |

The Manager checks the capability before adopting a preparation operation. Older Nodes return an
explicit unsupported result; legacy workspace creation remains available through its original paths.
A cancel or cleanup can reach the Node before prepare. Under the workspace and root locks, the
Node records a durable cancelled or removed receipt only when both the root and private storage
show that it owns no resources. A late prepare for that operation returns its recorded state.
Uncertain storage is retained. A missing receipt from an older Node leaves cancellation unconfirmed.
On Unix inherited subprocess locks allow reconciliation after Node death. On Windows an interrupted
in-flight command remains unknown until its execution can be established; it is never blindly replayed.

## Agents display settings

The default manager keeps the paired hub's `agents.show_botmux` and
`agents.use_herdr_tab_name` booleans in its
existing settings store, following the Agents triage route's ownership and role
checks. These are authenticated routes relayed by the hub; clients do not select
another manager for this shared preference.

| Method | Path | Response / request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/display-settings` | Defaults to `{show_botmux: true, configured: false, use_herdr_tab_name: false}`. `configured` reports whether `show_botmux` was saved. Authenticated answer-only devices may read. |
| PUT | `/api/v1/agents/display-settings` | Full access only (403 otherwise). Send one of `{show_botmux: boolean}` or `{use_herdr_tab_name: boolean}`. For `show_botmux`, optional `only_if_unset: true` uses an atomic insert without updating an existing key. Returns the current settings, including when another writer won. |

Invalid or missing booleans return 400; unavailable storage or failed reads/writes
return 503, never a default presented as a successful save. The conditional
migration and an explicit botmux update serialize at the unique settings key across
processes. Refresh on reconnect and the next Agents list refresh. For botmux,
Web paged lists use `exclude_pane_source=feishu`, complete
lists exclude botmux hosts before grouping/counting. Inventory and `seeBotmux`
to-do attribution are unchanged. The per-computer inventory switch is independent.

For an Agent with a named herdr or Herdr App tab, Web and Feishu use `slot_name`
as the primary name when `use_herdr_tab_name` is true. They also use it when
`title` is empty or is only a shell prompt such as `user@host:~/work`.
Inventory refreshes carry the current tab label. The unified Web Rename dialog
posts `tab_name` and, for a supported CLI, the same `title` to the existing
session rename route. Other managers read the same preference through the
hub's `app.call` method `agents.display.get`, which relays the default
manager's display settings.

Named assistant dispatches send `title` with `tab_name` in `session.start`.
The synchronous terminal reply uses the actual tab label when available,
including a suffix added for uniqueness. The manager persists the initial
Persona title for subsequent inventory reads.

With tab naming enabled, automatic naming calls the node's
`session.rename_tab_if_current` with `session_id`, `tab_id`,
`expected_tab_name` and `tab_name`. The node checks the live slot and its current
host label before changing it and replies with `{ok: true}` on success.

### Logical assistant conversation segments

Feature `assistant_segments` advertises an explicit manager-owned operation. A full-access client sends
`POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/switch` with `{source_machine_id, operation_id, expected_epoch,
machine_id, launcher, model?, effort?, permission_mode?}`. The target machine/launcher is explicit, including when
forcing another segment on the same engine. The response acknowledges durable `preparing`; it does not mean a model
turn ran. Reusing an operation ID requires the same request. Query
`GET /api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/switch/{operation}?machine_id=<public machine>` for
`{operation_id, phase, expected_epoch, error}`. Phases are `preparing`, `prepared`, `active`, `accepted`, `rejected`
and `in_doubt`. An unfinished operation serializes changes to that conversation. Ordinary model picks never initiate
this operation; they keep the existing cross-engine refusal.

`GET/PUT /api/v1/assistant/segments` reads/writes `{enabled}` (default true). Disabling new switches never disables
routing of existing segments. Queued inputs retain their original `client_msg_id`; a sending/in-doubt input fences
later input until reconciled. Definitive first-turn refusal restores the source at a higher epoch. The source is
closed only after first-turn acceptance. Full/image requests and scoped subscriptions always use public identity.

Logical seq values remain signed-int32-safe integers. Each later segment starts at the previous segment's offset plus
its frozen physical end. First-segment item IDs and history remain unchanged; later item IDs have a segment namespace.
Frozen-range backfill and retired-tail appends do not rewrite logical history. A real source-generation rewrite does.
Live spans, empty boundary bridges, history pages and reconnect backlog follow the same projection. The manager may
report `devices.state` machine `transport_for` to retain a bus identity after a source computer is removed; the hub
validates manager ownership and forwards only, without resolving segments.

The logical-segment client first reads
`GET /api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/segments?machine_id=...` to obtain the
current epoch and unfinished operation identity. The response exposes no physical
segment IDs and starts nothing. The explicitly confirmed switch sends its epoch
and a fresh operation ID to the switch POST. A transport retry must keep the exact
request, including the original epoch; it must not read a new epoch and silently
create a second operation. Registered runtime identity is part of a segment's
opaque engine identity, so two runtimes embedding the same engine are distinct
execution paths. Unknown engine kinds or identity suffixes are rejected.

### Cache keepalive fields

Assistant GET/PUT settings expose `cache_keepalive` (default true),
`cache_keepalive_minutes` (default 55, integer 1–55), and `cache_keepalive_max`
(default 24, integer 1–144). Partial updates preserve other fields. The web settings
control is shown only when GET reports the boolean. Claude launchers only;
Codex and other runtimes are not supported.

Manager-to-node `assistant.send` / `session.send` and node-to-manager `assistant.model`
carry optional `cache_keepalive: {enabled, interval_minutes, max_requests}` only for
the main conversation and registered lead ids. Missing policy denies warming.
The existing `follows_setting` flag is not sufficient authority.

| Method | Direction | Params / result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assistant.cache_clear` | manager → node | `{session_id}` → `{ok: true}`; cancel cache replay and erase its in-memory snapshot without stopping ordinary forwarding; used when archiving a conversation. Older nodes may reject it; the manager's fresh policy check also denies archived conversations. |
